Therefore, developing effective computational strategies to discover novel associations between LncRNA and disease is of great significance for further experimental verification. Traditional algorithms based on biological networks often have limitations of graph scale. Using machine learning techniques may avoid this issue. This paper proposes a machine learning-based approach, which utilizes Multilayer Perceptrons along with Feature Reduction to predict LncRNA and Disease Associations (MPFRLDA). First of all, a restart random walk algorithm is implemented to construct the topological similarity, which fully considers the topological characteristics of a network. Then, the sample features are extracted through matrix factorization and statistical measures, and their dimension is reduced via principal component analysis. Besides, the problem of the lack of negative samples for training is solved by randomly sampling from the unlabeled associations. Finally, the outputs of the multilayer perceptron constitute the distribution of expectations for the final rank of the associated pairs. Consequently, the model performance of MPFRLDA is superior to other classic algorithms, and the label randomization test indicates the proposed algorithm avoids overfitting. In addition, the candidate LncRNAs of colorectal and breast cancers predicted by MPFRLDA in case studies have been experimentally verified. Therefore, MPFRLDA appears to be an effective computing resource in biomedical research.

articleTitle: Multi-window Drift Detection Method Based on Integrating Outlier Identification and Input/Output Space Information with Its Application
abstract: In soft sensing application of actual industrial process, it is necessary to accurately identify samples that represent the working condition drift. Therefore, a multiwindow concept drift detection method is proposed in this paper, which integrates outlier identification and input/output space information. Firstly, a principal component analysis (PCA) model and a decision tree (DT) model are built by using historical data. Then, in the first window, the process data are standardized on the basis of 3σ criterion to remove outliers. In the second window, the T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and SPE of the new sample are calculated to determine whether it is a drift sample in the input space. In the third window, the prediction error of the new sample is calculated to determine whether it is a drift sample in the out space. Finally, we take the union of the concept drift samples detected in the input and output space to obtain the new updating sample set. At the same time, the PCA model and the decision tree model are updated after the number of the updating samples reach a pre-set threshold. The experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in the actual industrial datasets.

articleTitle: Scanpaths Prediction Based on Signals Competition
abstract: Human scanpath is an important reflection of the cognitive process in image observation and understanding. Accurately predicting scanpaths that match the physiological mechanism of the human eye under visual search tasks is helpful for designing a more natural human-computer interaction system. Aiming at the problem that current physiologically inspired scanpaths prediction model has simple input information and does not consider the interaction and competition of different signals, this paper proposes a scanpaths prediction model based on the signals competition. In this model, top-down and bottom-up signals are obtained from a two-stage object detection network, and a "parallel processing - organic fusion" computing structure is established based on physiological parameters to simulate the visual search process. In this paper, the model is tested on the dataset of clock and microwave(MCS), and the results show that the method has a significant improvement over the benchmark in the metrics.

articleTitle: Aircraft Wing Ice Online Detection and Fault-Tolerant Control Law Design
abstract: This paper focuses on the aircraft inflight icing detection and protection problem. A fault-tolerant flight control with the time-varying aerodynamic parameter online estimation is prweoposed to stabilize the aircraft attitude and maintain the flight height during the wing ice accretion process. The eigenstructure assignment and the proportional-integral- derivative control methods are utilized to design the flight control law. An aerodynamic parameter estimation method is adopted for the online ice detection and the control law reconfiguration. Then the accuracy of the parameter estimator and the performance of the closed control loop are evaluated by a steady-level cruise scenario of an ice research aircraft. The results indicate the feasibility of realizing the ice detection and control protection simultaneously in the fault-tolerant flight control loop.

articleTitle: Subspace Inference in SDE-Net for Bayesian Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Bayesian inference was once a gold standard for uncertainty estimation with neural networks. However, Bayesian inference is inefficient in high-dimensional parameter spaces of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs). A novel Non-Bayesian Neural Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE-Net) model quantifies epistemic uncertainty of DNNs from the perspective of dynamical systems. In this paper, we propose a subspace inference procedure in Non-Bayesian SDE-Net method for uncertainty estimation from Bayesian perspectives. This procedure contains two steps, first of all, the low-dimensional parameter subspaces of SDE-Net model are constructed to generate the first principal components from Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) trajectories, which involve various high-performance models. Secondly, Variational Inference (VI) and Elliptical Slice Sampling (ESS) methods are implemented in the constructed subspace to explore in the full parameter spaces for uncertainty estimation. The experimental results of Bayesian average on the derived posterior in the generated principal subspaces of model parameters show that accurate and well-calibrated results can be obtained for regression and classification tasks.

articleTitle: Overlapped Human Pose Estimation using Non-Maximum Suppression based on Shape Similarity
abstract: Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DNNs) have made significant progress on human pose estimation task in recent years. However, the question of whether we are making the most use of the information we get from DNNs has not been well studied. Top-down approach which first detects person body box then utilizes single person pose estimation by heatmap is a widely used method in multi-person pose estimation. However, information that predicted by DNNs contains more information than we consider. In person box prediction process, when two persons are closed to each other, the Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) we often use filters out the body boxes with smaller scores. For tackling this problem, we apply NMS based on Shape Similarity to person body boxes detection for tackling the problem that deleting the overlapped body boxes with smaller scores, and then extract keypoint coordinates and tag information for filter noise candidates from heatmap by Trasformer to improve the prediction accuracy. At last we develop an algorithm for refining keypoint coordinate by tag information. In experiment, we got mean Average Precision(mAP) of 76.0% in COCO2017 validation dataset, better than 75.6% with TransPose.

articleTitle: Marine Target Detection Algorithm Based on Deep Learning
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low detection accuracy and slow training speed of YOLOv3 for marine target, a ship target detection method based on the improved YOLOv3 algorithm is proposed. In this method, the BN layer is merged into the convolutional layer to improve the forward inference speed of the model. GloU is selected to replace the original mean square error loss function, which can not only focus on overlapping areas, but also other non-overlapping areas to improve the detection accuracy. In order to solve the problem of image distortion, blur and low contrast, gaussian filter brightness enhancement and histogram equalization were used to preprocess the image to improve the image quality. The preprocessed ship image was input into the improved YOLOv3 network for training. The experimental results show that, compared with the original YOLOv3 algorithm, the training speed is improved by 7.69%, the reasoning speed is improved by 27.47%, and the AP is improved by 3.12%, which verifies the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in marine ship target detection.

articleTitle: Object Detection Of Flexible Object With Arbitrary-Oriented Based On Rotation Adaptive YOLOv5
abstract: It is a difficult challenge to detect flexible objects with a large-scale span in the scene. In the task of detecting flexible objects with arbitrary orientation, the traditional object detection algorithm cannot accurately detect flexible objects, and the arbitrary-oriented object detection algorithm has boundary problems. In this paper, we propose to tackle the precise detection of flexible objects problem by using an adaptive rotation method. We change the parameter representation of the rotation detector using the long-side description method and solve the problem that the area of the detected object is much smaller than the background in the horizontal rectangular box. The angle parameter in the rotation detector is equally divided to change the angle continuity. The discretization of the angle parameters ensures that the anchor adjustment would not exceed the defined range, and solves the boundary problem of any flexible object in the detection direction of the rotation detector. Moreover, an symmetric function is proposed to convert angle categories, and the distance difference of each angle category is measured by bringing the prediction probability vector into the function. Extensive experiments and visual analysis on a self-built dataset showed the accuracy and effectiveness of the method for detecting flexible objects with arbitrary orientation.

articleTitle: Face Recognition Method Based on Deep-shallow Feature Fusion
abstract: Aiming at the problem of limited discrimination of features extracted by traditional shallow features and rapid decline of recognition rate in complex environments, a face recognition algorithm that fuses the deep and shallow features is proposed in this paper. We extract the HOG feature and PCANet feature of the face image respectively, and used Principal Component Analysis (PCA) method to reduce the dimensionality of the feature vectors. After fusing the processed feature vectors, we used Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) to further reduce the dimensionality and select the discriminative information. And SVM classifier is adopted for classification. The experimental results on AR and LFW dataset show that our algorithm has higher recognition rate and stronger robustness to complex environments than the single feature method.

articleTitle: Scheduling optimization of silicon single crystal production process based on adaptive improved particle swarm optimization
abstract: Aiming at the potential safety hazards of silicon single crystal production enterprises in the process of multi-furnace silicon single crystal production, and considering the maximum power load requirements in actual enterprises, a silicon single crystal production process scheduling model with the goal of minimizing the maximum completion time was established. Based on this model, an adaptive improved particle swarm optimization algorithm (Adaptive GPSO) is proposed to solve it. The algorithm retains the individual optimal value and global optimal value of the particle swarm algorithm, and introduces the crossover operation and mutation operation in the genetic algorithm to improve the new individual generation mechanism. At the same time, it performs dynamic iterative calculations on the mutation probability and crossover probability to avoid the algorithm fall into the local optimum, and improve the diversity and convergence of the algorithm. By solving different scales scheduling problems of silicon single crystal production process, the experiments on real-world data shows that the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

Author Keywords: silicon single crystal production process scheduling

articleTitle: Application of Sine Cosine Algorithm in Eigenvalue Extraction of Infrared Spectrum
abstract: In the field of infrared spectrum analysis, eigenvalue extraction plays a very important role in improving the modeling accuracy and computational efficiency of regression model. In this paper, in order to establish the analysis model of gas mixture, the infrared spectrum of the gas mixture was acquired by Fourier spectrometer. The spectral data dimension was too large, reaching 1,866 dimensions. So sine cosine algorithm(SCA) is proposed to extract eigenvalues of the spectrum data and partial least squares regression(PLSR) is used to build the quantitative analysis model. A total of 938 gas mixtures samples were prepared, consisting of methane, ethane and propane, and the concentration of each component gas ranges from 1% to 10%, 1% to 15%, and 1% to 10%. In order to improve the accuracy of the model and reduce the dimension of the infrared spectrum data even further, SCA is first used for waveband selection, and then SCA is used again for eigenvalue extraction in the selected band. In the experiments, regression models were established for each component gas, the eigenvalue spectrum data extracted by SCA are used as the input variables of each model, the mean relative error(MRE) between the calculated results of gas concentration of each component in the model and the expected output was used as the evaluation index. The experimental results show that after waveband selection, the dimension of the spectrum data is reduced from 1866 to 350, and the average of the MRE of the three component gas analysis models is reduce from 41.43% to 30.22%. On the basis of waveband selection, eigenvalue extraction is performed by SCA, the average dimension of the eigenvalue is about 28, and the average of the MRE of the three component gas analysis models is about 15.96%. Compared with the raw spectral data, the dimension of the spectrum data is reduced by 98.50%, and the MRE of the model is reduced by 61.50%. SCA has good global optimization ability and convergence ability, it is feasible to use this method to extract the eigenvalues of infrared spectrum data.

articleTitle: Cut To Size: A Lightweight Design for STR via Channel Pruning
abstract: In natural scenes, text full of rich and prominent information contributes to understand the scene. Scene text recognition (STR) is commercially viable in the wave of big data, which comes to be the center of attention. The existing STR methods based on deep learning have make significant progress, but for the complexity and size of model, it is difficult to be deployed in embedded devices. Therefore, a lightweight design for STR via synergistic pruning is proposed. To score the value of channels, it evaluates not only the convolution layer weights, but also the BN(Batch Normalization) layer scaling factors jointly. It can delete redundant channels which slightly influences the ability of the model. Meanwhile, some strategies are presented for fine-tuning model performance or contracting the model size. All models are trained and tested on public datasets. The experimental results on CCPD2019 well prove the effectiveness of this work, which can cut 87.60% params of CRNN and 78.31% params of Rosetta, respectively, and only reduce a little accuracy.

articleTitle: Stochastic Stability and Stabilization of Linear Time-delay Positive Systems With Two Independent Markov Processes
abstract: The stochastic stability and stabilization (SSaS) of Markov jump linear positive delayed systems (MJLPDSs) driven by two-independent Markov processes (TiMps) are examined. In view of the transition probability and the positivity of the system, this paper constructs a fresh stochastic co-positive linear Lyapunov-functional (LF). By describing equation of system via the mathematical expectation of the Markovianized states, several sufficient and necessary delay-dependent conditions for SSaS of continuous-time MJLPDSs with TiMps are presented draw on linear programming (LP). An sample is given to verify the theory achievements.

articleTitle: Primary Frequency Control of Renewable Energy Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Proportion of wind power, photovoltaic, and other renewable energy sources in the power system gradually increasing, the capability of system primary frequency regulation has a trend of weakening. To improve this situation, renewable energy sources are required to have the same ability to participate in system frequency regulation as conventional power sources. This paper analyzes the dynamic performance of the interconnected power system composed of wind farms based on doubly-fed induction generators (DFIG), then proposes a control method based on the deep reinforcement learning algorithm-Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient Agents (DDPG), according to the power generation characteristics of wind farms. The reward function, input states, and output actions of the DDPG algorithm are designed in conjunction with the control objectives, thus the DDPG algorithm is effectively applied to the primary frequency regulation optimization scheme to achieve the control goals which is adaptively acquiring the optimal coordination control strategies of the controllers of multiple renewable energy power plant. Numerical simulations on a two- area power system demonstrate that the design scheme can effectively mitigate the regional frequency deviation problem of each area containing in the power system, to maintain the stable operation of the system.

articleTitle: Empirical Research on the Integrated Innovation in Cross-Function Expert System Co-development between Industry and University
abstract: This paper discusses an integrated innovation based joint development model between industries and universities. As is well known, integrated innovation which includes explicit knowledge coming from universities and tacit knowledge coming from industries is fundamentally a process of knowledge conversion, thus the cooperation with universities is one of the important channel by which enterprises can enhance their research ability, so as to obtain sustainable development from the modern knowledge economy. In the case of intelligent robot thermal spraying expert system development, this work proposes a new cooperation pattern between universities and enterprises which consists of four basic modules: Technical Requirements, Process Modeling, System Implementation and Quality Analysis. Fuzzy Borda analysis of the cooperation development of universities and enterprises is also performed in this work aiming to explore the knowledge sharing management. Lastly, knowledge transfer related performance evaluation model is built to estimate the cooperation effect between the two.

Author Keywords: Intelligent Robot Thermal Spraying Expert System Development

articleTitle: Multi-component in fermentation online detection flow path control system based on novel enzyme electrode
abstract: Focus on the problem of multi-component in-situ on-line monitoring in fermentation, in this work, we proposed an on-line in-situ multi-channel detection flow path control system based on a novel enzyme electrode prepared from Prussian Blue (PB) nanomaterials. To match the detection behavior of this electrode, an innovative design of a multi-channel pump-valve synergistic flow path control system can effectively reduce cross-contamination and improve system reliability. According to the flow path detection logic requirements, software program modules, such as precise positioning and micro-injection of pipette needle, and calibration detection during the multi-component detection process, have been developed. Precise positioning and micro-injection of pipette needle were realized by the trapezoidal acceleration and deceleration algorithm combined with a subdivision drive circuit. For the continuous change glucose concentration in fermentation, an adaptive sampling strategy of the injection volume and calibration detection module were proposed to realize multi-component, wide-range from 1g/L to 180g/L, fast and accurate detection, which presenting the as-prepared in-situ on-line system was proved to exhibits a high accuracy with a low detection error (<2%) within the linear range.

articleTitle: Planning and Design Method of Integrated Energy Station in Complex Terrain
abstract: In order to promote the construction of the energy Internet and alleviate the pressure on resources and the environment, choose a suitable place for the integrated energy station is really important. In this article, we focused on the design of integrated energy stations that considers the coordination of multiple energy flows of cooling, heating, power, and gas under complex terrain conditions. Based on Regional geographic basis and load spatial characteristics, an integrated energy station location planning method is proposed under the framework of geographic information system. First of all, with the help of geographic information system, a geospatial analysis model is established, combined with a spatial multi-criteria decision analysis method to assess the suitability of the land in the area to be planned for building integrated energy stations. Secondly, a kernel density estimation method considering the spatial distribution characteristics of the load is proposed to determine the reasonable location of the integrated energy station. Finally, determined the final number and location of the integrated energy station. This paper takes a hypothetical area as an example to carry out simulation analysis and verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Compared with the k-means method, the results show that the site selection geographic score has increased by 41.49%, and the coverage of high-density load areas has increased by 25.93%. This method has guiding significance for the design of integrated energy stations in complex terrain.

articleTitle: Time Series Forecasting Based on Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Logic System with PSO
abstract: For some problems with unpredictable and random risk, such as building energy consumption, an interval type-2 fuzzy logic system is proposed for time series forecasting to reduce forecast errors. In the design, the particle swarm optimization algorithm adjusts the parameters of the designed interval type-2 fuzzy logic system, and the membership functions of the antecedent and the subsequent are all selected as Gaussian membership function which has uncertain standard deviation. Statistical results and contrast experiment confirm that the interval type-2 fuzzy model which used particle swarm optimization algorithm can simplify the system rules in a great extent and improve the accuracy of predicted results in contrast with the mathematical model which has not particle swarm optimization which has certain research value.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning Based Autonomous Racing Car Control With Priori Knowledge
abstract: In the community of artificial intelligence, re-searchers have devoted much effort to the application of deep reinforcement learning algorithms for autonomous driving. Under deep reinforcement learning framework, it is important for the racing car agent to interact with its external environment to accumulate enough driving experience. However, the inter-action process is usually inefficient, risky and time-consuming. Furthermore, it is a common problem in relevant studies that brake policy is difficult to master. In this paper, we adopt some priori knowledge about vehicle dynamics to design the brake force and update it to the actor-critic network by soft-learning strategy. In addition, some effective strategies are developed to improve the training efficiency and control performance. The Open Racing Car Simulator(TORCS) is adopted to evaluate our algorithm. The simulation results show the effectiveness of our proposed algorithm with better learning efficiency, robustness and generalization performance.

articleTitle: Target Localization in Underwater Acoustic Sensor Networks with False Data Attacks
abstract: Recently, the underwater sensor networks (USNs) play increasingly essential role in many applications, such as target localization. However, it faces extremely harsh environment including clock asynchronous and false data attacks. This paper investigates the above problem and proposes an attack-resistant target localization algorithm. The localization process is mainly divided into two phases. One is sensor nodes clock synchronization and self-localization. Followed by the USNs obtain the position of target. Specifically, sensor nodes complete clock synchronize using average clock synchronization algorithm and perform self-localization. Especially, taking false clock data attack (FCDA) in synchronize process into consideration. Then sensor nodes are grouped to solve the position of target under false estimations attack (FEA). The security test by adaptive threshold is used to determine whether the estimated position is accurate. The weight of attacked estimation is reduced by adaptively deviation-tolerant secure target localization consensus algorithm (DLCA). Simulation results in Section IV reveal the effectiveness of algorithm despite false data attacks exist.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Control for Networked Markovian Jump Systems with Disturbances
abstract: This article studies the Markovian jump networked control systems (MJNCS) with disturbances and variable network topology. Firstly, to obtain the information of the states and external disturbances, an unknown input observer (UIO) is designed instantaneously. Then, The control signal is constructed based on equivalent method, and the external disturbance is compensated by online information. Moreover, a new sliding function is constructed to bring it down to a stable origin. Additionally, the stability of the control system is proved. Secondly, to deal with the changes of network topology, a super twisting-based controller (STW) is adopted. The stability of STW controller is analyzed by using linear matrix inequality (LMT) technique and Lyapunov functional method. To make the closed-loop system stable, a composite super twisting sliding mode controller (CSTWSMC) based on two control signals is proposed for the first time. Finally, a result analysis is given to verify the performance of the proposed control methodology.

articleTitle: Power Quality Situation Awareness in Distribution Station Area Based on Data Mining
abstract: With the continuous development of renewable energy and the rapid growth of user power demand, it is significant how to obtain quickly and accurately the operation status and future development trend of power quality in the distribution station area. A data mining-based power quality situation awareness method in distribution station area is proposed. Firstly, in the stage of situation assessment, the criteria importance though intercriteria correlation(CRITIC) is used to mine the data of power quality acquisition device to determine the index weight at the time of on-line assessment, and the real-time data is used to construct the dynamic evaluation matrix of power quality ground to realize online evaluation of power quality; Then, in the stage of situation prediction, the complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise(CEEMDAN) is used on the basis of single long-short term memory (LSTM) to master its situation development; Finally, an example shows that the method can grasp the situation of power quality in distribution area in time, which is conducive to the realization of lean management.

articleTitle: Distributed Scalable Design of Local Controllers for a class of Nonlinear Networked Systems
abstract: This paper is motivated by a recently published IEEE AC paper and its targeted applications: “Distributed Synthesis of Local Controllers for Networked Systems with Arbitrary Interconnection Topologies”. This is a very interesting work in this area. However, the results presented in the IEEE paper have two major limitations: (1) it only applies to linear systems, and (2) robustness is only discussed in a remark without further investigation. In the work presented in this paper, with the same main features of the approach in the IEEE paper: “local and scalable”, we have applied our design to a class of non-linear systems. This is demonstrated by controller design for a system of N-inverted pendulums coupled by N-1 springs. Despite this achievement, our work still has two limitations: (1) it only applies to a class of nonlinear systems, and (2) although we have studied the robustness of our design in some detail, a systematic and theoretical result is still yet to be developed. These issues and planned future work are discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Computational Models of Stellate Cells in Layer II of Medial Entorhinal Cortex
abstract: In vivo experiments have found that animals encode their current location through spatial neurons (such as grid cells, place cells, border cells, head-direction cells, and so on) that are usually classified according to their functions (or firing patterns). And in vitro experiments revealed that there are two types of excitatory neurons within medial entorhinal cortex according to their structural characteristics: stellate cells and pyramidal cells. It is still unclear that how neuronal types with different functions correspond to multiple structural types. Previous researches have modeled spatial neurons primarily according to their functional type. In this paper, we attempt to model spatial neurons according to their structural type and propose computational models of stellate cells in layer II of medial entorhinal cortex. We use leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neurons to model the soma of stellate cells which are driven by feedforward excitatory current inputs. To obtain this drive current, up-stream velocity-controlled oscillators (VCOs) are used, and the output of VCOs is encoded using an inverse hexagonal discrete Fourier transform (IHDFT). At the same time, this current is regulated by a local recurrent network consisted of stellate cells and interneurons and by backprojection signals from down-stream hippocampus. Simulation results demonstrate that our model generates grid-like and border-like firing patterns. Our model explains the causes of stellate cell discharge activity and gives a new direction for modeling spatial neurons.

articleTitle: Detection of Mobile Phone Screen Defect Based on Faster R-CNN Fusion Model
abstract: With the increasing prevalence of mobile phone products, the quality of mobile phones has become more and more vital, especially the quality of mobile phone screens. Therefore, the accurate detection of screen defects is essential. However, traditional manual and machine vision method detection have the problems of low detection accuracy and slow efficiency. Based on the problems of the above detection methods, this paper proposes the detection method based on Faster R-CNN fusion model to improve the detection performance. First, the designed image preprocessing methods, U-Net and ResNet50, are combined and used as the feature extraction part of the whole network with the aim of obtaining more distinct feature information. Secondly, the region proposals the network part to generate initial anchors of specific size by K-means clustering algorithm instead of manual setting, which can have an improvement on the accuracy and rate of classification and position prediction of bounding boxes. The experimental show that on our dataset, improved Faster R-CNN achieves 83% mAp, which proving the applicability of the model proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Defect detection method with local low pass filter and adaptive threshold segmentation for photovoltaic cells
abstract: Any defects in the production process will seriously affect the safety and conversion efficiency of photovoltaic cells. This paper presents a defect detection method for photovoltaic cells using image processing technology based on photoluminescence (PL) imaging. First, the PL image of photovoltaic cell is preprocessed, and a local low-pass filter, which is different from the traditional low-pass filter, is designed to filter the high-frequency signal accurately in frequency domain for removing the grid lines. Then, the image is segmented by combining histogram bimodal method and adaptive threshold method. Finally, the defect detection is completed by using connectivity detection. To measure the performance of the proposed method, 45 photovoltaic cells sample images are used for testing experiments. The recall rate of detection is 95.28%, and the accuracy rate is 96.02%.

articleTitle: Research on lace defect detection based on fingerprint identification method of detail feature points extraction and matching
abstract: The development of lace has a profound impact on the economic development and new employment in some regions, so the demand for lace is increasing year by year. However, the quality inspection problem has been troubling the whole lace industry. In order to solve this problem, this paper uses the fingerprint identification method to extract and match the details of feature points to detect the defects of lace images. Firstly, a series of preprocessing is carried out between the template and the image to be matched, including normalization, distinguishing the initial foreground and background color, removing the void and burr, image refinement, etc. Secondly, two kinds of detail feature points, namely, endpoints and bifurcation points, are extracted from the thinning graph and the feature information of lace detail points is counted. Then, three kinds of pseudo feature points, short line, outlier and ring, are removed according to the process of distance and ring method. Finally, the Euclidean distance is used to calculate the distance between each step length of the same feature point in the two images and the current feature point, and the distance is saved. If the coordinates of the pixel points stored within the synchronous length are basically the same, it means that the two images are the same. The experiments show that the proposed algorithm is superior to the compared algorithms in terms of both recognition rate and algorithm speed, which meets the requirements of small and medium-sized lace enterprises.

articleTitle: Kinetic modeling and parameter optimization of n-butane isomerization reaction
abstract: The optimization of operating conditions for n-butane isomerization reaction is a typical nonlinear optimization problem. In order to improve the yield of the main product isobutane under the action of the same catalyst, in view of the difficulty in selecting the reaction process parameters, this paper proposes to apply the AWOA (Adaptive elite strategy whale optimization algorithm, AWOA) to the optimization of the process parameters of n-butane isomerization reaction. Firstly, according to the network structure and experimental data of n-butane isomerization reaction under laboratory conditions, the AWOA was used to identify the parameters of the reaction kinetics model, and the model was verified. Then, for the established n-butane isomerization reaction kinetics model, with the maximum yield of isobutane as the optimization objective, the process parameters at the maximum yield were obtained. Simulation results show that the proposed method can obtain a set of optimal process parameters and improve the yield of effective substances.

articleTitle: A Multi-Kemel Discriminant Analysis Framework for Specific Radar Emitter Identification
abstract: Specific radar emitter identification, a.k.a. radar emitter individual identification, plays a momentous role in modern electronic countermeasures. This paper concentrates on the multiple kernel learning (MKL)-based multi-feature fusion methodology, and a multi-kernel discriminant analysis (MKDA) framework is thus proposed for radar individual identification. Based on the Doppler shift slices of ambiguity function (AF) representation, multiple kernels corresponding to the AF slices are constructed firstly. Then MKDA algorithms are utilized to extract the nonlinear discriminative features, followed by the simplest nearest neighbor classifier. Considering the efficiency of real-time systems, we devise two two-stage MKDA algorithms based on the criteria of kernel discriminant ratio (KDR) and kernel between-class scatter degree (KBCSD), respectively. We use two real radar datasets to evaluate the proposed framework. The KDR-MKDA and KBCSD-MKDA algorithms perform best in terms of both time efficiency and identification accuracy.

articleTitle: Vehicle Trajectory Data Publishing Mechanism Based on Differential Privacy
abstract: In recent years, the intelligent connected vehicle technology has been developing rapidly, which will vigorously promote the construction of smart city. Vehicle trajectory data is of great value for applications such as city services and data mining. However, it will greatly endanger the safety of participants if trajectory data is released unprotected. In this paper, we consider the velocity factor and propose Douglas Peucker with velocity trajectory compression algorithm (DPWV) to achieve trajectory compression with lower error. Then, a ω-trajectory perturbation mechanism based on differential privacy (ω-TPDP) is proposed to protect the sensitive information of trajectory data. Meanwhile, in order to balance the utility and privacy of trajectory data, a privacy budget allocation method is adopted based on the weight value and the risk coefficient of privacy leakage of the current location. Through theoretical analysis and experimental comparison, ω-TPDP can obtain commendable data availability under the premise of ensuring the privacy of trajectory.

articleTitle: Cooperative Output Feedback Control of a Dual Rigid-Flexible Two-Link Manipulator
abstract: This paper studies a dual rigid-flexible two-link manipulator system. Based on the system, a cooperative output feedback controller is designed for grasping rigid objects. In order to establish the infinite dimensional model of the system, it is established by Hamiltons principle as coupled ordinary differential equations-partial differential equations (ODEs-PDEs). Meanwhile, four high-gain observers are used to observe the unmeasurable states. Based on the above preparation, we propose cooperative control law based on Lyapunov direct method. It can realize the coordinated control of object position and control force, and eliminate the vibration of flexible manipulator in the process of movement. In the last part of the paper, the effectiveness of the proposed controller proved by rigorous theoretical analysis and simulation.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Method of Complex Supply and Transportation Mechanism Based on EEMD Multi-scale Sample Entropy and PSO-SVM
abstract: The complex supply and transportation mechanism has the characteristics of difficult feature extraction. However, traditional fault recognition methods have disadvantages such as poor noise robustness and low fault recognition accuracy. In order to improve the accuracy of recognition, through combining Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD) with Multi-scale Sample Entropy (MSE), a fault diagnosis method of complex supply and transportation mechanism based on EEMD-MSE and Particle Swarm Optimization Support Vector Machine (PSO-SVM) is proposed. First, the method performs cross-correlation information analysis on a series of stable Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMF) of different time scales obtained by EEMD decomposition of the original vibration signal to reconstruct the signal; Then, the MSE of the reconstructed signal is calculated to construct a feature vector, which is divided into a training set and a test set; The penalty parameters and kernel function parameters are optimized through the PSO algorithm. The optimized SVM is used as a multi-fault classifier, and the training set is used as the input vector to train the vector machine to obtain the optimal parameters. The trained model is detected by using the test set to verify the accuracy of effective fault diagnosis. The bench test of the ammunition supply mechanism has proved that the proposed method can effectively identify its health status and failure type.

articleTitle: A hybrid immune algorithm for the min-cost flying sidekick traveling salesman problem
abstract: The flying sidekick traveling salesman problem (FSTSP) is an extension of the classic TSP, where a truck and drone are used to deliver packages to customers. A notable feature of the FSTSP is that a drone needs travel with a truck under synchronization constraints. Based on variable neighborhood search (VNS), a hybrid immune algorithm (HIA) is presented to solve the FSTSP with the target of minimizing the total operational cost. VNS includes basic VNS (BVNS) method used in the stage of generating the initial population and general VNS (GVNS) method used in the process of improving memory cells. Randomized variable neighborhood descent (RVND) is used as the local search method for GVNS, which applies a random neighborhood ordering. The proposed algorithm is compared with two existing methods in the literature. The experimental results show that HIA is very competitive and provides state-of-the-art solutions for most instances. In addition, our approach is more stable.

articleTitle: Q-learning based Robust Model Predictive Control for Uncertain Linear Systems
abstract: The Q-learning based robust model predictive control (RMPC) technique is proposed to solve constrained control problems of the linear system with multiplicative and additive uncertainty. The proposed method consists of RMPC mode and Q-learning mode. In the RMPC mode, only the effect of multiplicative uncertainty is restrained and the finite gain l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> stability of the real system can be guaranteed during the operation of RMPC modes. In the Q-learning mode, the feedback gain of the RMPC controller is improved by using the process data generated by a succession of RMPC modes, which leads to a reduction of l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gain from additive disturbance to system state. The case study shows the feasibility of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Adaptive Tracking Control for Mobile Robots With Multiple Constraints
abstract: This paper studies the mobile robots with multiple constraints based on path planning of A-star algorithm. A hierarchical adaptive control method is presented to handle multiple constaints. On the upper layer, a Astar path planning algorithm is designed. On the lower layer, a new controller is provided. Then, we design barrier Lyapunov function and adaptive RBF neural network control method to make sure that tracking error and velocity error converges to the specified set within a finite amount of time. Compared with other existing works, this system considers multiple consraints include tracking error, constraints velocity constraints and output saturation constraint, provides guarantee for the safe operation of the mobile robot. In addition, because of the unknown conditions on the ground, system also considers the impact of slipping. Computer simulation result demonstrates the effectiveness of control method. In the experimental verification, we use A-star algorithm to generate the appropriate path as the desired trajectory of the mobile robot. The experiment proved the stability of control method.

articleTitle: Grasp Planning Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning: A Brief Survey
abstract: Grasping is a fundamental ability for robots to inter-act with the environment. Recent advances show great progress on grasping unstructured household objects by leveraging deep reinforcement learning. This paper presents a brief survey on grasp planning based on deep reinforcement learning. The goal of grasp planning is to determine the actions of the robotic manipulator moving from its initial position to the target one so that the object could be grasped and manipulated. However, objects could be stacked or occluded, making the target object ungraspable by applying a simple grasp action. To tackle this issue, auxiliary actions (such as pushing) should be conducted along with grasping. According to whether auxiliary actions are performed, we categorize the existing grasping planning methods into two classes: methods without auxiliary actions and methods with auxiliary actions. We review them in details and show the advantages and limitations of each type. Furthermore, we show several popular evaluation metrics that are widely used in grasp planning. Finally, difficulties and future research directions are discussed.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-UAV Cooperative Defense Method with Support Mechanism
abstract: As an air carrier with strong mobility, an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) can carry various types of equipment and complete a variety of tasks. Aiming at the cooperative defense mission, this paper proposes a multi-UAV collaborative defense method with support mechanism for reasonable planning, and designs a simulation experiment for verification. The proposed method mainly uses hierarchical clustering for task assignment and a greedy algorithm for path planning to realize preliminary mission planning. Then, it sets up a one-to-one support mechanism to utilize the idle UAV resources to reduce the overall mission completion time, and realize the final mission planning.

articleTitle: The influence of performance limitations of roadside sensors on the stability of mixed traffic under vehicle-road cooperation
abstract: The reasonable layout of roadside sensors under the condition of vehicle-road cooperation plays an important role in the effective interaction and deep fusion between vehicle and road. In this paper, based on cooperative adaptive cruise control model and intelligent driver model, a novel micro model of mixed traffic which considered the sensor performance limitation and communication topology. After that, the stability of the model is proved by Routh-Horwitz stability criterion, and the stability conditions are obtained. Based on this, this paper studies the influence of the spacing of roadside sensors on the operation of the mixed traffic flow in holographic environment. The experiment demonstrates the dynamic characteristics of mixed traffic flow when the roadside sensors are deployed in accordance with the sensor’s accurate sensing range, effective sensing range and limit sensing range respectively. And the result shows that the model presented in this paper can accurately describe the process that the fluctuation amplitude of mixed traffic flow in evolution increases with the increase of spacing.

articleTitle: Accurate Annotation of Gaze Point for Wearable Eye Tracking Devices
abstract: As the cost of eye tracking devices decreases, wearable eye tracking devices are becoming more and more popular in head-mounted devices such as smart glasses and augmented reality helmets. Eye tracking enabled devices are believed to facilitate a better understanding of human behaviors and intentions, and will make the interaction between human and computing systems more natural and friendly. A challenging problem for wearable eye tracking devices is the accurate annotation of the gaze point in a real-world scenario, that is, to identity the real object where each gaze point is on and the accurate position of the gaze point relative to this object. We propose a framework for gaze point annotation in real-world scenarios and design a system to implement this framework by establishing an accurate mapping between the gaze point and its coordinates relative to a computer screen. Experimental results show our method is robust in real-world scenarios and can reach an error rate less than 1%, This demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Tracking Control of Uncertain Interconnected Time-delay Nonlinear Systems with Full State Constraints
abstract: This paper studies the tracking control problem for a class of uncertain interconnected nonlinear systems subject to deferred and asymmetric time-varying (DATV) delays. First, the case that system states are constrained at the very beginning is considered. It’s noting that this case is quite different from that the state constraints appear after the system running a period of time. Then, with combination of error-shifting technique and asymmetric barrier Lyapunov function, the proposed control scheme overcomes the DATV state constraints without requiring any initial conditions. Finally, a numerical example illustrates the effectiveness of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Distributed Optimal Dispatching of Multi-Agent Integrated Energy System Based on ADMM with Dynamic Step Size
abstract: Under the requirement of low-carbon energy operation, the integrated energy system is an effective way to meet the social sustainable development and achieve the goal of carbon neutrality. In this paper, the micro energy grid is taken as the agent of the integrated energy system. The micro energy grid is described based on the energy hub model, and a system framework for the coordinated operation with direct energy exchange of the multi-agent and the upper carbon management center is established. Alternating direction method of multipliers(ADMM)algorithm is transformed and introduced to realize the distributed solution of the problem. The system only needs the necessary information to solve the distributed optimization solution, which can minimize the operation cost and the environment cost.Furthermore, the convergence performance of the algorithm is improved by dynamically adjusting the iteration step size under the same convergence criteria. Finally, a simulation example is given to analyze the energy optimization results and step size adjustment results of the proposed method, and the effectiveness and improvement advantages are verified.

articleTitle: Switched Perimeter Control for Two-Region Urban Traffic Networks with Dynamic Macroscopic Fundamental Diagrams
abstract: Macroscopic fundamental diagrams (MFD) in a homogeneous urban road network are extended to dynamic ones for two regions constituting this network, and a novel perimeter control strategy based on switched MPC is proposed in this paper. During the peak hour, the road network can be partitioned several times triggered by some switching signals, and this is different from static road network partitioning. In this paper, a switching system control method called SMPC is proposed such that perimeter controller for the two-region urban network can switch among different schemes in the case of dynamic MFDs. By SMPC, the desired accumulation can be achieved and the congestion in the central region can be alleviated. Effectiveness of the proposed perimeter control strategy based on SMPC is verified by numerical simulations and the comparison results based on different evaluation indexes show the performance of SMPC is superior to another two control methods.

articleTitle: Multi-target relative distance perception based on monocular image
abstract: These years, target detection has been frequently used in autonomous driving, UAV scene analysis and robot vision due to its technological breakthroughs. Aiming at the problem that the category and category probability information provided by target detection is insufficient in the field of autonomous driving, a multi-target relative distance perception algorithm based on monocular images is proposed. Using monocular depth estimation to obtain a depth image, apply the target bounding box information to the depth map to find the location of the target, and then combine the relative distance perception based on pixel values to get relative distance information. The results of our experiments show that the proposed viewpoint adds a new information compared with traditional target detection, can provide relative distance information, and can help to realize the assistant driving of short distance straight line.

articleTitle: Research on Key Technologies of HSR Intelligent Dispatching based on Cloud-Edge Collaboration
abstract: In order to solve the problems of resource pressure, bandwidth load, multi-source heterogeneous data processing and security privacy caused by big data centralization in intelligent railway dispatching under emergencies, a hierarchical multi-level intelligent dispatching architecture of hybrid central cloud and edge cloud including network edge layer, central scheduling layer and station control layer is designed based on the idea of cloud edge collaboration. 1) The flow direction of network edge data is studied; 2)The operation flow of the edge node and the station control unit is designed with the help of service registration and message subscription; 3)The security of data and services is guaranteed by the mechanisms of edge node capability authentication, message time validity checking, mobile message window and node last will. Relying on the full play of resource efficiency of massive edge nodes close to data and more scene features and high-density data, the scheme can effectively improve the security card control performance of high-speed railway intelligent dispatching in emergencies.

articleTitle: Analysis of the influence of SOFC degradation on system State and performance
abstract: Solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) is a promising energy conversion technology because of its high efficiency, low emission and fuel adaptability. As there are many degradation mechanisms that affect the operating life of SOFC, and the internal state is difficult to measure, analyzing the specific relationship between the critical states which is easy to observe and system degradation is an important prerequisite for timely and effective evaluation of system health. In this paper, based on the established SOFC degradation model, then it is analyzed from two aspects: system mechanism and data characteristics, stack average temperature, stack temperature gradient and fuel utilization of three critical states affecting system degradation are determined, their effects on system degradation are analyzed comprehensively, and the competitive relationship between system efficiency and system life is analyzed based on the data. The average temperature, temperature gradient and fuel utilization of three key states affecting system degradation are determined, their effects on system degradation are analyzed comprehensively, and the relationship between system efficiency and system life is analyzed based on the data, which provides a basis for further optimizing the operation of the system with high performance and long life.

articleTitle: Study on Technology of Wind Power Frequency Regulation Capability Improvement
abstract: With the continuous increase of wind power in power system, the share of conventional generation and the frequency regulation capacity of power system is gradually decreasing. In the case of high power loss or system failure, it is very easy to cause frequency failure of the whole system. Integrating large-scale wind power without frequency regulation capability into power system will bring enormous challenges to the power system's reliable operation. For this reason, the world's major wind power developed countries and regions have all put forward clear requirements for the frequency regulation capability of wind power through grid-connection guidelines. Electric power workers in China are also thinking about standardizing the primary frequency regulation capability test and simulation technology of wind power. Taking Fujian power grid as a example, this paper study the refined mathematical modeling, primary frequency regulation control technology, and the detection and evaluation methods of wind power peak-shaving and frequency regulation performance. Then the technical requirements for wind power peak-shaving and frequency regulation capability is analyzed. The development of related research provides important information for clarifying the frequency regulation output characteristics of wind farms. By further enhancing the "grid-friendliness" of wind power, it will improving the safe and stable operation level of power grid with a high share of wind power in the future.

articleTitle: Neural Combinatorial Optimization for Coverage Planning in UGV Reconnaissance
abstract: Urban combat environment is affected by buildings and traffic network with certain spatial characteristics. A single unmanned combat vehicle carries out the coverage reconnaissance task will be constrained by the limited information and low efficiency, so multiple UGVs(Unmanned Ground Vehicles) cooperative coverage becomes an effective means to solve the problem. In this paper, the urban coverage reconnaissance task is formulated as a vehicle routing problem, and a new traversal model is proposed, which takes account the connectivity characteristics of the road. At the same time, different from the traditional routing planning, which takes the total cost of executing tasks as the optimization objective. We consider the time efficiency of the battlefield, and takes the coverage reconnaissance time as the optimization objective function (in most cases of multiple UGVs coverage tasks, the longest task execution time is taken as the optimization objective). And we proposed a neural combinatorial optimization technique to solve the problem. Through simulation experiments, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed model is verified.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Risk Processing Method of Distribution Line Based on Deep Learning of Multi-source Data
abstract: There are situations such as panic detection, omission detection, and false detection in the manual detection of power grid lines, and it is also an inevitable trend to reduce labor costs. The existing deep learning intelligent detection methods mostly use single model of deep learning for image recognition, and the current intelligent detection methods are mostly aimed at distribution line or a certain defect. This paper studies an intelligent identification technology of distribution line feature based on deep vision. It performs deep learning on the inspection image data and automatically obtains the classification of risk feature. Firstly, this paper studies the strategy of obtaining the image data of the line during the intelligent inspection of the power grid. Secondly, the research will use the image data obtained by intelligent inspection to perform target recognition. This paper studies and uses a variety of machine learning models, and compares the results of several models under different layers and different iterations. Finally, this paper studies the ensemble learning technology to combine the classification results of distribution line characteristics in multiple models, carries out the risk prediction of secondary learning, and compares the classification result differences with the single classifier model.

articleTitle: Target tracking algorithm based on improved kernel correlation filtering
abstract: Aiming at the problem of severe accuracy degradation in the traditional KCF (Kernel correlation filter) target tracking algorithm in a complex environment, we propose an improved kernel correlation filter target tracking algorithm. First, the target scale is estimated by fusing the scale filter in the DSST (Discriminative Scale Space Tracking) algorithm to solve the traditional KCF algorithm cannot estimate the scale. Secondly, So as to solve the KCF algorithm's limited ability to express the features of the target appearance model, by fusing HOG (Histogram of Oriented Gradient) features and CN (Color Name) features, the algorithm's ability to extract target features is enhanced. Finally, by introducing peak response fluctuation detection, the credibility of the tracking target is judged, so as to decide whether to update the filter model. The experiment tested the overall tracking performance of the improved KCF algorithm by using the video sequences in the OTB2013 and OTB2015 standard data sets. The experimental results show that the accuracy and performance of the improved algorithm in complex environments have been significantly improved.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Fault Detection Filter of Switched Positive Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of event-triggered fault detection for switched positive systems. An event-triggering scheme based 1-norm inequality is established to reduce the transmission frequency of filter signal. Using multiple copositive Lyapunov functions, a fault detection filter is proposed under the event-triggering scheme to generate the residual signal and detect system faults. Under the designed filter, an event-based residual system is positive and stable and satisfies ℓ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-gain performance. All presented conditions can be formulated into linear programming. Finally, two illustrative examples are given to verify the effectiveness of the obtained results.

articleTitle: Robust H∞ decentralized control of the fractional-order interconnected system with element-bounded uncertainties over finite frequency ranges
abstract: This paper focuses on the problem of robust H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> decentralized control of the fractional-order interconnected system with element-bounded uncertainties over finite frequency ranges. The main goal is designing the decentralized feedback controller for the system to guarantee the system meets the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance and the controller can stabilized the system.In this paper, sufficient conditions are promoted that ensure the fractional-order interconnected system satisfies the bounded real lemma (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance) based on GKPY lemma. Finally, a numerical example in order to illustrate the effectiveness of the designing method is provided.

articleTitle: Construction and Experimental Research on Leakage Sound Dataset of Urban Water Supply Pipeline
abstract: Waterpipe is prone to leakage, resulting in signifi-cant expenses for water-supplying companies. Hence, there is a rising interest in machine detection or monitoring to find leakage using different sensors including microphones. In deep learning community, the emergence of public datasets has done a profound influence in promoting the advancement in acoustic scene and event detection and classification. But as far as we know, there are no public datasets focusing on the normal and anomalous sound from operating pipeline with pressure. This paper presents a new dataset of sound of operating pipeline with pressure, which we call a sound dataset for recording operating pipeline with pressure (ROPP dataset), containing 4.7 hours of annotated normal and anomalous sounds together with 16.1 hours of interfered sound events which are common interference when recording in streets. Experiments with mature environmental sound classification systems showed that the dataset was suitable for developing deep models for water leakage sound recognition.

articleTitle: TransDeeplabv3: Multi-Prior Segmentor for Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: At present, medical image segmentation is a challenging and developing task in medical image field, in which semantic segmentation algorithms play an important role in many clinical applications. The atrous spatial pyramid pooling (ASPP) module of Deeplab-V3 can well balance the diversity, robustness, and connectivity of global feature map extraction under different scenarios. However, there is still a large improving prospect for medical image segmentation. Therefore, we introduce mechanisms of multi-group parallel processing, mass guided loss focusing on irregular shape, and k-nearest attention architecture, respectively, to achieve higher robustness and stronger global connectivity with more sufficient receptive field compared to original methods. The proposed model effectively alleviates the deficiencies of local semantic receptive fields, improves the ability of generalization of our model, and overcomes the agnosticism of feature spatial distribution. Under the premise of maintaining feature diversity and enhancing heterogeneous information correlation, we obtain better segmentation performance in our experiments by enriching global feature representations. We conduct a series of segmentation experiments using the proposed model and on medical image datasets: STARE, CHASE, DRIVE and HRF. Compared with Deeplab-V3 baseline, the performance is significantly improved in terms of several metrics, which verifies the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Droop control strategy of isolated microgrid based on fractional order active disturbance rejection
abstract: In this paper, aiming at the problem of voltage and frequency deviation caused by load fluctuations during the operation of island microgrid (MG), and the three-phase voltage waveform distortion caused by the uncertainty of distributed power output power, a FOPID controller based on active disturbance rejection (FOPID-ADRC) is proposed, which combines the advantages of active disturbance rejection controller (ADRC) and fractional order PID (FOPID) controller. The controller was simulated and verified by switching on and off the load and sudden disturbance on the direct current (DC) side, and compared the proposed controller with the classic PI controller and the linear active disturbance rejection controller (LADRC). The simulation results show that the controller has good anti-disturbance performance, robustness and flexibility, and can effectively ensure the stability of voltage and frequency of the island MG.

articleTitle: Attachment Fault Diagnosis for Tidal Stream Turbine based on Improved ShuffleNet_v2
abstract: Tidal Stream Energy, which is clean and renewable, is an effective way to solve the depletion of nonrenewable resources. Blades of tidal stream turbine (TST) are the crucial part of power generation, but the fault rate is high. Aiming to solve blades’ attachment fault and large calculation of neural network, an attachment fault diagnosis method for TST based on improved ShuffleNet_v2 is proposed. Firstly, the blades image of TST is preprocessed by normalization and centralization. Secondly, the square convolution is decomposed by singular value decomposition (SVD) to decrease the amount of convolution calculation. Then, h-swish, whose effect is better than ReLU, is used as the activation function to improve ShuffleNet_v2, the novel structure is utilized to train the preprocessed image and the trained model is saved. Finally, the trained model is applied to diagnose the blades’ attachment. Experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively reduce parameters calculation, requirement of hardware performance, and the accuracy of blades’ attachment diagnosis is higher than some lightweight neural networks.

articleTitle: Evaluation Method of the Whole Process Safety Situation Assessment of Urban Distribution Network Considering the Ice Disaster Environment
abstract: In recent years, power system safety assessment and early warning technology, and the impact of natural disasters on power grids have been hotspots at home and abroad. However, the security and stability of distribution networks are not closely related to the research of natural disasters. In the context of this research, on the basis of conventional system evaluation, this paper further considers multi-scenarios and multi-operation modes, analyzes the disaster status of the distribution network, the disaster-bearing capacity and resource response capacity of the distribution network, in order to proactively With defense as the goal, build a whole-process security situation assessment index system for the distribution network in an ice disaster environment, and then use an evaluation method that combines the analytic hierarchy process and the entropy weight method to quantitatively evaluate the indicators and calculate the distribution network's performance in the ice disaster environment. As a result of the security situation assessment, the security level of the distribution network is obtained. On this basis, the initial accident scenario set is updated according to the evaluation results to form a dynamic accident scenario set, and an active defense evolution strategy process considering scenario optimization is proposed. Finally, the evaluation and analysis of the safety level of distribution networks in various regions of Liaoning Province in icing disasters proves the comprehensiveness and rationality of the safety situation assessment model, which is of great significance for further improving the safety and defense level of the distribution network.

articleTitle: Robust Least Squares Projection Twin Support Vector Machine and its Sparse Solution
abstract: Because the solution of Least squares projection twin support vector machine (LSPTSVM) is obtained by solving two smaller-size systems of linear equations, LSPTSVM has closed form solution and it is faster than classical least squares support vector machine (LSSVM). However, LSPTSVM has two disadvantages, it is sensitive to outliers and its solution lacks sparsity. Therefore, the LSPTSVM is difficult to training large-scale datasets. To solve this problem, we propose the robust LSPTSVM (R-LSPTSVM) by applying truncated least squares loss function which is a bounded function. R-LSPTSVM can be represented as difference of convex programming, then the primal solution of R-LSPTSVM can be obtained by using Concave-Convex Procedure. The sparse solution of R-LSPTSVM is iteratively obtained by using the pivoting Cholesky factorization. Furthermore, sparse R-LSPTSVM algorithm (SR-LSPTSVM) is proposed. Experimental results show that the SR-LSPTSVM is insensitive to outliers and can deal with large-scale datasets fast.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Control With Prescribed Tracking Performance For Uncertain Nonlinear Systems Preceded By Prandtl-Ishlinskii Operator
abstract: When using smart actuators to drive an uncertain unparametrizable nonlinear system, it is a challenging problem to design such an adaptive controller that the output tracking error can be steered into a preset interval asymptotically, especially in the presence of possible actuator failures which are unknown in time, pattern and value. To overcome the challenge, in the paper, an adaptive control scheme is developed, based on the nonlinear system model of lower-triangular form, and preceded by an unsaturated Prandtl-Ishlinskii hysteresis operator. The techniques of direct adaptive fuzzy control, decomposition of nonlinearities, and backstepping recursive design are used. With our scheme, it can be proved that all closed-loop signals are bounded, and the plant output tracks any given reference signal asymptotically with a user-defined accuracy. These are also illustrated through simulation results.

articleTitle: Quasi-min-max Discrete-time MPC of Time-delay MIMO Systems with Application to Mobile Robots
abstract: For multi-input multi-output (MIMO) systems, trajectory tracking controller design is conventionally optimized without considering the time delays. However, delays are incurred when the controller is implemented in a discrete-time manner, which needs some time to calculate suitable control inputs. Network-induced delays may also be part of the physical system in both the feedback and forward channels. A novel quasi-min-max discrete-time model predictive controller (DMPC) is presented to stabilize a general class of time-delay MIMO systems, and its application to industrial mobile robots is concerned meanwhile. To achieve this, the statistic information of the time delays is integrated during formulating the model-dependent tracking controller. Then, a robust DMPC that asymptotically stabilizes the time-delay system at the equilibrium point, i.e., origin. Moreover, optimal control decisions can be made by optimizing the constructed quasi-min-max quadratic cost function. Experiments based on a four-wheeled omnidirectional mobile robot are carried out to verify the validity and practical appeals of the presented DMPC scheme for lateral motion control.

articleTitle: Rumor Detection Based on Bi-directional Graph Attention Network
abstract: Information dissemination on social media is often accompanied by a large number of false or true rumors. The spread of these rumors on social network platforms does serious harm to social stability. Traditional rumor detection methods use text or image contents to identify rumors, but the performance is not satisfactory. Deep detection models combined with deep learning algorithms are developed recently. In this study, a new bi-directional graph attention network (Bi-GAT) model is proposed for rumor detection, where two directions of rumor information propagation are considered at the same time. Firstly, rumor information is transformed into a bi-directional graph structure form, simultaneously. Secondly, the feature of each node is extracted and input to graph attention network with the graph structure information, where the multi-head attention mechanism is adopted. Thirdly, after being processed via two graph attention layers, the two-directional data are concatenated and input to a fully connected layer. The results of rumor classification can be obtained according to the output of the fully connected layer. The simulation results on some open datasets demonstrate the validity of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Motion Simulation of Flying Quadruped Robot Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Traditional motion control methods for fixed-profile aircraft are difficult to satisfy the requirements of flying quadruped robot. However, the emergence of artificial intelligence provides new ideas for the design of variant aircraft systems. During the deformed flight, the flying quadruped robot is extremely susceptible to various internal and external disturbances. Therefore, it is challenging to ensure its stability. On this basis, the motion problem of flying quadruped robot is investigated by employing the new deep reinforcement learning technology. The twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm (TD3) is adopted to acquire gait and flight strategy through interactive learning with the environment. In order to enhance the learning efficiency in the training process, the framework of actor-critic learning system is proposed. In the meanwhile, the extra domain-specific knowledge is applied to shape the reward function. In addition, simulation studies are also carried out to verify the performance of the proposed TD3-based controller.

Author Keywords: twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient

articleTitle: An Observable Degree-based Adaptive Federated Filtering for Bionic Integrated Navigation
abstract: Reliability is a pivotal problem in the bionic integrated navigation. To improve the accuracy and reliability of the inertial/polarization skylight/geomagnetic integrated navigation system suffering from abnormal data, an adaptive federated filter (AFF) based on observable degree is proposed. In this method, the observable degree is used to update time- varying information sharing factor. Particularly, it is used to dynamically adjust the measurement update process of the subfilter and the feedback weight of the main filter. On the basis of AFF, the integrated architecture of the bionic integrated navigation system is designed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed AFF is verified by simulation. The accuracy, stability of the bionic integrated navigation system can be effectively improved under abnormal sensor data.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Control for Consensus Problems of Uncertain Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: In this paper, we consider the consensus problem of distributed multi-agent systems with nonlinear dynamics and disturbances. The underlying system is described based upon the stochastic communication network topology. To solve this problem, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning-based method that converts the consensus problem with multiple nonlinear agents into one learning target and automatically learns effective strategies. The actor-critic method is adopted for updating learning policies. Moreover, we design a distributed communication method to ensure that each agent in the multi-agent system can obtain consensus information. Two examples are presented to show the effectiveness and potential of the proposed design technique.

articleTitle: Asymptotic Attitude Tracking Control for Uncertain Spacecraft With Multiple Disturbances: A Composite Anti-Disturbance Approach
abstract: This paper considers the attitude tracking problem of a rigid spacecraft in the presence of both uncertain inertia parameters and multiple disturbances. A novel robust adaptive anti-disturbance control scheme is proposed to achieve high-precision attitude tracking. The design of the composite control scheme integrates both the disturbance rejection approach, adaptive control and robust integral of sign error (RISE) method. The attitude tracking error is proved to asymptotically converge to zero and the control inputs remain continuous. The effectiveness of the proposed control scheme is validated by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Online Tensor Decomposition for Hyperspectral Data Representation
abstract: Tensor is a natural representation of visual data, such as hyperspectral image data. Other than vector representation based feature extraction methods, tensor-based representation methods are more informative. Most existing data representation methods only work on vector spaces which are implemented by stacking the original tensor elements into a long vector. However, the vectorization will inevitably lost the underlying structural information and lead to high computational complexity. In order to reduce the memory requirements, we proposed an online tensor decomposition (OTD) method for hyperspectral image feature extraction. It does not require to load the whole tensor data set into main memory, and with the insertion of new tensor samples, it can update projection matrices incrementally, which is desirable for large data sets. In the experiments, the proposed method was applied into the task of apple hyperspectral data classification.
