The Rijke tube system is mapped as a stable target system by the invertible transformation. The simulation verifies that the system stabilizes under the designed control law.

articleTitle: Multi-Agents Based Safe Path Planning of Autonomous Mobile Robots in Smart Factories
abstract: In the smart factory, multiple autonomous mobile robots (AMR) need to work together, which brings the problem of path conflicts. In addition, the smart factory should be able to handle the collaborative work with people, in order to plan the path reasonably without stopping the robot and ensure the safety of people. Hence, real-time control should be guaranteed, and the control algorithm needs to be robust and fast enough in order to ensure the safety of the planned path of AMR. Based on the characteristics of the smart factory, this paper presents a novel approach based on the avoidance vector field, which can realize the collision avoidance between each AMR and the dynamic intruder. A digital simulation platform is constructed to valid the effect of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Research of Wireless Power Transfer System for Animal Robot
abstract: The battery capacity of the animal robot neural stimulator is relatively small. In order to avoid frequent battery replacements affecting the results of the nerve electric stimulation experiment, the paper proposes a coupled magnetic resonance wireless power transmission system for animal robot. The receiving coil of the system needs to be placed on the animal. In order not to hinder the movement of the animal, a smaller-sized coil is selected. At the same time, so as to ensure the uninterrupted supply of electric energy, a multi-transmitter system is adopted. Based on the equivalent circuit theory, this paper first establishes the equivalent circuit model of single-transmitter system and multi-transmitter system, and analyzes output power and power transmission efficiency of systems. Then using MATLAB/Simulink to analyze the impact of the transmission distance, offset angle and offset distance on the systems. Finally, a coil model is built in High Frequency Structure Simulator, and the magnetic field distribution of the coils is simulated to further verify the size of the system power. The results show that maximum output power of multi-transmitter system is higher than that of single-transmitter system, and transmission distance of the multi-transmitter system is longer.

articleTitle: Coordinate transformation and connection feature for Skeleton-based action recognition
abstract: Graph structure is an important part of Graph convolutional networks (GCNs), which can reflect the connection between each nodes of non-Euclidean data. A connection feature between nodes is hidden in graph structure, which can provide additional spatial features that represent the relationship between human joints. However many GCNs-based methods ignore these spatial features. We put forward a connection feature extraction module, which can obtain implicit connection between human joints, and extract the implicit spatial features from the structural connection and implicit connection of human joints. In order to enhance the temporal representation, we propose a long-range frame-difference feature extraction module. Furthermore, we also propose a coordinate transformation module, which can map joint from Cartesian coordinates to spherical coordinates to extract more representative features. Experiments show that our method outperforms several advanced methods.

articleTitle: Distributed Event-Triggered Impulsive Consensus Control Strategy for Heterogeneous Multiagent Systems
abstract: The distributed event-triggered impulsive (DETI) consensus control problem for heterogeneous multiagent systems (HMS) is investigated in this paper. Based on the DETI control methodology, some sufficient conditions are presented to guarantee the consensus of HMS by using Lyapunov theory. Different from basic impulsive control algorithm, two event-triggered conditions to obtain the impulsive time instants rather than fixed sampling are adopted, the control input only occurs when the measurement error exceeds the threshold. As the updating frequency of controller is decreased, the energy consumption by the controller can also be reduced. In the end, simulation results are given to demonstrate the performance of DETI control methodology.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Switching Control Strategy for Mixed Traffic at Freeway On-Ramps: A Cyber-Physical Perspective
abstract: Since the ramp merging zone have consistently witnessed potential conflicts between on-ramp vehicles and mainline vehicles, ramp metering becomes a key element of advanced demand and traffic management strategy for freeways. Moreover, mixed traffic will be the main form of transportation in the next few years. At the same time, the control methods could be applied in homogeneous traffic might not be applied in mixed traffic. In summary, in order to improve the safety of the ramp merging zone, it is necessary to study the control algorithm of CAV. In this paper, we proposed an event-triggered switching control method to optimize the traffic situation of the mixed traffic in the merging zone. The method could avoid unnecessary braking and optimize traffic. Numerical simulation results show our method could be applied in mixed traffic situation. Impact of penetration rate and platoon length are also be researched.

articleTitle: Improved RRT Algorithm for Field Environment Tends to Smooth Path
abstract: RRT algorithm is a widely used method for path planning. The 3D path planning of mobile robots in the field environment tends to be flat. An improved RRT algorithm is proposed. In view of the particularity of the field environment, considering the limitation of the maximum turning angle and the maximum pitch angle of the mobile robot, a new node acceptance criterion is proposed. The acceptance criteria of the new node takes into account the changes in the altitude of the field terrain, the flatness of the path, and the mobility constraints of the mobile robot itself. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the improved method. Under the premise of avoiding mountains, valleys and rugged terrain, the required planning path can be generated to ensure the safety of the mobile robot.

articleTitle: Speed Control of a Biomimetic Robotic Fish Based on Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control
abstract: This paper proposes a speed control method for a biomimetic robotic fish based on linear active disturbance rejection control. Inspired by a bluefin tuna in nature, a robotic fish with a two-joint propulsive mechanism and a crescent-shaped caudal fin is first designed. Thereafter, for a steady forward swimming speed, a speed control framework based on the linear form of active disturbance rejection control method is proposed, where the oscillation frequency of the caudal fin is adopted to regulate the swimming speed. Meanwhile, a swimming speed estimation approach based on the oscillation period is provided to effectively reduce the phenomenon of swimming speed fluctuation. Finally, both simulation and experiment results illustrate that the proposed method is effective for the speed control of robotic fish.

articleTitle: Stewart-Inspired Posture Control for a UAV Undertaking Platform Based on Dynamic Model Predictive Control
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy and dynamic characteristics of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) undertaking platform with Stewart mechanism, a posture control strategy based on dynamic model predictive control algorithm is proposed in this paper. First, the dynamics of the Stewart platform is analyzed, and the state space expression of the dynamic model of the Stewart platform is established. Then, the algorithm based on the dynamic model predictive control is proposed, and the model predictive controller is designed. Finally, a simulation model of the UAV undertaking platform is established, the parameters of the model predictive controller are tuned, and the undertaking platform pose control simulation experiment is carried out. Physical experiments are performed to compare the control effects of traditional PID control and dynamics-based model predictive control on the undertaking platform.The results show that the model predictive control method based on dynamics can effectively improve the control accuracy and dynamic characteristics of the UAV undertaking platform.

articleTitle: Image Self-Generation Based Defect Detection Method for Train Brake Pad
abstract: The brake pads of trains will inevitably wear out with use. The most common defect is the wear, missing or damage of the brake pad’s friction block. This will directly affect the braking performance of the train and lead to potential risks to the safety of train operation. In order to detect defects on train brake pads with insufficient defect samples, an algorithm based on an image self-generation mechanism is proposed. This algorithm first identifies the brake pads at different locations in multi-view complete images of the bottom of the train. Then, utilizing multiple encoder-decoder combinations obtained by learning on normal samples, the algorithm can automatically generate defective samples and add them to the discriminator training for defect diagnosis. Experiments on real train brake pad data show that the proposed algorithm has higher performance and more usability than other advanced methods.

articleTitle: Cooperative Tracking Control for Multiple Robots Based on self-structuring neural networks
abstract: In this paper, a cooperative tracking control strategy is proposed for multiple robots with uncertainties. The barrier Lyapunov function (BLF) is adopted to solve the problem of time-varying consistency error constraints and improve the robustness of the cooperative control. The self-structured method combined with the adaptive neural network (NN) is used to estimate the complex uncertainty dynamics and avoid the excessive computational burden. Under the proposed control strategy, the consistency error does not violate the predefined time-varying constraint bounds, and the asymptotic cooperative tracking can be achieved. All signals of the closed-loop system are proved to be bounded via Lyapunov analysis. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated by simulation results.

articleTitle: A symmetric alternating direction method of multipliers for controlling the movement of multiple trains on a railway line
abstract: We consider the design of control inputs for multiple trains on a single railway line with several stations. A discrete time system model is firstly established to approximate the dynamics of a single moving train. Combining this with the headway constraints between adjacent trains and the station punctuality constraints, a distributed optimal control problem is formulated for the design of control inputs for multiple trains on a single railway line. We then propose an algorithm based on the framework of symmetric alternating direction multiplier to solve the distributed optimal control problem. The pseudocode of the algorithm is finally provided for the interested reader.

articleTitle: The Mechanical Design and Control of a Master-Slave Catheter Interventional Surgical Robot
abstract: Interventional therapy has become the best way to treat cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases due to its advantages over other treatment methods, and has gradually become the "gold standard" for the treatment of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases. In order to obtain higher surgical accuracy and stability, and reduce the doctor’s exposure time under X-rays during the operation. This paper proposes a new type of 3-DOF master-slave catheter interventional surgical robot. The continuum manipulator at the end of the robot can achieve bending in two directions, and accurate positioning of the target point can be achieved. The kinematics, mechanics model and its master-slave mapping relationship were established, and the accuracy of the established model was verified through experiments. In vitro experiments were performed on the left atrium model to verify the feasibility of the system.

articleTitle: Target Lure Guidance in Active Aircraft Defense
abstract: The active aircraft defense scenario includes three entities, namely an attacking missile, a target aircraft and a defending missile. In this scenario, the attacking missile aims to intercept the target, and meanwhile the target launches the defender to impact the attacking missile. The cooperative guidance laws for the target-defender team have been widely investigated, which makes target help the defender to intercept the attacking missile with appropriate control effort. In this paper, the lure maneuver of target is considered, and with this maneuver, the defender can intercept the attacking missile with zero control effort. The missile-target pursuit-evasion engagement is analyzed, and the conclusion shows that the general pursuit guidance laws try to make the line-of-sight (LOS) angle rate converge to a very small value. Based on this conclusion, the sufficient condition for successful capture is established, and the target lure guidance law is derived by using Lyapunov function and fixed-time convergence theory. The key point of target lure guidance is that the target use lure maneuver to attract the attacking missile, in order to make the defender-missile LOS angle rate converge to zero. This guarantees the defender impacts the attacking missile. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the target lure guidance law.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Control of Autonomous Vehicle with Double Layer Controller
abstract: Aiming at improving the yaw stability of unmanned ground vehicles during high-speed steering, a double layer control architecture based on feedback linearization and model predictive control is proposed. The upper controller uses the model predictive control algorithm and the lower controller uses the feedback linearization method. This architecture makes full use of the performance advantages of the two controllers and improves the accuracy of the controller model and the path tracking performance while ensuring the real-time performance of the calculation. Finally, the effectiveness of this control framework is verified by the joint simulation of MATLAB/Simulink and CarSim, which proves that the performance of this controller is higher than that of the single-layer dynamic MPC controller.

articleTitle: Finite-time passivity control of reaction-diffusion genetic regulatory networks
abstract: In this study, the finite-time passivity control of reaction-diffusion genetic regulatory networks (GRNs) with time-varying delays is concerned in the case of Dirichlet boundary conditions. The derivatives of time-varying delays are assumed have upper and lower bounds. In order to analyze the finite-time passivity of GRNs, an appropriate Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional (LKF) is constructed, which involves some triple and quadruple integrals. The derivatives of these integrals are handled by taking full advantage of the inequality technique. The primary idea of this article is to present finite-time boundedness analysis for GRNs firstly. Then, the finite-time passivity analysis and passivity control are investigated. Meanwhile the explicit expression of the state feedback controller gain matrices are proposed. Finally, the feasibility of the obtained theoretical results is illustrated by a numerical example.

articleTitle: Framework of the Tourism Comprehensive Service Platform Based on Blockchain Technology
abstract: Blockchain is considered to be one of the most promising transformational technologies in the era of digital economy, but it is still in the initial stage in tourism industry. Toward this end, in this paper, we put forward a systematic framework of tourism comprehensive service platform based on the blockchain technology. We first analyze the problems of the current tourism industry and the value of blockchain to it. Then, we introduce the proposed platform in detail, including its component modules and advantages. Lastly, we discuss the limitations and development trends of the platform. This paper is aimed at providing helpful guidance and reference for future research efforts.

articleTitle: Multi-person coded brain-computer interface based on steady-state visual evoked potential
abstract: Previous studies have made great efforts to extend available frequencies of EEG signals to increase the number of targets in steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP)-based brain-computer interface (BCI), but most of them focused on single-person paradigms. Inspired by the idea of binary coding, we proposed a multi-person SSVEP-coded BCI paradigm, which could increase the number of targets by the cooperation of multiple participants. Fourteen subjects participated in this study, and the performance of the paradigm was evaluated by using an online two-subject cooperative experiment. The results showed that the average online accuracy of 92.83% and an information transmission rate (ITR) of 86.88 bits/min could be achieved with the proposed multi-person SSVEP-coded BCI. Compared with traditional one-person BCI paradigm, the proposed paradigm could increase the number of generated commands exponentially with the number of participants while without decrease in accuracy, which is of great significance for extending the application of BCIs.

articleTitle: Neighboring Optimal Control Laws Based On Radau Pseudospectral Method
abstract: This paper develops a feedback control law for regulating nonlinear time variant system about reference trajectories, and it is applied to the guidance for reusable launch vehicles entry. The neighboring optimal feedback controller presented in this paper is based on the two-point boundary value problem on discretization pesudospectral points. The feedback control laws in this paper can be calculated without solving the matrix Ricaati differential equations, construction of transition matrices or any explicit integration. This facilitates neighboring optimal control laws is calculated in real-time. A numerical example of a hypersonic vehicle entry problem demonstrates the effectiveness of neighboring optimal control method.

articleTitle: Research on Simulation of Hot Cell Ventilation Control System Based on COMSOL and MATLAB
abstract: The hot cell is the core equipment in the nuclear chemical treatment process. Before the construction of hot cell, it is often necessary to carry out simulation verification of the ventilation control strategy to ensure the effectiveness of the control strategy. To solve this problem, COMSOL is used to build the simulation model of the hot cell to simulate the ventilation condition of the real hot cell, and the simulation process is controlled online with MATLAB. Firstly, the boundary conditions and structure of the hot cell are analyzed, and the multi-physical field model is established. Then, the principle and implementation method of data transmission and sampling control in the co-simulation are studied. Finally, the co-simulation between COMSOL and MATLAB is implemented, and the simulation results are drawn in MATLAB. The simulation results verify the effectiveness of the ventilation control strategy under typical working conditions, which has certain reference for the design of the actual hot cell ventilation control system.

articleTitle: The Control Design of Space Flying Net Robot System Based on RBF Network
abstract: Space Flying Net Robot System (SFNRS) is a new capture method of space debris. In this paper, the SFNRS dynamic equations are established by using the lumped mass method. The previous studies about controller design assumed that the mass of the maneuvering unit in SFNRS is known and a constant while it is unknown in fact. In addition, the upper boundary of tension in the space net is often assumed as a known constant, but it is difficult to get the value. In this paper, the radial basis function (RBF) network is used to design a controller in order to overcome the shortcomings above. Finally, the simulation is carried out to verify the effectiveness and the robustness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Silent Speech Recognition based on sEMG and EEG Signals
abstract: In recent years, silent speech recognition attracts attention with particular interests either using surface electromyogram (sEMG) or electroencephalogram (EEG), but both have limitations. This paper proposes to combine sEMG and EEG signals for recognizing silent speech. Data are first preprocessed to get clean signals followed by extracting sEMG and EEG respectively. Then time domain features and entropy features are separately extracted from the dataset, which are classified by a typical random forest classifier. Feature fusion and decision fusion are also researched to explore their effects on recognition. Our experimental results show that entropy features play a certain role in recognition, and the second level decision fusion obtains a better result with a correct rate of 86.53%. It may remind more researchers of combining EEG and sEMG in this field.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Optimization of Path-Constrained Switched Systems Using the Modified ε-Constraint Method
abstract: This paper considers the multi-objective optimization of path-constrained switched systems. A multi-objective dynamic algorithm is proposed for locating approximated local Pareto solutions with guaranteed feasibility and finite convergence. The algorithm iteratively solves modified ε-constraint problems to avoid generating weak Pareto solutions, which are formulated into semi-infinite programs embedded with ordinary differential equations by performing the control vector parameterization technique. The guaranteed feasibility is attained by enforcing the path constraints at discretized time points with a restriction parameter on the right-hand side. The main advantage of the proposed multi-objective dynamic algorithm is that it generates solutions with specified tolerances of Pareto optimality, and ensures that path constraints are not violated at any point of the whole time period.

articleTitle: Apply Uncertainty to Address the Problem Caused by Incomplete Information in Training Data
abstract: Machine learning and deep learning have been applied to various fields. In general, training a model requires a large amount of data to make the model more accurate and reliable. But in practice, training data is usually limited, which leads to the problem of incomplete information and may ultimately cause the model to give some wrong results when facing new data. In order to avoid the unreliable results of the model being adopted by people as much as possible, the trained model should not only output an absolute result, but also give the confidence of it. In this paper, Bayesian approach is applied to neural network with dropout to solve the regression problem with incomplete information in training data. The model trained with limited data can give the mean and variance of the output simultaneously, where variance indicates how confident the model is in its output. Finally, the experiments verify the effectiveness of this method and give useful experience for the structure and parameter selection of the model when setting up the model.

articleTitle: Classification and Implementation of Relevance Data Based on Address Text
abstract: Tasks based on address text are commonly seen in real life, such as location-based services based on geographic information systems, rapid localization and positioning systems for emergencies, and alignment of different address information systems. This article introduces the solutions to the classification problems of address text by comparing different models of different parameters, such as pre-training + nezha + rdropout and pre-training + nezha + swa + rdropout, in the classification of address information, obtaining different model effects. After using rdropout, it also shows a faster training speed and convergence speed.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of BCM-Oriented Automatic Test System
abstract: Body control module (BCM) is one of the important control units in automobile electronic control module. To ensure the accuracy and reliability of BCM, so as to ensure the overall quality and function of automobiles. Aiming at the low efficiency and poor compatibility of BCM testing, the hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test system is built based on National Instruments (NI) platform, and the experimental management interface is built by Verist and software. It is convenient to calibrate and observe the test signal. At the same time, based on functional test cases, test sequences are built by using TestStand software, and automatic testing is realized on the premise of meeting test specifications and requirements. The actual test results show that: the test system can accurately and reliably complete the BCM test task, and significantly improves the test efficiency and test coverage of the BCM.

articleTitle: A Power Load Shedding Strategy in Active Distribution Network Considering User Satisfaction
abstract: The development of demand response (DR) technology provides a new approach for the optimal removal of controllable load in the distribution network. The traditional load shedding scheme is relatively extensive, the load power is directly cut off in this scheme, which will worsen the relationship between power grid companies and users. In this paper, an active distribution network (ADN) load shedding model considering user satisfaction is proposed. Taking the maximum user satisfaction and the minimum distribution network DR cost as the objective function, the min-max standardization method is used to simplify the multi-objective function. The second-order cone relaxation technique is used to linearize the original mixed-integer nonlinear model and establish a mixed-integer second-order cone programming model. The results show that the multi-objective active distribution network load shedding model can effectively reduce the DR cost and improve the voltage stability.

articleTitle: Flight Control for Three-surface Morphing Aircraft Using Linear Quadratic Regulator Design Based on Stochastic Robustness Analysis
abstract: This paper proposes a robust linear quadratic regulator (LQR) Design based on stochastic robustness analysis (SRA) for the stability control of a three-surface morphing aircraft to resist the uncertainties and disturbances caused by both its morphing and external environment. Based on the Kane method, a dynamic model is built. Then, the linear variable parameter (LPV) model in the morphing process is obtained. After that a robust LQR controller is proposed based on SRA, while control allocation (CA) method is applied to reduce the hinge moment. The results of comparative simulation demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Double-Joint Motion Planning Method in Park based on High-Definition Map
abstract: In order to solve the turning problem in narrow space, Double-Joint Method is proposed in this paper. The spiral has a continuous curvature, but rarely considers road boundary and shape constraints. On the other hand, High-Definition map provides prior information of road for motion planning. Double-Joint Method utilizes road boundary and curvature of map to determine the target area and a series of pseudo target points of motion planning, generates a series of path respectively, and then design the cost function for selection. Above all, path generation employs two joints for shape determination of cubic spiral by designing the objective function and combining road structure information. The method adds a joint near turning to allow the path more flexible without increasing the degree of the curve. VTD-ROS simulation platform is built to verify. Theoretical and simulation results display proposed method can guide the vehicle turning right in narrow space to obtain a larger turning radius through lane borrow without loss of smoothness. And it is feasible to sacrifice the accuracy of reaching target points to suit special scenario.

articleTitle: Identification of bad measurements in power system from historical measurement data
abstract: Bad measurements identification is an important problem for system monitoring and controlling in electric power system. In recent years, some studies have shown that the bad measurements can be corrected by some state estimation methods. However, most of the studies mainly focus on a single measurement snapshot but ignoring the possibility of the continuous measurement errors existence in historical measurement data. In this paper, we propose an algorithm for identification of bad measurements from historical measurements. And considering the different occurrence pattern of bad measurements, we propose a more common situation of bad measurements which is a continuous error in multi-snapshots of measurements rather than a single one. In our method, we use a least-square optimization model as the basic estimator to get the initial results of measurement residuals. After that we set a searching strategy based on hypothesis test and normalized measurement residuals to find a continuous errors in historical measurement data. Then we update the computation of the basic estimator to correct the biases in state variables caused by bad measurements, which lead to more precise results of system states. The performance of the developed identification algorithm is demonstrated and compared with conventional estimation methods based on experiments using IEEE 30-bus systems.

articleTitle: A Method of Electricity Meter LCD Screen Defect Detecting Based on Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: In order to quickly and accurately detect the display defects of electric meter LCD screen, this paper proposed an electric meter LCD screen defect detecting method based on convolutional neural network (CNN). First, a horizontal straight line of LCD screen frame is found by LSD line detection method for tilt correction. Second, the LCD area is positioned by normalized correlation matching of the corrected image. Then, the accurate positions of the meter characters are located by the characters position information generated by a template annotation tool. Finally, a CNN is used to perform character defect detecting and OCR recognizing on the segmented meter characters. The experimental results show that the accuracy of the method of positioning and detecting the LCD screen characters is about 99%. At the same time, the CNN has an OCR recognition function, which can accurately identify the meter LCD screen characters.

articleTitle: Multi-Dilated Hierarchical Filter Based 3D U-Net for Multi-Modal Brain Tumor Segmentation
abstract: Brain tumor segmentation is an essential task in the field of medical image analysis. Brain lesions (e.g. gliomas) have various shapes, sizes, and locations between different patients, making it challenging localizing and doing other tasks. For a single tumor, the essential contextual information may inhabit much larger regions than itself. Multi-scale feature representation can improve model generalization. However, existing U-Net models perform with layer-wise features. In this paper, a 3D multi-dilated hierarchical filter module is proposed based on hierarchical multi-scale strategy and multi-fiber strategy. The main points of our proposed module are multi hierarchical filter connection and multi-branch dilated convolutions. Besides, the proposed module is applied with a 3D U-Net. The results of experiments on the validation subset of BraTS2018 dataset show the efficacy of the proposed module.

articleTitle: Design of Trigger Circuit Applied to Sectional Switch of Linear Motor
abstract: This article introduces a trigger circuit to turn on the plate-type thyristor electronic switch, which is used in the segmentation of high-speed long-stator linear motors. The trigger circuit collects the bus current signal to generate a high-level pulse signal with a time of 100 us to turn on the thyristor, and the pulse signal generation position can follow the point where the bus current signal is zero, that is, zero-crossing triggering. Finally, the trigger pulse waveform and the current waveform after the conduction are measured through experiments, and the expected effect can be achieved.

articleTitle: Speed Prediction of Cutter Suction Dredger Mud Pump Based on Cuckoo Algorithm Optimized Support Vector Machine Algorithm
abstract: In the development of cutter suction dredgers, the improvement of dredging efficiency and energy utilization has always been the mainstream development task. This paper accurately predicts the setting value of the speed of the mud pump for direct control according to the current construction environment parameters and the optimized value of concentration and flow rate to improve the dredging efficiency. The support vector machine algorithm (CS-SVM) improved by the cuckoo algorithm is used to predict the speed of the mud pump, and the cuckoo algorithm is used to optimize the selection of the penalty factor C and the kernel function parameters in the prediction and fitting process of the support vector machine. In order to verify the effectiveness of this method, the predicted output of CS-SVM is compared with the actual measured speed of mud pump, and the comparison is made with BP neural network. The simulation results show that CS-SVM has a relatively accurate prediction ability and a short calculation time. The prediction output can provide the construction personnel with a direct reference to the setting value of the speed of the mud pump to improve the efficiency of dredging.

articleTitle: Initial Alignment Method for SINS of UAV Based on Digital Filter Pretreatment
abstract: The two-stage method, which is divided into coarse alignment and fine alignment, is a traditional initial alignment method for SINS (Strapdown inertial navigation system, SINS). First, the coarse alignment is carried out based on the transformation relationship between the geographic information of the earth and the output of inertial measurement unit, and then the fine alignment is carried out based on optimal estimation. However, this method can mainly solve the alignment problem under angular interference. Aiming at in-motion alignment for SINS of UAVs (Unmanned aerial vehicle, UAV) under linear interference, this paper introduced the idea of digital filter and designed the digital filter by analyzing the frequency characteristic of useful signal. Then the reference velocity information is filtered to realize isolation of linear interference at specific frequency. Thus, the in-motion alignment problem under the combined action of angular interference and linear interference is effectively solved. Finally, numerical simulation results show the effectiveness of the above method.

articleTitle: Distributed optimal cooperative control for nonlinear multi-agent systems with input saturation and full-state constraint
abstract: The issue of distributed optimal cooperative control for nonlinear multi-agent systems (MASs) with input saturation and full-state constraint is discussed in this paper. Different with the traditional states constraint, the dynamic and asymmetric constraint conditions are considered and a barrier function is employed. Besides, a smooth function is constructed to map the input saturation. The adaptive dynamic programming (ADP) is utilized to seek distributed optimal control policy and the predefine cooperative performance index function is estimated by a critic neural network (CNN), in which a weight updating law is proposed to learn the ideal weights. The closed-loop system and weight estimation errors are proved to be uniformly ultimately bounded(UUB). Finally, simulation results testifies to the viability of the design algorithm.

articleTitle: Behavior Recognition Algorithm Based on Key Points of Human Bones
abstract: Human behavior recognition method based on video image easily influenced by background factors with lead to recognition accuracy is not high, and in view of the traditional Shuangliu network needs computing optical flow chart in advance and consume large amounts of time and need a lot of space to store an image of a light flow, an improved fusion skeleton information and image information of human behavior recognition algorithm. The experimental results show that the algorithm can effectively improve the accuracy of behavior recognition in video, and improve the identification ability of time-dependent behaviors and approximate behaviors.

articleTitle: AI Graphical Programming Learning Platform for Children
abstract: In this era of rapid development of artificial intelligence, the truth of competition in the future is the talent. Countries all over the world attach great importance to the programming and artificial intelligence education of children. In the future, the theoretical development and practical application of this emerging field will usher in a period of rapid development. This paper presents an artificial intelligence graphical programming learning platform based on Jetson Nano, which combines artificial intelligence education with modular software programming, provides students with a more open, intelligent, and interesting programming environment through the cross-platform development mode of "cloud service + intelligent hardware", and adopts visual programming to reduce the difficulty of artificial intelligence programming. The platform can fully tap learning resources, reduce education costs, and make artificial intelligence education more intuitive and humanized.

articleTitle: Multilane Energy-efficient Predictive Cruise Control Using Mixed-integer Programming
abstract: Vehicle to vehicle (V2V) communication have enabled the obtainment of the information and the prediction of the traffic conditions. In this paper, a model predictive control (MPC) based algorithm is proposed to control the host vehicle to drive more energy-efficient and faster. Multilane Energy-efficient predictive cruise control (PCC) algorithm establishes a mixed-integer programming model which can make the lane-change decision and generate the optimal acceleration in a look forward horizon. Ideally, by updating data and continuously implementing algorithms, the host vehicle can always be in an optimal state. Simulation results show that PCC can find the optimal lane and acceleration accurately, which verifies its practicability.

articleTitle: The Policy-Making of Evacuation Route Based on Neural Network for Cruise Ship
abstract: The cruise ship is the largest mobile building in the world, and some cruise ships can accommodate more than 7000 people at the same time, then the emergency evacuation of cruise ships is very important for safe navigation. Usually, the ship designers simulate the behavior of people when fire accidents happen, and the optimal evacuation routes in the simulation are used as the evacuation policies. However, the offline optimal evacuation routes are different from the real evacuation situations. In order to get the real-time optimal evacuation routes in a short time, this paper uses neural network to decide how to evacuate people when the fire situation changes. It uses a lot of evacuation routes to train the neural network, and the train makes the neural network learn how to move from dangerous areas to safe areas facing different situations. The neural network is trained offline and outputs evacuation policy online to guide people on how to evacuate to the safe areas. Although many different situations are outside the training samples, the neural network knows how to make decisions due to its generalization ability. The simulation results show that the neural network is an effective policy-making machine for evacuation routes of cruise ships.

articleTitle: Onboard Capability Assessment and Decision-making Method of Launch Vehicle
abstract: The propulsion system failure of launch vehicle during flight will lead to capability degradation or even a crash. To quantitatively indicate the capacity degradation, an onboard capability assessment method based on height constraint in three force balancing state is proposed in this paper. An analytical method of the optimal inclination angle of local acceleration under the quasi-equilibria flight condition and an approach to evaluate velocity increment are put forward to preliminarily estimate the residual flight capability of rocket. Then mathematical simulation shows the capability assessment and control decision can be made in a rapid, simple and reliable way based on the method proposed in this paper, which has advantages of rapid computation speed, strong engineering practicability and provides the theoretical basis for future research of a rapid onboard generation algorithm of trajectory.

Author Keywords: Onboard Capability Assessment and Decision-making Method

articleTitle: A New Constrained Cost Value Iteration for Optimal Control of Discrete-Time Nonlinear Systems
abstract: In this paper, a new constrained cost value iteration (CCVI) adaptive dynamic programming (ADP) algorithm is developed to solve optimal control problems with constrained cost function. The CCVI algorithm is initialized by a feasible control law, and the cost function of this initial feasible control constitutes the constraint condition in the policy update step. The convergence and optimality of the CCVI are analyzed. Furthermore, the feasibility of any iterative control law and the on-line evolving control law are proven. It is emphasized that the feasibility of any iterative control law and the on-line evolving control law guarantee that the CCVI algorithm can be used in situations where the cost function constraint is extremely important. Finally, a simulation example is given to verify the effect of the developed algorithm.

articleTitle: An improved Auxiliary Classifier Generated Adversarial network for Bearing Fault Diagnosis
abstract: The generative adversarial network (GAN) and its derivatives has been applied in data generation, especially auxiliary classifier GAN (ACGAN) provides an alternative solution for fault diagnosis under the condition of unbalanced dataset. In this paper, aiming at the problem of training instability and gradients optimization in training ACGAN model, we propose an improved ACGAN to improve data-enhanced capabilities and the classification accuracy of class-imbalanced fault data. In particular, the improved ACGAN produces more convincing generated samples by improving the measurement mode of distribution distances and enhance the speed and stability of training process by splitting the model structure. Finally, the fault dataset for rolling bearings from CWRU are used to confirm the validity of the proposed model. Experimental result shows that the improved ACGAN performs better when comparing to the original ACGAN across several evaluation metrics.

articleTitle: Collision-free Circle Formation Control for Mobile Robots with Velocity Constraints
abstract: Circle formation is a type of cooperative task for multiple mobile robots that attracts lots of attentions in both research work and engineering applications. In order to be successfully applied to robots, many factors, such as collision avoidance, velocity or acceleration constraints, distributed execution, should be considered in design of circle formation control laws. However, few works have integrated them all. This paper design a circle formation control law taking all the above features into account. Despite the strong nonlinearity of the law due to the introduced hyperbolic tangent function for velocity constraints, the convergence and collision avoidance are all proved. The effectiveness of the law is demonstrated by simulations.

articleTitle: Design of Ripple Motor Current Signal Test System Based on LabVIEW
abstract: As the so called ripple signal is critical for the entire anti-pinch protection system based on ripple, the quality along with the stability of such a signal during the motors lifetime must be deeply investigated before production part release. The window controller sets multiple parameters for the ripple current signal to evaluate whether the ripple motor is qualified. In order to obtain relevant parameters to determine the motor current signal, a ripple motor current signal test system based on LabVIEW software and hardware acquisition system is designed. Firstly, the test system hardware uses high-precision current probe and data acquisition cards to build a portable signal acquisition device. Secondly, using the idea of modular programming and functional design, it mainly realizes the functions of signal acquisition and recording, analysis and processing, storage and viewing. The core is to perform time-frequency domain analysis on the current signal to obtain the characteristic value of each parameter, then compare it with the motor standard value and display the test result to the interface in real time. Finally, the test results of PA5000H power analyzer are used as the standard for accuracy analysis, and the evaluation results of multiple tests of are evaluated to reach 100% consistent with correct results. The function of this test system also has the characteristics of strong scalability and easy operation.

articleTitle: RootMiner: A Rapid Root Cause Location Method for KPIs with Multi-Dimensional Attributes
abstract: Additive key performance indicators (KPI) with multi-dimensional attributes are important monitoring indicators in internet companies. When the anomaly occurs in the overall KPI, it is critical but challenging to locate the root cause of the anomaly. There are mainly two important challenges in the task. Firstly, it is difficult to locate the root causes in two typical scenarios: the amount of anomalies is not obvious and two kinds of abnormal variations interact. Secondly, the number of KPI attribute value combinations is huge, which requires higher real-time performance of the algorithm. In this paper, a robust and rapid root cause location approach, RootMiner, is proposed to address the above challenges. Firstly, a new evaluation function is adopted to achieve good results in more complex scenarios. Secondly, a multi-tree data structure as well as pre-pruning strategy is applied to improve the calculation efficiency. Based on real data set from Alibaba Cloud Computing, the experiment results show that RootMiner achieves a great improvement in effectiveness, with an average improvement of 40% compared with the state-of-the-art. The results also show that RootMiner reduces the runtime from 10s to 1s on average.

articleTitle: Adaptive boundary control of an Euler-Bernoulli beam subject to unknown tip load
abstract: This paper concentrates on adaptive boundary control of Euler-Bernoulli beams with unknown tip loads and distributed perturbations. An adaptive law is designed by using the boundary output signal to estimate the tip load. To inhibit the vibration of the beam, an adaptive boundary controller is presented by introducing the designed adaptive law. With the proposed controller, the uniform boundedness of the adaptive error and the beam system state are obtained. At the end, the validity and merits of the proposed method are simulated and demonstrated.

articleTitle: Iterative Learning Control for Accelerated Inhibition Effect of Initial State Error
abstract: An iterative learning control (ILC) with accelerated initial state correction is proposed for linear time-invariant systems with initial state deviations to improve tracking performance. Correction interval, which fallen sharply with the increasing of the iterations number, is designed for con- trolled object with any arbitrary initial state. In the correction interval, the initial state error is corrected by using the control algorithm, however in the outside of the interval, the control algorithm is same as the one without initial state error and realize zero error tracking of reference signal. The convergence of the proposed algorithm is proved in a paradigmatic sense. The designed ILC control method for LTI has better tracking performance by compared with the classical ILC control without initial state error. The numerical simulation verifies the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Camouflaged target tracking based on a scaleadaptive correlation filter algorithm
abstract: Considering the continuous development of intelligent technology and the wide application prospects of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), the target tracking technology will be applied in future combat. In order to deal with the complex battlefield environment and the scale change of the target during tracking, an improved scale-adaptive correlation filter algorithm based on fusion features is proposed to realize the tracking of military personnel. First, the fast histogram of oriented gradient (FHOG) features and the local binary pattern (LBP) features are adaptively weighted and fused to achieve the target location. Then the translation filter of kernelized correlation filters(KCF) and the scale filter of discriminative scale space tracking(DSST) are combined to comprehensively improve the calculation speed and scale adaptation performance of the algorithm and track the target in time. The experimental results prove the robustness and practicability of the proposed method, which can accurately track military targets in real time.

articleTitle: Variable Window Mechanism of Candidates for Map Matching
abstract: The ubiquitous popularization and deployment of mobile sensor technology has enabled GPS to observe and record vehicle states. Digital road maps as well as transport information of vehicles also has brought great convenience to intelligent transportation systems (ITS). However, raw GPS locations are usually too noisy and thus cannot be used directly by downstream applications. To alleviate the issue of location noise, map matching has been investigated to chronologically map a series of geographical GPS locations onto the actual road segments. In this paper, a variable window size for the candidate selection mechanism is introduced, which can confine the search region to optimize map matching process. We conducted experiments with a real-world road transport dataset and evaluated the performance to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Stability analysis of Markovian jump systems with delayed impulses
abstract: This paper addresses stability for Markovian jump systems with delayed impulses. The delayed impulse has a largely negative effect on the system stability and is hard to be studied. The main reason is that so many factors such as Markovian switching, impulse and time-varying delay, are simultaneously contained and make its analysis complicated but difficult. In order to analyse these factors clearly, some novel enlarging techniques are presented and used to establish LMI conditions ultimately. One numerical example is used to show the effectiveness and superiority of the methods.

articleTitle: Design of positioning and mapping system for space station mobile robot based on ROS
abstract: The extravehicular work, such as space station maintenance and outer-space exploration, is still very dangerous for the astronauts due to the adverse circumstance. Therefore, a mobile robot is developed and its function of positioning and mapping is also realized in ROS. The virtual prototype of robot is established by following the URDF patterns, and the control technology of robot main body and sensor system is programmed by visual C++, and map for the potential automatic navigation is then built by the Gmapping SLAM. This paper provides some useful references for robot autonomous navigation, obstacle avoidance and manipulator arrangement.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Human-Machine Safety System Based on Visual Perception
abstract: A human-machine safety system based on multi-target detection and tracking is proposed for the safety problems in the human-machine coexistence environment. For the motion state of pedestrians, the YOLOv5 detection algorithm and Deep SORT tracking algorithm are used to compare and study the effects of different activation functions and loss functions on the performance of neural networks, and the detection accuracy is improved by using Mish activation functions, and the motion trajectory and motion speed of pedestrians are obtained. To address the human-machine safety issue, the human-machine safety system model is proposed to establish the information feedback from vision processing to robot decision making and control robot motion decision. It is verified on the actual system and the goal of human-machine safety is achieved.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis of WTG-PV-ESS Microgrid System
abstract: Increasing the proportion of renewable energy connected to the grid is the one way to achieve "2030 carbon peak" and "2060 carbon neutral", but the intermittent, volatility and randomness of renewable energy output will bring severe challenges to the stable operation of the microgrid. Through reliability analysis, it can not only qualitatively describe the impact of renewable energy output on the microgrid reliability, but also give a quantitative basis for microgrid planning. Therefore, this paper first established a wind, solar, energy storage system model, and then introduced reliability indicators and written evaluation procedures as the basis for analysis. Finally, an example system was built with the improved IEEE-RBTS BUS6 F4 system to evaluate the changes in the proportion of photovoltaic capacity, the influence of wind and solar proportion rate and ESS capacity changes on system reliability. The results show that the combined effect of the wind and solar proportion rate and the ESS capacity will have a significant impact on the reliability of the system.

articleTitle: Research on Multiple model Method of Nonlinear System with Recurrent Neural Network
abstract: The multiple model method has achieved extensive results in nonlinear system research area for it can deal with problems such as relatively large set value changes, uncertainty, and sudden changes of control target etc. Simultaneously, with the rapid development of machine learnings, recurrent neural networks (RNN) have been widely used for modeling a general class of nonlinear systems. In this paper, a multiple model framework based on recurrent neural networks (RNN) is proposed, where the sub-model adopts the recurrent neural networks (RNN) network and global model is assembled with a hard switch. Finally, Computational implementation of the method and application to a chemical reactor example demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Robust Control for a Class of Nonlinear Systems Against Denial-of-Service Attacks
abstract: This paper explores the state-feedback control problem for a family of nonlinear systems subject to denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. The unknown nonlinearities and DoS attacks involved in the closed loop render the existing approaches for resilient control of linear systems or robust nonlinear control infeasible. A solution is provided by designing a novel robust control scheme together with a constraint-handling technique. Two technical lemmas are also given to establish the boundedness of the signals in the resulting control system. As a distinct property, our approach is flexible enough such that the system reaches a predefined steady state in a specified time after the occurrence of DoS attacks.

articleTitle: Optimal Allocation of DGs in Distribution System for Minimum Active Power Loss using Improved Firefly Algorithm
abstract: In modern power system, distributed generators (DGs) have become an effective method to reduce active power loss, improve voltage stability, etc.. In this paper, a new Improved Firefly Algorithm (IFA) is proposed to obtain optimal placement and capacity of DGs to improve power flow distribution and voltage stability, reduce active power loss in distribution system. Compared with the standard Firefly Algorithm (FA), the proposed IFA has better convergence speed and can obtain a smaller active power loss. In addition, the power loss sensitivity factors are introduced to steer the algorithm to seek the best position about the DGs. In order to verify the performance of IFA, IFA and FA are tested on the standard IEEE-33 and IEEE-69 systems to solve the problem of joint configuration optimization of multiple generators. The results of simulation show the active power loss of the distribution system decreases and the voltage stability of the system node improves. By comparing the results of the IFA and FA, a conclusion can be reached, the IFA is more effective and more suitable to reduce active power loss by reasonably allocating the capacity and placement of DGs than FA.

articleTitle: Research on Biological Disaster Early Warning and Decision Support System of Nuclear Power Plant
abstract: In view of the lack of effective early warning with high time-effectiveness and large-scale monitoring data in the water intake area of Binhai Nuclear Power station, this paper is committed to the study of early warning and decision support system of typical disaster-causing organisms in Binhai nuclear power station. On the basis of constructing three-dimensional monitoring system to comprehensively monitor the typical Marine environment and disaster-causing organisms in the water intake area of nuclear power station, The deep learning prediction model of disaster-causing biomass and the prediction model of disaster-causing biological trajectory were established, and the disaster-causing biological warning and decision support system was finally constructed. According to the predicted results of biomass and migration trajectory, the system can realize the classification and early warning of discomfent-causing biological disasters and provide disposal methods. Finally, the system can publish the disaster through webGIS humancomputer interaction interface and wechat service release. Experiments show that the system can effectively assist the cold source department of nuclear power plant to carry out biological disaster prevention and control work.

Author Keywords: Prediction of nuclear disaster causing organisms

articleTitle: Weapon-target Assignment Based on Improved Particle Swarm Optimization for Different Allocation Criteria
abstract: In this paper, weapon-target assignment (WTA) mathematical models for various allocation criteria are built, and a fast WTA optimization algorithm is proposed. By introducing the target threat assessment, missile interception probability and target time-to-go, five allocation criteria are designed, which are i) maximum intercept probability criterion, ii) reaching intercept probability threshold criterion, iii) fast and high-probability intercept criterion, iv) maximum cost-effectiveness criterion, and v) target-threat-priority based stochastic assignment criterion. Based on those criteria, the WTA problem is formulated as a zero-one integer programming problem, with considering multiple assignment constraints. Furthermore, an improved heuristic-swarm-intelligence optimization algorithm is proposed, which combines the particle swarm optimization and the simulated annealing to solve WTA problem efficiently. Also, the performance indexes are built for evaluating WTA optimization results. Numerous simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed optimization algorithm, and show its advantage in searching global optimal solution. Meanwhile, each criterion achieves best performance in a specified scenario with considering related task requirements and weapon resources.

articleTitle: An improved ESN with three reservoirs for time series prediction
abstract: In this paper, an improved echo state network with three different reservoirs in serial connection(TR-ESN) is proposed for time series prediction. For obtaining the internal characteristics, The hidden layer of TR-ESN can alternately amplify and extract the input signal. A sufficient condition is given to ensure that the TR-ESN architecture has the echo state property. The gradient descent method is used to optimize eight parameters. Finally, simulation Experiment results show that TRESN can significantly improve prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Fast Distributed Stochastic Nesterov Gradient Descent Algorithm for Image Classification
abstract: Based on stochastic gradient descent, this paper presents a fast distributed stochastic Nesterov gradient descent algorithm denoted by SFDGND, which can effectively solve the problem of image classification with distributed neural nets. The proposed SFDGND algorithm allows data to be randomly and evenly assigned to agents. Each agent updates its parameters with a local subset of data, thus enabling parallel computation. Finally, we compare the effectiveness of the proposed stochastic algorithm for training distributed neural nets optimizing problems. The experimental results are implemented on MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets, which clearly demonstrates that SFDNGD algorithm performs well in practical applications and compares favorably to the existed algorithms.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Prediction and Health Status Estimation Based on Joint-Loss Convolution Neural Networks
abstract: Remaining Useful life (RUL) prediction and health status (HS) estimation are two key tasks of predictive maintenance, which are previously treated as two separate tasks. This setting ignores the correlation between the two tasks. In this paper, the joint-loss convolutional neural network is proposed to capture the common features between two related problems. The architecture realizes the joint learning of RUL prediction and HS estimation of aerospace engines by sharing part of the network and parameters, while retaining the output layers of different tasks. Meanwhile, in the network optimization stage, We build a joint-loss (JL) function to learn the common features of RUL prediction and HS estimation, and enhance the generalization ability of the model. Then, in order to reduce the computational complexity of the network, a composite index was constructed based on the monotony and correlation to screen the sensor groups containing more degradation information. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method was verified on the C-MAPSS dataset. The results show that the proposed method can be used for the cross application of RUL prediction and HS estimation.

articleTitle: Improved Adaptive Neural Network Control of Rehabilitation Robot with Variable Load
abstract: This article presents an adaptive-adaptive radial basis function (RBF) neural network (AANNRBF) control strategy for lower limb rehabilitation robot (LLRR), which to adapts the uncertainty of the physical parameters caused by different patients or the same patient's muscle tension changes in different training periods. The load disturbance changes and the uncertainty of the system physical parameters generated in the human-machine interaction are controlled by parameter adaptive control, which solves the problem that the neural net¬work approximation domain of the traditional purely adaptive RBF neural network (ANNRBF) control algorithm is easily a¬ffected by the change of the load. ADAMS (automatic dynamic analysis of mechanical system)-MATLAB co-simulation results show that the control method proposed can achieve accurate gait trajectory tracking training, and has good adaptability and robustness to system load fluctuations caused by changes in muscle tension during patient training.

articleTitle: Bttery management system based on Freescale chip
abstract: In order to reduce the design cost and improve the acquisition accuracy, a battery management system(BMS) based on Freescale MC9S12XEP100 chip was developed for the standy battery system of a base station. BMS’ s main functions are monitoring the voltage, current, and temperature of the lithium battery, and also realizing the CAN communication between the host computers. According to the experiment’s result of measuring the battery voltage and estimating the SOC value, it can be said that the BMS is stable in reliability. In terms of software, it is mainly divided into two parts, bottom driver and functional application. Meanwhile a logic task without a task stack is designed to make the software low coupling and high cohesion.

articleTitle: New Single-Phase High-Frequency Isolated ∏-Z-Source AC-AC Converter
abstract: In order to improve the voltage range of AC/AC converter, reduce the cost and ensure the safe operation of the circuit, a single-phase isolated AC/AC converter with high-frequency transformer is proposed in this paper. This converter adds ∏-source impedance network to quasi-Z-source AC/AC converter, and integrates a single winding on the ∏-source coupling inductor to form a high-frequency transformer, which makes the circuit form electrical isolation. The new converter can not only make the output voltage and input in phase or inverse phase, but also can provide a wider range of buck boost output voltage, making the circuit more flexible. The working principle of the circuit is analyzed, the relationship between input and output is calculated, the simulation model is built by Simulink, and finally the experimental model is built in the laboratory for verification. Simulation and experimental results verify the correctness and feasibility of the converter.

articleTitle: Sparsity Adaptive Compression Identification Algorithm for Volterra Series Model
abstract: Amount of computation will increase sharply in identification of Volterra series with the increase of order and memory length of nonlinear system. A sparse kernel coefficient identification model based on sparsity of coefficients in polynomial expansion and method of sparse signal reconstruction in compressed sensing is constructed in this study. Measurement matrix form of the second-order Volterra series is derived and sparse adaptive matching pursuit algorithm is used to reconstruct kernel coefficients of each order. Simulation results showed that this algorithm overcomes the influence of excessively high and excessively low estimated signal sparsity on reconstruction accuracy compared with orthogonal matching pursuit algorithm.

articleTitle: Hybrid Attitude Controller Design for a Rigid Spacecraft with Angular Velocity Constraint
abstract: In this work, we propose a solution to the attitude tracking problem for a rigid spacecraft with full torque actuation and angular velocity constraint. Under some reasonable assumptions, by employing the backstepping of hybrid feedback laws, a quaternion-based attitude tracking controller is designed such that the spacecraft is able to track the desired attitude. A barrier Lyapunov function is introduced to ensure that the angular velocity always stays within a predefined bounded range. At last, simulation results are provided and analyzed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Intelligent target heating curve generating method and its application for annular heating furnaces
abstract: This paper proposes a method for generating a target rod-billet heating curve of heating furnace. The temperature field model is used in the heating furnace thermal field to establish an offline rule editor, which transforms the currently applied heating system into a target rod-billet heating trajectory with the horizontal axis as the position. By this generating curve guide, an optimized temperature control system is designed and applied to an annular heating furnace. The operating action saves resources in production applications and obtains a good temperature control effect by controlling and optimizing the heating furnace target heating process of the rod-billet.

articleTitle: Research on "two-step positioning method" of high voltage cross-bonded cable based on sheath current
abstract: After the cable failure, whether the fault location can be carried out immediately has an effect on the power supply reliability of the urban power grid. Different from overhead lines, the cable has multi-layer metal structure, especially the high-voltage cross-bonded cable, which makes the electrical relationship between the layers complex. It is very difficult for the traditional transmission line theory and fault location method to accurately locate the fault. In this paper, based on the analysis of the structure of high voltage cross-bonded cable, the model of sheath current is established, and the single-phase fault criterion and location method based on sheath current are summarized. Through a large number of simulations, it is verified that the proposed algorithm is still applicable to different fault types, fault locations, transition resistances and fault initial phase angles, and has high ranging accuracy.

articleTitle: Robust PI Observer Design of the Welding Process Model
abstract: In this paper, robust proportional integral (PI) observer design problem of the welding process model is investigated. Because of the existence of unknown state and unknown disturbance in the welding process model, PI observer is designed, moreover, the relevant gains are solved. At last, a simulation example is shown to illustrate feasibility.

articleTitle: Node Gain-based Cooperative Fault-tolerant Tracking Control of Multi-helicopter Systems
abstract: The study proposes a cooperative fault-tolerant tracking control scheme for multi-helicopter systems with sensor faults, actuator faults, and system nonlinearities. The control framework contains a decentralized fault estimation and distributed fault-tolerant tracking control structure. To ensure the excellent tracking performance of multi-helicopter systems, a cooperative fault-tolerant tracking control protocol based on distributed node gain is proposed equipped with the estimation information in fault estimation. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed cooperative tracking control algorithm.

articleTitle: Path Tracking Control of Dynamic Positioning Ship Based on Self-coupling PI
abstract: Aiming at the problem of model-free parameter tuning in path tracking control of dynamic positioning ship, a self-coupling proportional-integral (SC-PI) controller was proposed. The SFLOS guidance law is designed to obtain the desired heading angle as the system input. The adaptive speed factor is introduced to design the SC-PI controller of the expected heading angle, longitudinal velocity, transverse velocity and yaw angular velocity of the dynamic positioning ship to realize the path tracking control of the dynamic positioning ship. It has the advantages of less tuning parameters and no need to consider the problem of system instability. The stability and anti-disturbance robustness of the system are analyzed by complex frequency domain and time domain methods. The simulation results show that the dynamic positioning ship based on SC-PI controller can track the desired path well by quickly tuning parameters, and has good anti-disturbance ability.

articleTitle: Observer-Based Event-Triggered Tracking Control of Multi-Player Nonlinear Systems via Adaptive Dynamic Programming
abstract: This paper investigates event-triggered optimal tracking control (OTC) problems of unknown nonlinear multiplayer systems by using adaptive dynamic programming. To begin with, a neural network-based observer is constructed to obtain the unknown system dynamics. By establishing an augmented system and designing a discount performance index function, the OTC problem is transformed to an optimal regulation problem. Subsequently, critic-only structure is adopted to solve the event-triggered tracking Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation. Moreover, for the purpose of reducing the computing and communication burdens, a novel triggering condition which is suitable for multiple controllers is designed via Lyapunov’s direct method, and tracking controllers are renovated at triggering moments only. Theoretical analysis shows that the tracking error is guaranteed to be uniform ultimate bounded. Finally, simulation example is provided to validate the effectiveness of the developed method.

articleTitle: Preset Performance Train Tracking Control using Quantified State and Dilated Error Feedback
abstract: This paper is concerned with a train tracking control scheme, with respect to an offline-obtained speed profile versus mileage and time, in the presence of preset performance constraint and quantified state measurements, using a new dilated error feedback design. By dilated error feedback, it means that the combination of "transformed" and "un-transformed" errors, raised in the frameworks of prescribed performance control and traditional linear feedback respectively, is utilized in the control design. A dilated error-based proportional control is proposed, which can not only establish the stability of the closed-loop system, but also ensure the train tracking errors are kept within preset performance constraints. Meanwhile, the proposed control exhibits low complexity in sense that adaptation, learning and approximation of unknown parameters or dynamics are all not involved. Considering the performance of on-board sensors, a hysteretic quantizer is used for states measurement. Information of train and environment parameters and external disturbances is not required in the control design, only quantitative measurement is included. The closed-loop stability is proved via Lyapunov stability theorem. Finally, simulation results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed control.

articleTitle: Continuous Nonsingular Terminal Sliding Mode Speed Control based on Finite-time Exact Observer for Marine Diesel Engine
abstract: In this paper, a practical tracking control approach of the marine diesel engine is developed using an exact observer-based continuous nonsingular terminal sliding mode (CNSTM) control algorithm. The parameter uncertainties and the external disturbance of the marine engine system in modelling. A finite-time exact observer (FEO) is designed, by which the lumped uncertainty is accurately estimated in finite-time. By combining the observed information, a novel CNSTM speed controller is designed for the marine diesel engine, which features fast response, strong robustness and high accuracy. Especially the low-pass filter is introduced to realize free-chattering sliding mode (SM) control, and it is not necessary to obtain the differential information of state variables for the control law in practical application. Comparative simulations with the traditional second-order sliding mode (SOSM) control are presented to validate this paper.

articleTitle: The Research on Robustness of Traditional Input Shaper by Satellite
abstract: This paper makes the research on the problem of robustness of the input shaper by satellite. Firstly, we do the research on the sensitive-function of the input shaper by satellite. On the basis of research, the coordinate meaning in the sensitive function is modified, and the robustness evaluation parameter is added. By setting the preconditions of the curve, we have drawn the input shaper. Compare simulation results, this research methods will make good help for using the input shaper by satellite.

articleTitle: Study on TS Fuzzy Observer for BAB System with Unmeasurable Premise Variables
abstract: A ball and beam system with unknown premise variables is described. A TS fuzzy model is used to represent the ball and beam system. Since it is difficult to measure the internal state of the unstable ball and beam beam system directly, a TS fuzzy observer is proposed. After establishing TS fuzzy model, reclassify the premise variables in the equation. The TS fuzzy observer designed by this method is validated in the simulation program. In order to see the actual effect of the observer, it can see the tracing effect after running the program connected to the real ball and beam system.

articleTitle: Polar Transformation Based Rotation Convolution Network for Oriented Object Detection
abstract: Recently, oriented object detection has made considerable progress in the field of remote sensing image interpretation. However, there are still some challenges for oriented objects including the dense distribution, the different shapes and the multi-scale. To put the axe in the helve, we propose a Polar Oriented Object Detector (PO<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Det) modeled in polar coordinates. The PO<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Det consists of the Feature Rotation Alignment Module (FRAM) and the Polar Detection Head (PDH). Firstly, the FRAM is designed to enhanced representation properties of the model to objects in the situation of dense distribution and different shapes by adjusting the sampling location of the convolution kernels to adapt to the shapes, the sizes and the orientations of the targets. Then, the PDH can obtain oriented bounding boxes by predicting two polar angles as well as one polar radius in polar coordinates, where the scales of the oriented objects can be both more clearly expressed by one polar radius than Cartesian coordinates to optimize multi-scale target detection ability of the model. Experimental results on the two commonly remote sensing datasets (i.e., DOTA and HRSC2016) proved that PO<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Det can achieve the up-to-date performance.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Data Decoupling Model for Rotating Machinery Multiple Faults Diagnosis
abstract: Single-point fault diagnosis of rotating machinery is a matter of great concern at present, and the mature study findings are fruitful in this field. However, since the interrelationship of subunits and the faults features correlation, the multiple faults diagnosis for rotating machinery commonly existing in actual industrial systems is still an intractable problem. Therefore, in order to solve the multiple faults diagnosis problem, an adaptive data decoupling model is proposed, and then, a solution programme for rotating machinery multiple faults diagnosis is constructed in this paper. Specifically, 1) A novel loss function and an initial weights constraint are formulated to improve the feature learning diversity of sparse autoencoder. 2) A decoupling constraint term is constructed to reduce the harmful influence of data coupling. Finally, comparison tests and trial results analysis are developed to verify the effectiveness and practicability of this proposed model.

articleTitle: Multi-feature Fusion With Attention and Receptive Field for Camouflaged People Detection
abstract: Camouflaged object is usually visually similar to the surrounding environment.
