abstract: In this article, we consider the control problem of uncertain nonlinear cyber-physical systems (CPSs) in the face of attacks known as denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. First, a novel event-triggering mechanism (ETM) with dynamic adjustment is proposed, which is used to determine instants of data transmission, and a parameter estimator is designed that does not rely on the real-time system state. Then, on the basis of DoS assumptions, we give a sufficient condition, under which the system state is uniformly ultimately bounded (UUB). Finally, a numerical simulation is presented to confirm that the control method is valid.

articleTitle: A Classification Model of Music Genres Using BP Neural Network Based on Genre Similarity Analysis
abstract: The classification of music is not only beneficial to art research but also conducive to the development of music. As one of the main research issues, the automatic classification of music genres has attracted many researchers' attention. To classify a genre into the category, this paper proposes a music classification method based on neural network by using a large number of music data as samples. Firstly, in order to quantify the similarity of music genres, hierarchical cluster analysis is carried out by using 14 indicators from characteristics of the music, type of vocals and music description. Then, the BP neural network music genre classification model is established based on the clustering analysis of music genres. Finally, the accuracy and effectiveness of the music genre classification model are verified through a data set of nearly 90,000 songs. The results show that the classification accuracy of the model can reach 91.4%.

articleTitle: Delta Robot Trajectory Tracking Based on Fuzzy Adaptive Sliding Mode Controller
abstract: A trajectory tracking controller for Delta robot is developed in this paper. The tracking performance of Delta robot is usually affected by unknown external disturbances, model inaccuracy and uncertain couplings, these are considered as lumped disturbances to the system. Sliding mode control has a good nature of being insensitive to disturbance, however it brings the issue of high-frequency chattering, which is harmful to practical system. In order to alleviate chattering as well as maintain robustness for trajectory tracking of Delta robot, a novel control method combined sliding mode and fuzzy adaptive function is proposed. First, a sliding mode control law is designed. Then, a set of fuzzy logic rules and an adaptive law are introduced, the smooth and continuous output K of the fuzzy function is used to replace the discontinuous product of sign function and a gain vector in sliding mode control law. Moreover, the Lyapunov stability theory is used to prove the finite-time stability of the closed-loop control system. Finally, the numerical simulation results verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: A Decentralized Algorithm for Deep Echo State Networks
abstract: As a class of recurrent neural networks (RNNs), echo state networks (ESNs) have been studied extensively in recent years, particularly in time-series prediction and non-linear system identification. It is well-known that deep learning (DL) has been applied to ESNs and shows more outstanding performance than conventional ESNs. However, due to the large-scale dataset and complexity required to train deep learning models, the time required to train deep ESNs based on traditional centralized algorithms is highly extended. Hence, a decentralized training algorithm combining DL and ESNs is presented in this paper to aim at multiple time scales processing of temporal data. We propose this algorithm based on an optimization program called the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) and decentralized average consensus (DAC) procedure. The results based on a large-scale artificial dataset prove that it has more advantages in generalization accuracy and training time than the centralized experimental scheme.

articleTitle: An approximate design of reduced-order unknown input estimator for a two-link serial manipulator
abstract: In this paper, the problem of simultaneous estimation of states and perturbations for a class of serial manipulator is investigated. First, the model of the serial manipulator is simplified by using LPV modeling with uncertainty characterization. Based on this, an incremental system model on state and perturbation is further constructed. Then, a class of reduced-order unknown input estimators is designed using a parameterization method. Finally, a simulation case is given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Bi-C shape antenna design based on a proposed particle swarm optimization algorithm
abstract: A proposed particle swarm optimization algorithm is presented, and the method is used for design of a bi-C shaped broadband weakly circularly polarized antenna. The structure of the antenna is based on the multi-mode technology, resonance branches are employed, two different shapes and sizes of radiation units are used to excite different resonant frequencies of the antenna and the new particle swarm optimization algorithm is introduced to optimize the parameters to achieve a wide band; to increase the impedance bandwidth, ,to improve the impedance matching of the antenna, and to expand its coverage (2-9G), the return loss at multiple resonance points of the antenna is significantly reduced, the antenna has better radiation characteristics comparing with the similar antennas, it has higher gain and wider bandwidth(130.5%), it canbe used in WiFi, Bluetooth and other fields.

articleTitle: An Improved Artificial Fish-Swarm Algorithm and Its Applications
abstract: The convergence and accuracy of the artificial fish swarm algorithm (AFSA) depend not only on the algorithm parameters, but also on the four different behaviors of the fish swarm algorithm. This paper analyzes the influence mechanism of fish swarm algorithm's four behaviors: preying, swarming, following, and random moving behavior on the convergence speed and performance of the algorithm. Combined with the interval division of the bird swarm algorithm, the number of fish swarm of the four behaviors in the AFSA is modified, and a novel algorithm based on interval division (DAFSA) is proposed. Simulations in 5 test functions show that the DAFSA algorithm can quickly converge to a better global solution, has good convergence accuracy. Meanwhile, DAFSA has good practical value in solving the parameters of neural networks.

articleTitle: EU-Net: A Novel Semantic Segmentation Architecture for Surface Defect Detection of Mobile Phone Screens
abstract: In this paper, a new semantic segmentation algorithm, EU-Net (Efficient U-Net), is proposed to realize surface defect detection of mobile phone screens. Compared with U-Net, the encoder and decoder of EU-Net are modified with EfficientNet-B0 and MBconv Block to enhance the detection efficiency and accuracy. Due to the loss of feature information in the cropping operation, it is removed in our EU-Net to improve the detection accuracy. In addition, conventional image processing techniques are used to enhance the dataset. The experiments are conducted on a dataset collected from a production site of the mobile phone screens to verify the superiority of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Self-updating Fault Diagnosis Method of Dynamic Positioning Ship Sensor Based on Wavelet Neural Network
abstract: In order to solve the problem that the fault diagnosis method of intelligent dynamic positioning ship sensors has poor accuracy and the difficulty in obtaining a large number of fault data of each specific ship, this paper proposes a self-updating fault diagnosis method based on wavelet packet decomposition and neural network, combined with semi-supervised learning method. The method uses labeled data sets to train the initial model and unlabeled data sets to improve the accuracy of model. Finally, based on a specific dynamic positioning ship model, the simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively improve the overall accuracy of the fault diagnosis model and decrease the rate of false positives, misstatement of the fault diagnosis model by using the sensor data acquired during ship operation, overcome the lack of historical data of neural network, and improve the performance of fault diagnosis on a specific ship.

articleTitle: A new particle swarm optimization method based on random disturbance
abstract: A new method is presented in this paper to update the inertia weights, the orbital motion based on the nonlinear adjustment of parameters in the particle optimization iterative process is evolved, thus multi-modal and high-dimensional complex optimization is avoided. The computational burden is decreased and the accuracy is improved. Four test functions are employed to verify the effectiveness and correctness.

articleTitle: Design of Electromagnetic Emission Experiment Teaching System based on Ultrasonic Positioning
abstract: A small electromagnetic emission experimental teaching system based on STM32F103 microcontroller and ultrasonic sensor is designed. Through electromagnetic launch theory analysis, the structure including the two - dimensional steering gear head and electromagnetic coil gun is designed. Ultrasonic wave is used for horizontal tracking and distance measurement of the target. Optimal launching angle is automatically calculated by STM32. After adjusting the firing angle of the gun barrel, the relay is turned on to discharge, and the projectile hits the target center. At the same time, the measured distance, charging voltage and emission angle is displayed on the TFT screen. The test results show that electromagnetic launch system can quickly complete the target search and location, and can reach preferable precision. The system has advantages in low cost, moderate difficulty and stable performance, and has potential value of experimental teaching and practical application.

articleTitle: A Connection Event Based Time Synchronization scheme for BSN enabled BLE nodes
abstract: Time synchronization is very important for sensing nodes in a body sensor network (BSN). The uncertainty of the wake-up time of Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) air link makes it is a great challenging of achieving precise time synchronization between nodes. Hence, we propose a connection event based BLE-BSN node time synchronization scheme to ensure accuracy clock between nodes. We firstly analyzed the factors cause the time error of CC2642R sensor nodes in a star network, and proposed a BLE connection event based pulse synchronization method to estimate the time error between the master node and the slave nodes. The estimated time error was compensated at each connection beats, which strictly guarantees time coherence of node in the application of physiological measurement. We tested the proposed time synchronization scheme with a four-nodes network. Experimental results show that with the proposed method, the time error of the node is less than ±150ps under the 200ms connection interval. The proposed method has good potential using in BSN physiological measurement application.

articleTitle: Iteration-Based Adaptive Inverse Control of Uncertain Nonlinear Systems With Hysteresis Modeled By Preisach Operator
abstract: This paper is devoted to solving the tracking control problem of uncertain nonlinear systems preceded by the Preisach operator. Such a problem is challenging, mainly because the precise knowledge of the Preisach density function cannot be obtained through identification due to the coupling effect of hysteresis output with uncertain system dynamics. To overcome the problem, a new iteration-based adaptive inverse control scheme is developed, which is composed of a direct adaptive fuzzy controller as the feedback module, and a numerical adaptive inverse as the feedforward compensator. With our scheme, it can be proved that all signals of the closed-loop system are bounded, and the output tracking error goes to a prescribed interval asymptotically with time going to infinity. The results are verified also by a simulation study conducted on a practical piezoelectric positioning stage.

articleTitle: Research on collaborative formation of heterogeneous multi-agent systems with nonlinear terms
abstract: In order to study a heterogeneous multi-agent consisting of a first-order linear agent and an agent with second- order nonlinear terms, a multi-agent system is designed under action of the one order virtual navigator and according to the conformance protocol. The distributed formation control algorithm of the system uses the Lyapunov function theory and model conversion to analyze the stability of the multi-agent system(MAS). A sufficient condition for the formation control stability of multi-agents is given and expressed as linear matrix inequality. The validity of the theory is verified by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Evaluation Based on Surrogate Model for Multidispatching Sections of High-Speed Railway Scheduling
abstract: Under the condition of network operation of high-speed railway, the influence of disruptions on the train scheduling at the current line and related lines is more and more significant. For the multi-region high-speed railway scheduling, the process of network operation and constraint is complex, which leads to a not accurate model. The method of simulation can get an accurate model and evaluate global indicators effectively, but the simulation and optimization process of large-scale high-speed railway network is expensive and time-consuming with the ever-expanding high-speed railway network and intensive High-speed railway traffic. The paper proposes a surrogate model to replace high-speed railway network simulation for low-cost evaluation, which effectively reduces the expense of simulation.

articleTitle: Modeling and decentralized finite-time connective tracking control with preseted settling time for a double inverted pendulum system with stochastic excitation
abstract: This paper investigates the modeling problem and decentralized finite-time connective tracking control problem with preseted settling time for a double inverted pendulum system under random excitation. It is the first time to establish the stochastic mathematical model of the system. And this paper focus on the connective stability problem of this system. A novel method is proposed by utilizing a prescribed finite-time performance function (PFTPF). The obtained controllers can assure the system tracking errors are restricted by the PFTPF, they can assemble to a predesigned region of the equilibrium point in any settling time. The system signals are probability bounded and the whole system is connectively stable. Finally, simulated example shows the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Bearing-Based Formation Tracking Control with Prespecified Convergence Time
abstract: This article proposes a formation cooperation control strategy that is based on bearing for a first-order multi-agent system. For this multi-agent system, our control goal is to achieve a desired target formation shape, which each agent only need to obtain the relative orientation and position of its neighbors. In this paper, we can find that it is different from considerable existing works, which achieve global asymptotic stability, that is, expect formations to be formed only in an infinite period of time, the control law proposed can reach the desired target formation shape within the time selected by the user and can also ensure exponential convergence within the selected time simultaneously. In addition, in this paper, analysis on convergence of formation of the system studied is also guaranteed by the Lyapunov theory. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed approach is verified by us by presenting two numerical simulation examples.

articleTitle: Three-level PMSM model predictive torque control based on extended voltage vector set
abstract: In order to reduce the torque and flux pulses in the traditional model predictive torque control, a method to expand the voltage vector based on a given duty cycle is proposed, which expands the three-level inverter space vector from 27 to 73 and make full use of a pair of positive and negative redundant short vectors to balance the midpoint potential to simplify the value function. In order to reduce the computational burden of the system, the candidate vector set is selected by judging the area of the reference voltage vector, and the optimal voltage vector is optimized by the weight function. The switch signal of the optimal voltage vector is output through the look-up table, which enhances the real-time nature of the scheme. In order to verify the practicability of this algorithm, through MATLAB/SIMULINK simulation, the extended voltage vector can reduce torque and magnetic flux pulsation, and compared with the traditional method.

articleTitle: VFM-based modelling of burden descent under varying burden charging matrix for blast furnace
abstract: The blast furnace (BF) is the main equipment in ironmaking industry in China. For the BF, the production and the smooth operation largely depend on a reasonable burden structure. In the burden structure modelling, the burden descent is the weak link due to the black-box nature of the burden descending process. The viscous flow model (VFM) is a widely used burden descent model with relatively high accuracy. However, when adopted to determine the burden structure, the VFM can only perform under a constant charging matrix. In this work, we incorporate the VFM into the burden structure model which is capable of utilizing varying charging matrixes. First, to incorporate the VFM, a new layout of the burden structure model is designed. Then, to address the multiple burden descents problem caused by the VFM, a new strategy implementing the VFM is proposed. With this strategy, the multiple burden descents are compact into one solution process, and the model efficiency is thereby increased. Finally, the case study on the performance of the proposed burden structure model is carried out. Results show that the proposed model is able to capture the layer details in the burden. Results also show that, unlike the VFM alone, this VFM-based model is able to utilize varying charging matrix and depict structure of each individual layer.

articleTitle: Supervisory Predictive Control of Circulating Fluidized Bed Based on T-S Fuzzy Neural Network
abstract: In this paper, the algorithm and theory of supervisory predictive control (SPC) based on T-S fuzzy neural network is proposed and applied in Circulating fluidized bed (CFB) boiler system successfully. SPC combines both the plant economic process optimization and regulatory process control into a hierarchical control structure, in which the economic optimization is at the upper level and the dynamic tracking is at the lower level. Nonlinear CFB process is expressed by T-S fuzzy neural network. The simulation results of CFB system show that the SPC has more reliable and satisfactory control effects.

articleTitle: Gesture Recognition Based on Dual-channel Feature Fusion
abstract: In order to solve the problems of traditional gesture recognition based on artificial feature extraction, such as complicated operation, low accuracy, and insufficient feature extraction of classic convolutional neural network, we propose a two-stage dual-channel convolutional neural network. The entire network structure is divided into two stages which including a segmentation stage and a recognition stage. In the segmentation stage, a network consisting of a fully convolutional residual network and a Pyramid Pooling Module (PPM) module are used to execute the segmentation. As the shown in the experimental verification results, the proposed segmentation network designed has a very good effect in light changes and complex environments; For the recognition stage, we use a network which is composed of a two-channel convolutional neural network. The input of two channels is the RGB image and the feature map segmented by the segmentation network, and the output is the fusion of the extracted features of the two channels. For experimental verification, we paper use the OUHANDS data set. In theory, the recognition accuracy rate reaches 97.31%, and the network size and parameters are several times smaller than those of classic networks such as Lenet-5, ResNet-18, and VGGNet.

articleTitle: The software design for realizing the serial communication of the quadrotor
abstract: This article discusses the window program design of the serial communication between the quadrotor and the host computer. Firstly, the single-chip microcomputer module of the quadrotor is introduced. Secondly, the quadrotor ground station and its communication relationship with the quadrotor are introduced. Thirdly after understanding the principle of serial communication, the software design of serial communication is mainly introduced from the four aspects of design platform Visual Stdio2012, programming language c#, software interface design, and part of the communication software code. Finally, connect the quadrotor flight control board, and realize serial communication after repeated debugging.

articleTitle: User behavior control method for HPC system
abstract: It is very important to identify and control the user behavior of high performance computing system, especially the abnormal behavior. This article proposes a new model that improves the safety of HPC systems by fully integrating protection and monitoring technologies. The model covers physical security, host security, network security, and application security. The security of computing resources and user data is achieved through enhanced application layer access control. Various types of log data are collected to analyze user behavior and identify abnormalities. The analysis result will be used as a reference for authority adjustment. The proposed method implements behavior monitoring in a low-intrusion manner, and has the ability to detect unauthorized access and sharing behavior. It upgrades HPC system security protection from traditional border protection to business-based behavior control.

articleTitle: The Optimal State Estimation and IMU Fault Diagnosis of Aircraft Based on Optimal Two-Stage CKF
abstract: As a typical nonlinear system, the nonlinear state estimation problem of aircraft needs to be solved by nonlinear Kalman filter with high numerical accuracy. The standard Cubature Kalman Filter based on the spherical - radial cubature rule, which could be applied to solve high-dimensional nonlinear filter problems with minimal computational effort. However, when the nonlinear systematic dimension increases, the accuracy of CKF will decline. And CKF will lose the optimality of state estimation with the occurrence of fault. Two-Stage Kalman Filter can solve this problem, but it only applies to linear systems. In order to achieve high-precision estimation of aircraft state and fault diagnosis of the inertial measurement unit (IMU), an optimal two-stage volume Kalman filter (OTSCKF) is proposed in this paper. We take the IMU fault as random deviation and establish the aircraft and filter model. By comparing the simulation results of CKF and OTSCKF on aircraft state estimation and IMU fault diagnosis under the condition of unsteady wind field, we found that OTSCKF can obtain the optimal estimation of system state and deviation under the condition of random deviation of nonlinear system. Compared with CKF, the accuracy of OTSCKF is greatly improved. Moreover, it has the capability of fault diagnosis and robustness to IMU fault.

articleTitle: Cascade Transfer Function Models of MSWI Process based on Weight Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization
abstract: To establish combustion process model for accurately analyzing the dynamic characteristics of the municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) system is helpful. In this paper, a cascade transfer function model based on weight adaptive particle swarm optimization (WAPSO) is constructed. First, a cascade transfer function modeling strategy is designed by analyzing the characteristics of process variables. Second, the transfer function model is utilized for furnace temperature, flue gas oxygen concentration, and steam flow. At the same time, the WAPSO algorithm is used to identify model parameters. Finally, the cascade transfer function model is verified on the basis of the actual industrial dataset. The simulation results show that the established model can represents the dynamic characteristics under actual working conditions, which proves the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of Indoor Localization Algorithm Based on WiFi Fingerprints
abstract: WiFi-based indoor localization has been deeply studied and researched due to the convenient deployment of the WLAN infrastructure. However, indoor localization based on WiFi suffers the fluctuation of Received Signal Strength (RSS), including missing RSS during collection, redundant Access Points (APs), and abnormal RSS values. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a hybrid filtering algorithm based on isolated forest and weighted mean to ensure the real-time filtering correction of RSS signal and provide high-quality fingerprint signal for online location. In addition, a two-panel fingerprint homogeneity graph is adopted to gauge the resemblance of localization fingerprints, and the estimated 2-D location is predicted by the integration of panel results. We have conducted experiments to demonstrate the localization algorithm’s performance. Compared with other algorithms, the results show that the proposed method can achieve the best performance.

articleTitle: A variable neighborhood search algorithm for the balanced K-way partitioning problem with weight constraints
abstract: The balanced K-way partitioning problem with weight constraints (BKPWC) is a NP-hard combinatorial problem with several real-world applications. In this article, we present a variable neighborhood search algorithm for the BKPWC by combining an initialization method generating a feasible initial solution, a variable neighborhood descent method acting as the local search procedure, and a perturbation operator to generate the offspring solutions. Experiments on the benchmark instances show that the proposed algorithm is very efficient and is much faster compared with the existing best performing algorithms in the literature.

Author Keywords: Balanced K-way partitioning problem with weight constraints

articleTitle: Optimal control method of ship DC microgrid based on multi-mode switching
abstract: Ship microgrids can be connected to new energy power generation units, which can not only solve the power supply problem of the ship's partial load, but also solve the instability problem of new energy power generation and improve the power generation efficiency of new energy. Therefore, it has received extensive attention. Aiming at the problem of serious diesel loss of diesel generators in ships, an optimized control method of ship DC microgrid based on multi-mode switching is proposed. The ship operation is planned into six modes. According to the load power demand, the ship DC microgrid is used to adjust the diesel generators’ power. The operating efficiency can improve the high-efficiency operating time of diesel generators. According to the actual ship load curve, the method is simulated and verified to reduce the fuel consumption by 7.97%-8.17%.

articleTitle: Research on simulation modeling of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor based on variable parameters
abstract: The inductance of interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) is set to a constant value, ignoring the time-varying characteristics of the motor inductance in the traditional modeling method. In this paper, the finite-element analysis (FEA) model of the IPMSM is built by electromagnetic field analysis software, and the dynamic time-varying inductance parameters are calculated by the FEA model. The parameters are applied to the circuit model built by MATLAB/Simulink, and a PMSM simulation model with dynamic inductance parameters is established, so as to improve the accuracy of the simulation model. Finally, the model is applied to the MTPA control system to verify its correctness, and then compared with the traditional model of simulation results, it is found that the model has better dynamic characteristics.

articleTitle: Command Filtered Control for Time-Delay Systems with Asymmetric Full State Constraints
abstract: This paper develops a novel controller design for strict feedback nonlinear systems with constant full state constraints and unknown time-varying full state delays. Lyapunov-Krasovskii functionals (LKFs) are applied to handle the unknown time-varying full state delays. To evade the explosion of complexity, command filters (CFs) are utilized with filter errors compensated by introducing compensating signals. In Lyapunov function-based stability analysis, barrier Lyapunov functions are employed to prove that the compensated tracking errors can be constrained in predetermined constant bound limits through the controller design, where the boundedness proof of all signals in the closed-loop system is further simplified. Simulation experiments verify the effectiveness of the proposed design.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Corn Harvester Spray-duct Following Model System Based on Arduino Technolog
abstract: The spray-duct device represents one of the major components of the corn harvester for harvesting operations, whereas the control of the spray-duct angle constitutes the primary challenge for accomplishing this task. At present, the majority of the existing impurity removal devices or grain output spray-ducts in large harvesters cannot be easily adjusted, while for those adjustable ones, the accuracy of the spray-ducts is limited with relatively low utilization of human resources, which fails to satisfy the intelligent development of agricultural machinery at this stage. In this paper, the Arduino control function is applied to realize the control over the spray-duct model. In this system, an integrated design is carried out involving camera module, servo control module, ultrasonic module, Beidou navigation module and software part, with a view to achieving multi-directional control of the spray-duct.

articleTitle: Semi-supervised Adversarial Domain Adaptation Based on Maximum Mean Discrepancy
abstract: Domain adaptation aims to transfer knowledge from a source domain to a new but related target domain. Most adversarial training methods align feature distributions thus both domains can share the same classifier. However, compared to unsupervised adversarial domain adaptation, supervised information from the labeled target domain can better guide the transfer process by learning transferable as well as discriminative features. In this paper, we propose a novel semi-supervised adversarial domain adaptation (SSADA) method that can align the feature distributions across domains. In SSADA, labeled target samples are used to learn discriminative features while unlabeled target samples are used to learn transferable features based on Maximum Mean Discrepancy. The experiments on public datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Prediction of Product Quality Based on Multiple Kernel Learning Least Square Support Vector Machine Regression
abstract: Some important product quality variables in the distillation column are difficult to be detected and predicted online. To solve this problem, a novel method of soft sensing based on multiple kernel learning least square support vector machine regression (MKL-LS-SVM) is proposed. To improve the generation of the soft sensor model, polynomial kernels, radial basis function kernels, sigmoid kernels are used in the multiple kernel learning LS-SVM algorithm. The application shows that multi-core instead of single kernel can improve the interpretability of decision function and obtain the better performance. By using such as root mean squared error as evaluation index to evaluate the learning algorithm in the nonlinear function data set and the continuous distillation simulation data set under noise disturbance. The simulation results show that this MKL-LS-SVM method can improve the prediction accuracy of soft sensing in the distillation process.

articleTitle: Energy Consumption Optimization of a Serial Production Line with Unreliable Machines and Limited Buffers under Batch Production
abstract: Increasing the energy efficiency of industrial processes has been a major issue for the manufacturing industry. To achieve energy-efficient production while maintaining the required productivity, the efficiencies of machines should be optimized. In this work, the energy consumption optimization for a kind of batch production-based serial line with limited buffers and Bernoulli reliability machines is discussed. The analytical solution is obtained for a special case of the optimization problem. A calculation procedure is proposed to find the numerical solution for general cases. Experimental results show that the proposed procedure can solve the energy consumption optimization problem effectively.

articleTitle: Low-light image enhancement and acceleration processing based on ZYNQ
abstract: Most embedded vision systems are used to capture an image in low-light condition which results in an image with low visibility and quality. However, high-performance image enhancement algorithms take up lots of chip resources and are time consuming in embedded vision application scenarios with high real-time requirements. In this paper, a multi-core heterogeneous embedded vision system is designed based on ZYNQ, and it uses the optimized screen blending algorithm to complete the enhancement of low-light images. First, the inverse color coefficient is optimized to enhance the texture details of the image. Secondly, adaptive gamma correction is performed on the inverted image to maintain the trueness of the enhanced image color. Finally, through reasonable hardware and software co-design, the inverse color coefficient is calculated by hardware logic circuit to speed up the algorithm. Experimental results show that the low-light images collected and processed by this system have a certain improvement in the image quality than the original algorithm. The processing speed is nearly 5 times faster than without hardware acceleration, which meets the real-time requirements of embedded vision systems.

articleTitle: Prediction of the eigenfrequency of industrial robots based on the ANN model
abstract: When industrial robots are used in various machining processes, higher requirements for processing accuracy and performance stability are put forward. Low-frequency chatter occurs in the machining process. Because of the articulated mechanism of industrial robots, the low frequency varies in the whole workspace. This is related to the eigenfrequency of industrial robots. To investigate the low-frequency distribution, the first eigenfrequency of an industrial robot is obtained through the impact modal experiment, which is used to evaluate the machining field and robot pose. To obtain the eigenfrequency distribution of the workspace with limited experimental data, an artificial neural network (ANN) is used to establish a prediction model. The structure and prediction accuracy of the ANN model are discussed.

articleTitle: Simulation of control and maneuverings under Ship-ship interaction
abstract: To avoid collisions between guide ship and approach ship during the maneuvering process, it is important to maintain a certain distance between the two ships. In order to simulate maneuverings between two ships, Firstly, the modeling and simulation research of a single ship are carried out, and then, based on the interaction forces of two ships, the parallel maneuvering motion simulation of two ships is completed. Finally, a simulation is performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the control method. The hydrodynamic interaction is the main factor affecting the navigation control and safety of two ships.

articleTitle: A Modified Chimp Optimization Algorithm for Short-Term Hydrothermal Scheduling
abstract: The short-term hydrothermal scheduling (STHS) problem with the valve point effect is a nonlinear and non-convex optimization scheduling issue in the economic operation of power systems. In order to overcome these difficulties, we propose a modified chimp optimization algorithm (MCOA) to work out the STHS problem. On account of the standard COA has a strong dependence on the initial population and is easy to fall into local optimal defects, two improvement approaches are proposed in this paper. One is to initialize the population by using sin map, the other is to improve the chaotic parameter. We use a test system with four hydro plants and three thermal plants to prove the effect of these improvements. The experimental consequences indicate that MCOA has a strong competitive advantage over other approaches in terms of the optimal result, which verify the feasibility and effectiveness of MCOA in the solution of hydrothermal scheduling.

articleTitle: A fusion method based on ANN to overcome the GNSS Outages for GNSS/INS System
abstract: The performance of the GNSS/INS integrated navigation system will be reduced during GNSS outages. In order to deal with GNSS outages, a fusion method based on ANN is proposed. First, the ELM network is used to achieve rapid detection of the sudden outages of the GNSS signal. Then, according to the output of the INS system, the BP neural network is used to predict the incremental output of GNSS, and the accuracy is improved by adopting the past information of the INS in different steps.This method has been verified in actual vehicle data experiments.The accuracy of the ELM detection method was tested through comparative experiments, and the improvement of navigation accuracy based on the improved BPNN fusion method during GNSS outages.Comprehensive experiment show that the integrated navigation fusion algorithm based on ELM and BPNN can effectively reduce the navigation error during GNSS signal interruption.At the same time, different algorithm options are provided to balance the computational burden and navigation accuracy.

articleTitle: A Stackelberg Game for Relieving Peak Pressure of Power Grid Using Electric Vehicles with V2G Technology
abstract: The recent explosive application of electrical equipment has brought a great burden on the power grid, which can easily lead to power shortage and slow down the economic growth. Electric Vehicles(EVs) can be a workable solution with the character of removability and energy storage. In this paper, we study a EV discharging strategy via V2G technology, which aims to release the pressure during peak time. Specifically, we set up the above EV discharging problem as a multi-leader and multi-follower Stackelberg game model. In which the EVs are acted as leaders and charing stations are acted as followers, they are allowed to bid freely in the market. Then, we proved that our proposed Stackelberg game based discharging strategy achieves the property of Nash equilibrium. Besides, the experimental results show that the proposed method can significantly reduce the cost of the charging stations and reduce the electricity demand on the power grid.

articleTitle: Motion Planning in Lane Change Scenario for Autonomous Vehicles
abstract: Motion planning is an important and complex research content in automatic driving system. This paper proposes a motion planning method in lane change scenario, which decouples the motion planning into two parts: longitudinal and lateral planning. This method takes the leading vehicle of each lane change gap as the following control vehicle, obtains the longitudinal trajectory of each gap by LQR algorism. Then the most appropriate lane change gap is selected through a certain strategy, which is developed on driving comfort and timeliness. After the gap selection, the host vehicle follows the leading vehicle of the selected gap to adjust its speed and position to meet the lane change condition. The lateral planning is initialized when the condition is met. The whole algorithm has a small amount of calculation and is convenient for practical engineering application. Finally, the validity and practicability of this method are verified by a real vehicle test.

articleTitle: Multi-Layer Flat Refractive Underwater Camera Calibration for Visual SLAM
abstract: Most underwater camera calibration methods only consider the refraction of light in the water and ignore the effect of glass. During the calibration process, the angle between the imaging plane and the refraction plane was ignored, which inevitably generates calibration errors. To address this problem, a new underwater camera model is proposed, which rotates the camera by taking into account the refraction of light among different media. The imaging plane of the camera after rotation is parallel to the refractive surface. According to the refraction of light between different adjacent media, the camera model we derived shows that the intrinsic of the camera under different media only differs by a scale factor. Finally, an experimental platform is established to verify the correctness of our theoretical derivation.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Consensus of Second-Order Multi-Agent Systems with Prescribed Performance
abstract: In this paper, a new approach to design event-triggered control protocol (ETCP) for second-order multi-agent systems (MASs) with prescribed performance is proposed. First of all, we introduce a nonlinear control protocol integrating a prescribed performance function and an error transformation function, thereby guaranteeing the prescribed performance with respect to the convergence of the position. Based on the nonlinear control protocol, an edge-based event-triggered control strategy is designed, where the neighbors’ position information is only required at the triggering time instants. Furthermore, it is showed that Zeno-free property holds for each agent. In the end, a simulation case is provided to verify the conclusion.

articleTitle: Design of Adaptive Cruise Control Considering Mulit-scene Application
abstract: Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) is an important part of the intelligent driving system. This paper proposes a system design method to make ACC applicable to multiple scenarios. Firstly, in consideration of the complexity and diversity of the car-following scenario in ACC, a fuzzy LQR method based on kinematics model is proposed, which can ensure the safety and comfort driving of the host vehicle under various road conditions. Secondly, a lane change mode is added on the basis of cruise and car-following mode, which is consistent with drivers' lane change behavior. It enables the host vehicle to accelerate or decelerate as early as possible without collision during lane change. Thirdly, a compensation control strategy is designed to reduce the impact that the actuator cannot follow the expected well due to changes in the road environment and vehicle parameters during actual driving. Finally, the effectiveness and practicability of the designed ACC are verified by a real vehicle test. The test results show that the system can apply to various scenarios well.

articleTitle: Path Tracking of Vehicles on Urban Roads Based on Fuzzy Control and NMPC
abstract: Since the curvature of urban roads varies greatly, path tracking in this scenario faces the problem that it is difficult to simultaneously guarantee high accuracy and high efficiency. According to previous work on path tracking, nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) has good accuracy when the curvature of the reference path varies. But when it is hoped to further improve the efficiency, the accuracy of NMPC-based path tracking control is still difficult to guarantee. So, we combined fuzzy control and NMPC to design a path tracking controller, which can adjust the speed to ensure high accuracy and high efficiency. Then, we verified the proposed controller through the joint simulation of MATLAB/Simulink and CarSim. When the simulation environment is consistent, the maximum absolute values of the displacement error and the heading error of the proposed controller are 80.4 % and 46.6 % smaller than those of the NMPC controller. The proposed controller is robust to positioning error, and it can operate normally when the positioning error is not greater than 0.04 m. Besides, the real-time performance of the proposed controller can be ensured by reducing the control horizon. The maximum calculation time in the simulation only accounts for 28 % of the control period.

articleTitle: Manual assembly action segmentation method based on spatiotemporal features
abstract: Accurate segmentation of manual assembly action in an uncertain assembly scene is the premise and important foundation of robot autonomous learning to obtain action sequence. Therefore, this paper proposes a method of hand assembly action segmentation based on spatiotemporal features. This method takes the RGB-D video in the process of manual assembly demonstration as the research object. Firstly, the assembly scene graph of each video frame is constructed. On this basis, the spatial features of each video frame are extracted by using the graph network model. Then, the multi-stage temporal convolution network is used to process the spatial features in the time dimension to obtain the spatial and temporal features of each video frame. The spatiotemporal features pass through the softmax layer to obtain the recognition results of each frame of video, and the adjacent frames with the same action type are combined to obtain the manual assembly action sequence. This method obtains the temporal relationship between the front and back actions and avoids the problems of unaligned action boundaries and unsmooth action fragments in the hand assembly action segmentation method based on a single spatial feature. The experimental results show that the action editing score is improved from 78.18% to 99.28%, which verifies the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Ship Detection Based on Aerial Images with Modified YOLOv5
abstract: Ship detection is a significant application with aerial image detection, which faces the challenges of data imbalance and rotation of the ship objects while the horizontal annotation boxes have a large amount of redundant information. This paper focuses on the scene of real-time ship inspection and YOLOv5 is selected as the baseline for fast detection and identification. Dynamic data enhancement during the training process is designed via loss feedback, which can alleviate the problem of data imbalance. Considering the rotation characteristics of ships, classification method is used to predict angle and a loss function is proposed based on rotation-aware Pixels-IoU (RA-PIoU). This method can solve the problem of angle periodicity in rotation object detection and improve the accuracy of loss calculation, so as to achieve better detection performance. Further, we construct an aerial image dataset with offshore ships. Experiments on the largescale public dataset HRSC2016 and our own dataset show that the proposed method can significantly improve the real-time ship detection performance.

articleTitle: Research on Early Warning of Temperature Fault of Wind Turbine Converter Based on GA-PSO-BP Neural Network
abstract: In order to solve the effect of fault deterioration on the performance of the converter during the operation of the wind turbine, and to improve the accuracy of its fault prediction, this paper proposes an early warning method for temperature faults of wind turbine converters based on GA-PSO-BP neural network. Firstly, select input variables that are closely related to the temperature of the converter, combine the SCADA system data to build a BP neural network model, and use genetic algorithm and particle swarm algorithm to optimize; Secondly, establish a sliding time window model based on the temperature residual output from the neural network model, to monitor the operation status of the wind turbine converter; Finally, the accuracy of the model was verified through actual operating data of a wind farm in Xinjiang. The results show that the wind turbine converter temperature fault early warning method based on GA-PSO-BP neural network has high accuracy in monitoring the temperature status of the converter, it can effectively identify the abnormal state of the converter, and can realize early fault warning 48 hours in advance. Which is of great significance to the stable operation and safety maintenance of the wind turbine converter.

articleTitle: Model-based Reinforcement Learning Variable Impedance Control for 1-DOF PAM Elbow Exokeleton
abstract: Providing effective physical human-robot interactive control is one of the most important considerations in designing an exoskeleton robot. The purpose of the study is to develop a variable impedance control method for providing a reliable approach to different users to operate the exoskeleton by using interactive torque and a spring-damper model. The proposed method based on a model-based reinforcement learning structure and model predictive control frame, designed a neural network dynamic model to replace the state-action value function and using a linear estimate model to fit the action generated from the agent. Analysis and experiment results indicate that the designed method has less interactive torque and tracking error than the traditional impedance control method. Meanwhile, the results also illustrate the changing process of impedance parameters. The proposed control method sufficiently applies to the 1-DOF PAM elbow exoskeleton system.

articleTitle: A Multi-loop Control Strategy for 5 kW Solid Oxide Fuel Cell Hybrid System
abstract: In this paper, a simple multi-closed Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller is presented for a 5 kW solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) system. Referring to the presented detailed dynamic model, the external load performance, control parameters and control objectives are studied and discussed. In order to achieve the goal of fast load tracing and high efficiency. Then the designed multi-loop control strategy is introduced and its responses on the external load change and system efficiency are investigated. Results show that the presented multi-loop PID control strategy can not only improve the system efficiency, but also gain the fast tracking of the output power.

articleTitle: Classification of benign and malignant lung nodules based on residuals and 3D VNet network
abstract: This paper proposes a classification method of lung nodules combining 3D VNet network and residual network. This method first preprocesses the original CT image and sends it to the VNet network for pulmonary nodules detection. Then the detection results are used to complete the classification of benign and malignant lung nodules through the residual network. Finally, the classification results are output. A large number of experiments have shown that this method can well extract the position information of lung nodules in CT images. Based on the LUNA16 data set, this method has achieved high accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. Numerically, it has achieved better classification results than traditional network models.

articleTitle: Robust SLAM in Dynamic Scenarios Based on Deep Learning and Geometric Constraints
abstract: Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (VSLAM) is critical to autonomous robotic systems. Many impressed slam systems heavily rely on a static environment assumption and face the problem of an erroneous map and wrong poses estimation caused by moving objects. In this paper, we propose a slam method based on the combination of a semantic segmentation network and geometric constraints. First, a real-time light-weight semantic segmentation network is introduced to detect the potential dynamic objects. Then a geometric module including optical flow tracking and epipolar constraints is designed to detect the dynamic points further. Hence, more effective and complete dynamic points considered as outliers are classified and the camera poses based on static points after dynamic points removal are estimated more accurately. Experiments on public datasets are conducted and the experimental results indicate that the adoption of the method proposed in this paper significantly improve the accuracy of pose estimation in highly dynamic scenarios.

articleTitle: A Novel ZVS Interleaved Series-Capacitor Tapped Buck Converter with Low Start-Up Voltage Stress for High Step-Down DC-DC Application
abstract: SC-Buck Converters are widely utilized in high voltage conversion ratio DC-DC applications such as modern communications and industrial equipment. However, the efficiency and the power density of the traditional SC-Buck converter are not high enough to meet application requirements. In addition, the switching tube voltage stress is too high when starting so high voltage resistant switching tube needs to be used, which means that the cost of the circuit is increased. In order to figure out the problem, a novel soft-switched interleaved series-capacitor tapped buck converter is proposed in this article. On the high-voltage side, two switching tubes on the same bridge are connected in parallel with a capacitor. On the low-voltage side, based on the series-capacitance tapping inductor, ZVS for all switching tube is realized by using LC resonator. In this article, the operating strategies of the proposed converter is analyzed, the formula of voltage conversion ratio is derived, and the condition of realizing soft switching is instructed. Finally, a simulation model with input of 24V and output of 1.8V is used to verify the property of this topology.

articleTitle: Optimal State Estimation Using Model-Free Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This article investigates adaptive dynamic programming based optimal state estimation where the effect of inevitable noise is considered. The designed optimal state estimation process conforms to Bellman optimality principle. Based on adaptive dynamic programming, the proposed optimal state estimation method provides the design condition for the Kalman filter gain. A novel model-free reinforcement learning algorithm is proposed to synthesize the Kalman filter gain, which can handle state estimation without the knowledge of system dynamics. A simulation is demonstrated to show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Air Feeding Adaptive Backstepping Sliding Mode Control for Automotive Fuel Cell System
abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) systems have been used in fuel cell vehicles as the main power source. The cathode air mass flow rate regulation for the automotive fuel cell has a vital influence on the dynamic characteristics of the system. The sufficient feeding of air can avoid the oxygen starvation and prevent the service life degradation of the proton exchange membrane. According to the air supply system model, typical linearization points are selected to linearize and obtain the state-space equations. Aiming at tracking the desired air mass flow rate of the PEMFC system, the backstepping sliding mode controller with parameters adaptive adjustment is developed to realize the air feeding control. Moreover, the output current of the automotive PEMFC under the urban dynamometer driving schedule (UDDS) driving condition is used to test the air mass flow rate response and the stability of the presented controller. The simulation results show that the developed controller can maintain the air mass flow rate tracking error at about 0.0003 kg/s by manipulating the air compressor, and the relative error of the oxygen excess ratio (OER) is within 4%.

articleTitle: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Method for Mobile Robot Path Planning in Unknown Environments
abstract: In this paper, a path planning method without global maps for mobile robots is proposed. At present, the traditional path planning methods have become mature. However, most of these methods are based on map information, and complex models need to be defined. To address these issues, we propose an end-to-end path planning model based on deep reinforcement learning, which takes the lidar sequence and depth image as the inputs, and the robot's velocity and angular velocity as the outputs. With the proposed method, the mobile robot can plan the motion path from the initial position to the target position without colliding with the obstacles in the environment. Besides, we propose a neural network that has the ability of multi-sensor information fusion from different dimensions. We build a simulation environment for mobile robot path planning in the gazebo based on Robot Operating System(ROS). Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Synchronization of Multi-Weighted and Directed Network Under Pinning Impulsive Control
abstract: In this paper, multi-weighted and directed complex dynamic networks (MWDCDNs) under the control of hybrid impulses are analyzed. Two cases are considered. In the first case, impulses can be only applied on one fixed node. In the other case, impulses are applied on different nodes according to whether they are synchronized or de-synchronized in MWDCDNs with unbounded time delay. By limiting impulsive interval and Chebyshev distance between the normalized left eigenvectors (NLEVec) of multiple coupling matrices corresponding to the zero eigenvalue, we obtain some criteria for the synchronization of MWDCNs. Some numerical simulation are also given.

articleTitle: Informative Path Planning for AUV-based Underwater Terrain Exploration with a POMDP
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) in underwater terrain exploration applications represent a topic area, and the interesting problem is planning paths to maximize the vehicle information gathered and combining this information to build a complete map. The Gaussian process (GP) is utilized as a basic environment model and updated using the Bayesian data fusion technique with sensor information. A path planning algorithm, which formulates the terrain exploration problem as the finite-horizon partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), is proposed to overcome the limitation of the planner converge to locally suboptimal solutions. In addition, a Monte Carlo Tree Search based on the motion primitives tree (MPT-MCTS) solver is developed to solve this POMDP. The effectiveness of the proposed method is explored in the simulation experiment, and its potential is demonstrated by comparing it with other optimization algorithms.

articleTitle: Feed Rate Control for Robot-assisted Laminectomy based on Milling Sound Pressure Signals
abstract: This paper aims to present a method based on real-time analysis of the milling sound pressure signal(MSPS) to provide a safe highest milling feed rate for the robot-assisted laminectomy. First, we analyze the robot-assisted laminectomy's critical tasks. Then, we discuss the principle of using the MSPS to estimate a safe highest milling feed rate by analyzing the vertebral lamina forced vibration. Next, we propose a sound pressure signal processing method to extract some specific harmonic amplitudes of the MSPS and design a fuzzy controller whose inputs are these harmonic amplitudes to control the milling feed rate. Finally, our validation experiments indicate that the control method can make the milling feed rate adapt to the bone density and the bone cutting depth. The proposed method can reduce the robot-assisted laminectomy's milling time as much as possible while ensuring surgery safety.

articleTitle: Fault Detection Method for Blast Furnace Based on Small-sample Fault Data Generation
abstract: Fault monitoring in ironmaking process is divided into two steps: anomaly detection and fault classification. Compared with anomaly detection, the research of fault classification is very limited due to the lack of fault data. Different from other researches, this paper studies the generation of blast furnace(BF) fault data for the first time. In this paper, we propose a method to generate samples of BF fault data based GAN network. In order to solve the randomness of the data generated by GAN, we introduce the steps of prior knowledge adjustment and data filtering to make the generated fault data closer to the real BF fault data. Finally, the data-driven BF fault classification algorithm can be trained well by using the generated fault data. Real BF operation data are used in this experiment, the results show that the generated fault data can effectively improve the accuracy and stability of the fault classification algorithm.

articleTitle: Computer vision-based method for online measuring the moisture of iron ore green pellets in disc pelletizer
abstract: Iron ore green pellets are widely used in steel industry. In the manufacturing of green pellets in disc pelletizer, the pellet moisture (PM) should be frequently monitored to guarantee product quality. Current methods for PM measurement are off-line and time-consuming, which cannot meet the requirement for real-time measurement and control of pelletizing process. To solve this problem, a computer vision-based method is proposed to online measure the pellet moisture. Firstly, a set of experiments are conducted to capture green pellet images with different moisture. Then, the image features are extracted and sent to polynomial regression for model establishment, so that the PM can be measured by the proposed model. Test on iron ore pellets images demonstrate that the proposed method can measure the PM accurately and only cost 0.361s for each pellet image. The proposed method has advantages in rapid, low cost and non-destructive, and it is helpful to improve the automation level of production process in pelletizer.

articleTitle: Analysis on Mechanics and Magnetic Adsorption of Wheeled Wall-Climbing and Obstacle-Jumping Robot
abstract: In order to meet the needs of working on the inner wall of oil tank, a new wheeled climbing robot with magnetic adsorption ability and obstacle crossing ability was designed. Meanwhile, for meeting the requirements of stable adsorption and safe ability of obstacle crossing, the statics analysis of the wall-climbing robot were carried out, and the safe adsorption force of the wall-climbing robot operating on the wall under different conditions was obtained to avoid slipping and capsizing. The effects of the distance between the magnet and the wall on the adsorption force were analyzed by experiments, and the optimal structure size was obtained to ensure that the robot could be safely adsorbed on the wall during the process of obstacle crossing. The experimental results show that the overall trend of the experimental results is basically consistent with the calculated results. The research results can provide theoretical reference for the mechanical analysis and obstacle-climbing stability of the wheeled wall-climbing robot.

articleTitle: A Tongue Color Classification Method in TCM Based on Transfer Learning
abstract: In the field of TCM tongue diagnosis, the most important feature is the tongue color. Recently, the deep learning method can be used to classify the tongue color, which has been one of the important research directions for the objectification of tongue diagnosis. However, if there is a small amount of training data and low hardware equipment configuration, directly use of the current deep learning methods to classify the tongue color will not achieve satisfactory results. In order to solve these problems, this paper proposes a tongue color classification method in TCM based on transfer learning. This method transfers the model parameters trained on the ImageNet data set to the task of tongue image feature extraction and classification, splits of the tongue image data set is used for training and testing. We have used the obtained depth network to classify the color features of tongue image. Experiments illustrate that this method has good accuracy and short training time, and can better complete the task of tongue color classification.

articleTitle: CPS Attack Detection of Ships using Particle Filter
abstract: In this paper, a method based on particle filter (PF) is proposed to detect the attack on cyber-physical Systems (CPS) of ships. Considering that CPS usually has state delay and Markov property, this paper estimates the markov jumping parameters of the time-series amplified system by particle filter, and estimates the system state by using Kalman filter. The residual evaluation function is designed to detect whether the attack exists. The above method is verified by the real ship data, which proves that the method can be used in the actual CPS attack detection and shows a good detection effect.

articleTitle: An Improvement of Bird Swarm Algorithm and Its Applications
abstract: There are three behaviors in the two levels original bird swarm algorithm (BSA): forage behavior and alert behavior in first level, migration behavior in the second level. In the improved method, a few executing birds with migration behavior is modified in the first level behaviors. 5 different benchmark functions are optimized to verily the effectiveness of the improved method, the results illustrate that the accuracy and convergence speed are both increased. In addition, a case study of neural network is carried out to optimize the weights and thresholds, and the improved BSA achieves smaller errors than the original BSA.

articleTitle: P2P Energy Transaction for Multiple Microgrids Considering Power Flow Constraints
abstract: Energy transactions among multiple microgrids (MMGs) can improve economy and reliability of electricity markets. However, power flow constraints (e.g., voltage tolerance and node balance constraints) with respect to distribution networks (DNs) are usually overlooked for reducing the complexity of energy transaction problems in existing studies. This paper models a bi-level energy trading framework between MMGs and DNs. Firstly, in order to guarantee the safety operation while minimizing the total cost of DNs, full alternative current power flow constraints are considered at the upper level. Then a comprehensive energy trading model for MMGs is established at the lower level. Furthermore, analytical target cascading (ATC) algorithm is applied to solve energy trading problems between MMGs and DNs in a distributed manner. Finally, numerical tests on an IEEE 33-bus distribution system are implemented to demonstrate the performance of our distributed energy transactions method.

articleTitle: Design of Two-Wheeled Self-Balancing Vehicle Based on Fixed-time Observer
abstract: The two-wheeled self-balancing vehicle (TWSBV) is a typical wheeled mobile robot. Since it is a multi-variable, nonlinear, strong coupling, and under-actuated system, the TWSBV is usually used as a benchmark to test control algorithms. The design and control problems of the TWSBV are addressed in this paper. In practical application, the TWSBV may be subjected to external disturbances. Meanwhile, the accurate model parameters of the TWSBV are difficult to be obtained. The model uncertainties and external disturbances are regarded as the lumped perturbation term, which is estimated by a designed fixed-time extended state observer (FXESO). Based on the estimation of the lumped perturbation term, an active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) is developed to compensate for perturbation and stabilize the TWSBV system. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is verified by the TWSBV platform.

articleTitle: Denoising Method for LiDAR Intensity Image via Combining Adaptive Non-local Means and Exponential Soft Thresholding
abstract: Image denoising plays a fundamental role in many computer vision and signal processing tasks. Due to the laser active imaging principle of LiDAR, there is significant speckle noise in LiDAR intensity image. To remove noise and enhance image quality, a new image denosing method based on adaptive non-local means (NLM) and exponential soft thresholding is proposed. First, speckle noise is converted from multiplicative noise to additive noise by homomorphic transform and the tranformed noisy image is decomposed into high-frequency and low-frequency coefficients by discrete wavelet transform (DWT). Second, we present an improved NLM filtering called adaptive NLM to suppress the noise in low-frequency coefficients, and present a new exponential soft thresholding method to remove the noise in high-frequency coefficients. Finally, inverse DWT and homomorphic transform are carried out to reconstruct the denosied intensity image. We take both qualitative and quantitative tests on the proposed method, and make comparisons with three state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method is superior to the other three methods by achieving best trade-off in suppressing noise and keeping details.

articleTitle: Research on sEMG Gesture Recognition Based on Hybrid Dilated Convolutional Neural Network Combining Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit And Attention Mechanism
abstract: Aiming at the problem of low accuracy and large amount of calculation for gesture recognition based on surface electromyography (sEMG),a research method for sEMG gesture recognition based on a hybrid dilated convolution neural network combining bidirectional gated recurrent unit and attention mechanism was proposed.Compared with ordinary CNN,HDC can expand the receptive field,reduce over-fitting,and extract more features by setting the dilation rate to parity hybrid and different sizes. The BiGRU module can extract and process the timing features of the data well, Attention module gives greater weight to important features,they can improve accuracy. The accuracy rates of 92.72 and 97.85 were achieved on the NinaproDB1 dataset and the dataset collected by ourselves, respectively, which proved the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Time-Jerk Optimal Trajectory Planning of Industrial Robot based on Hybrid Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Industrial robots need to execute specific trajectories on production lines, which requires rational planning of robot joint trajectories in Cartesian space. To improve the efficiency and control accuracy of industrial robots, time- jerk multi-objective trajectory optimization is required. The main research of this topic is to apply the particle swarm optimization(PSO) algorithm based on crossover and subgroup to complete the trajectory optimization of a six-degree-of- freedom robot in Cartesian space with time-jerk multi-objective function and compare the optimization effect of the hybrid particle swarm optimization algorithm relative to the traditional particle swarm optimization algorithm. Firstly, a seven segment S-Spline interpolation function is applied to complete the trajectory planning and the basic PSO algorithm is applied to optimize the trajectory for the interpolation time. Then based on the shortcomings of the basic PSO algorithm, the particle swarm optimization algorithm based on crossover and subgroup is proposed to improve the speed and effectiveness of the trajectory optimization algorithm. Finally, simulation experiments show that the total time and joint shocks of robot trajectory planning are greatly reduced, which verifies the effectiveness of the hybrid PSO algorithm applied to robot time-shock optimal trajectory optimization.

articleTitle: Finite-time Circle Formation Control with Collision Avoidance
abstract: In this paper, we study the finite-time circle formation control problem for multiple agents, where each agent is moving freely in a plane and is merely able to perceive the relative position information of a given target and its neighbors, with the aim of converging to the desired circle surrounding the target point at a preset time and maintaining desired distances from their neighbors. To this end, we design a distributed controller which has a good feature that there is no collision among the agents during forming the desired formation. To demonstrate the effectiveness and good performance of our proposed finite-time circle formation controller, we provide both theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Direction-of-Arrival and Range Estimation of Near-Field Sources Based on Subspace Fitting
abstract: A new algorithm is proposed to address the problem of near-field source localization using weighted subspace fitting (WSF) in this paper. Through separating the two parameters of bearings and ranges, the two-dimensional parameter estimation problem is first transformed into one-dimensional parameter estimation problem. The specific method is to construct a Toeplitz-like correlation matrix by using the anti-diagonal elements of the near-field source signal covariance matrix. Then the subspace fitting algorithm of sparse recovery is used to estimate the direction of arrival (DOA). The estimated direction is substituted back to the original near-field source model. After that, the sparse recovery algorithm based on singular value decomposition can be used to calculate the estimated value of the ranges. Computer simulations verify the excellent performance of the algorithm. In addition, the algorithm has lower requirements for SNR and snapshots.

articleTitle: A Novel and High-efficiency Razor Clam Inspired Burrowing Robot that Utilizes Localized Fluidization Mechanism
abstract: Nowadays, as underwater exploration and scientific research become increasingly important, the new underwater equipment puts forward new requirements for the functions of burrowing and anchoring, and hopes to integrate multiple functions. Razor clam can borrow efficiently and anchor firmly by using the local fluidization mechanism. Therefore, we took design inspiration from the razor clam and imitated its structure and movement mechanism to design a burrowing robot. The robot is divided into two parts: the driving part and the end-effector part. The end-effector is the main part of the robot which causes local fluidization of the soil by making its shell move in a radial direction. Through the mechanical analysis of the end-effector part to verify that it can complete the function of efficient burrowing. Let the robot burrows in the soil to explore the relationship between how long it burrows and how deep it burrows, and by testing the situation when the robot does not use the localized fluidization mechanism for burrowing to compared with the previous experiment, which fully verified its efficient burrowing ability and the advantages of this design compared with the normal burrowing equipment. The anchoring force of the robot in the soil is also obtained through experiments. The above experimental results can prove that the design of this robot can meet the requirements of burrowing and anchoring functions.

articleTitle: Interactive and Interpretable Knee Point-Driven Multiobjective Optimization for Multiobjective Decision Making
abstract: In the optimization of real applications, it is challenging to find a representative solution set to cover the whole Pareto optimal front (PoF) of the problems due to the resource-intensive, time-consuming, and complex manifold of the PoF. Accordingly, preference information from the decision makers (DMs) is commonly utilized to guide the optimization process towards the regions of interest (ROIs) on the PoF. However, it is non-trivial for decision makers to articulate preferences without a priori knowledge. To fill the gap, this paper introduces the naturally interesting "knee point" on the PoF into the optimization and designs an interactive knee point driven optimization framework with interpretable preference information, aiming to facilitate DMs in preference articulation, decision making and further investigation on the optimization problems. Experimental results on a number of benchmark problems have verified the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Attitude Tracking Control for Hypersonic Flight Vehicles Based on Sliding Mode Observers
abstract: In this paper, a novel backstepping control scheme based on sliding mode observers is proposed for the attitude system of a hypersonic flight vehicle. By employing sliding mode observers, the estimations of the disturbances and extra dynamics are guaranteed to converge to their exact values in finite time. The control scheme is designed through backstepping approach, which benefits for compensating the mismatched disturbances. Then the Lyapunov stability analysis is given to prove that the closed-loop system which contains the observers, the controller and the vehicle is asymptotically stable with attitude states converging to reference signals. Simulation results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Research on working condition recognition of Cement Precalciner based on Expert System
abstract: The precalciner plays an important in the production of cement. Most cement plants rely on the experiences of operators to control the operations for the production of cement for best quality and control. This paper summarizes the application of an Expert System to recognize the working condition or state of the precalciner of a clinker production unit for a cement plant. An expert system mimics the fore mentioned operator knowledge and experience in the form that a computer understands and give suggestion and strategies for the control system based upon the current state of the system. Simulation shows that the system could determine the state of the precalciner and showed effective inference.

articleTitle: Cooperative Guidance Law for Unpowered Missiles
abstract: In this paper, a novel three-dimensional cooperative guidance law is presented for unpowered missiles. The velocity of missiles without motive force will change and be uncontrolled in the terminal guidance stage. Relative range and closing speed between missiles and target are taken as coordination variables rather than estimate time-to-go in the design of the cooperative control law. The whole guidance process is divided into two phases. Specifically, the first phase utilizes distributed tracking control law and integral sliding mode (ISM) protocol to achieve consistency of coordinate variables under disturbance. When the coordination variables tend to be consistent, missiles attack the target under proportional navigation guidance (PNG) law. The simulation results show that the cooperative guidance law can effectively attack the target simultaneously.

articleTitle: Evolutionary Optimization of Robust Multi-objective Expensive Problems Assisted by Incremental Kriging Models
abstract: There are many multi-objective and multi-constrained robust optimization problems in engineering design field, and their inputs or parameters are often uncertain. The two-level robust optimization is widely used in the field of robust optimization to obtain the optimal solutions which are less sensitive to uncertainties.
