The electric pole and insulating cross arms are preliminarily detected based on the geometric features, and then the geometric constraints between the electric pole and cross arms are used to iteratively optimize the recognition results by the least square method. Using the geometric information provided by the obtained structure composed of the electrical pole and cross arms, the point cloud of power lines is further processed to recognize them. Experiments show that the proposed approach can segment and recongnize the electric poles, cross arms and power lines from the LiDAR point cloud of the operation area quickly, accurately and robustly, providing sufficient information for the robot to perform various subsequent operation tasks.

Author Keywords: live working robots for distribution networks

articleTitle: Multi-label Constitution Identification Based on Tongue Image in Traditional Chinese Medicine
abstract: Constitution identification is an important research topic in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), which is the basis of health management and disease prevention. Tongue diagnosis is one of the common methods in TCM treatment. Combining knowledge of Traditional Chinese Medicine and computer technology to analyze tongue images can identify constitution objectively and effectively. The existing intelligent constitution identification algorithms can give only one constitution result for each tongue image. However, in the actual process of constitution identification, individuals often present two or more constitutions. In this paper, a multi-label classification method is used to identify the composite constitution of tongue images, and the feature extraction performance of four different networks is compared. The idea of complex perception is applied to the DenseNet-121 network, and the applicable condition of the classification method based on complex perception is given through experiments.

articleTitle: Parallel Current Sharing Control Algorithm Of Four Phase Interleaved Boost Converter
abstract: Interleaved boost converters are widely used in hydrogen fuel cell vehicles due to their good performance. In this paper, a parallel current sharing control algorithm of four phase interleaved Boost converter was proposed based on fuzzy control algorithm. The simulation model of topology control system of four phase interleaved parallel Boost converter was established by using MATLAB simulation tool. The parallel current sharing algorithm and fuzzy control parallel current sharing algorithm were used to control the four phase interleaved parallel Boost converter, and the influence of these two different algorithms on the system was analyzed. By comparing the simulation results, it was found that the system response speed was accelerated, the overshoot was decreased, and the output current ripple and voltage are decreased, which proved the superiority of the proposed control algorithm.

articleTitle: Controller design and analysis of active suspension system in frequency domain
abstract: Several control methods have been developed to improve the vehicle’s dynamic performance and, specifically, its active suspension system. Most of the existing researches are carried out in the time domain. However, from the point of view of practical problems, the system’s stability and anti-disturbance can be described more intuitively in the frequency domain. Hence, this paper analyzes and designs a quarter-car active suspension system operating in the frequency domain. First, by choosing as input the road disturbance and the body acceleration as the output, we establish the corresponding transfer function of the quarter-car active suspension system. Then, we design a PI controller where the controller’s parameter ranges are obtained by the Routh criterion, which guarantees the closed-loop system’s stability. Finally, we demonstrate our method’s effectiveness through a comparative analysis of several simulation results.

articleTitle: Temporal Enhanced Multi-Stream Graph Convolutional Nerual Networks For Skeleton-Based Action Recognition
abstract: Compared with image sequence, skeleton sequence is an ideal choice for human action recognition because of no redundant information and lightweight data. Recently,a tremendous breakthrough in skeleton-based human activity recognition methods. By way of illustration, Spatial- Temporal Graph Convolutional Networks (ST-GCN) creatively distill the information of human joints into the structure of a graph and Two-Stream Adaptive Graph Convolutional Networks (2S-AGCN) propose to use the length and orientation information of bones and combine it with joint information to predict in an explicit way. However there are still some issues exist in these GCN-based models. The model lacks long-term dependency modeling capabilities and does not explore the deep correlation between joints and bones. In this work, we propose a temporal enhanced multi-stream graph convolutional nerual networks (TAMS-GCN) for skeleton-based action recognition.We combine the temporal attention module with a graph convolutional neural network to extract skeletal information of each frame and actively incorporates it into the global features by global pooling of all joints for each frame to acquire attention at the frame level of the action. In addition we propose a fusion network of joint and bone information that implicitly learns the connection between joints and bones, increasing the compactness between joints and bones. We tested our TAMS-GCN model on NTU-RGBD datasets, the model achieves excellent performance compared to the state-of-the-art.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Online Detection System for Anode Current Distribution in Aluminum Reduction Cell
abstract: With the urgent demand for reducing carbon emissions brought by global climate change, the digital transformation of process industry has been accelerated to minimize the carbon emissions of all segments of the production process. For aluminum reduction process, anode current distribution is a very important parameter, which is closely related to the stability and energy saving level of the aluminum reduction cell. The current manual measurement method has problems such as large error and data lag. It is necessary to develop an online detection system suitable for high temperature, strong magnetic, corrosive gas and narrow space to meet the needs of digital transformation of aluminum reduction plant. This paper presents an online detection system of anode current distribution based on distributed sensor network. The system is composed of the single guide rod monitoring modules, main controller and human-computer interaction unit. Experimental results in industrial site show that the method proposed in this thesis realizes the online monitoring of anode current distribution data with low cost and high reliability.

articleTitle: The Discrete Sliding Mode Control for a Hypersonic Vehicle
abstract: A novel control algorithm is proposed for a hypersonic vehicle (HV) based on discrete sliding mode control and parameterization. Unlike traditional sliding mode control of the HV, which requires the use of input and output feedback linearization to decouple the nonlinear system, the discrete sliding mode control law is designed on the basis of a linear structure model. The switching function is firstly designed, and then the control law is designed according to the exponential reaching rate. In addition, the adaptive law and the power function are introduced to suppress the chattering of the closed-loop system. Comparison of simulation results verifies the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: Research on Adaptive Speed Control of Marine Diesel Engine based on Discrete Time Integral Minimal Control Synthesis
abstract: The marine diesel engine propulsion system is a nonlinear, time-varying, and uncertain system. A new method based on the discrete-time minimal control synthesis algorithm (DTMCSI) is proposed to address the problems of long controller parameters adjustment cycles and degradation of dynamic speed regulation performance when its structure or parameters are changed. It can achieve accurate control of engine speed without any a priori knowledge of object parameters. Firstly, the response relationship between the speed and the fuel injection is modeled based on the idea of mean value modeling of diesel engines. Then, a speed control strategy for DTMCSI was designed. The resulting control strategy seems simple enough to adjust the engine speed quickly and precisely. The tracking performance is compared with that obtained with a standard PID controller. Simulation results show that this control method can improve the precision of engine speed control. In addition, the calibration of control parameters can be greatly reduced.

articleTitle: A novel sliding mode based nonlinear tracking differentiator for filtering noise
abstract: Obtaining reliable signals and their derivatives is important from noisy input signals. Toward this problem, this paper presents a novel nonlinear tracking differentiator (TD-N) based on sliding mode for filtering the noise of input signals and estimating their derivatives. TD-N is an improvement of Denis et al.’s nonlinear tracking differentiator by adopting a sigmoid function and a power function to balance the trade-off between filtering performance and responding speed. The validity of TD-N is evaluated through Numerical simulation examples.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Automatic Berthing of the Underactuated Twin-propeller Twin-Rudder Ship
abstract: In order to cope with the problem that the automatic berthing control of the underactuated ship cannot track any path, this paper proposes an automatic berthing method for underactuated twin-propeller twin-rudder ships based on the nonlinear model predictive control. Through establishing the ship berthing maneuvering constrained optimization model, the time sequences of the control commands are obtained based on the rolling optimization feature of the model predictive control. Through numerical simulation of forward berthing and U-turn berthing, which are the two typical berthing methods, the effectiveness and adaptability of the proposed control method are verified. The research results can provide references for the berthing control design of the underactuated ship.

articleTitle: A trajectory tracking control method for quadruped robot based on limit value
abstract: During the walking process of the quadruped robot according to the foot trajectory, due to the rapid acceleration and deceleration process of the joint motor, the torque of the motor changes too sharply, which causes the problem of high-frequency vibration of the fuselage. Therefore, in order to solve this problem, the foot-end trajectory function of the quadruped robot is combined with the leg inverse kinematics function, the function between the rotation angle of each joint motor and time is obtained, then find the derivative of the motor rotation angle concerning time, and the limit value point is used as the control time node. The joint motor is controlled by the fuzzy PID method, which solves the problem of commutation torque impact under different loads and reduces the trajectory tracking error. The overshoot of the system response was reduced from 24.6% to 17.0%, the adjustment time was reduced by 45.2%, and the experimental conclusions were verified through actual tests.

articleTitle: EEG-based Functional Brain Connectivity during Crossroad Passing Driving-A pilot study
abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG) based driving intention recognition is a key issue for brain computer interface based driver assistance system. It is a major challenge to mining and extraction the features of EEG signals during driving and achieve a better detection for driving intention. Current studies mainly focus on few channels in sensorimotor area. The purpose of this work is to study the cooperation mechanism between different brain regions during the steering process and extraction the spatial features. Functional brain network is an excellent tool for exploring the spatial features and based on a stimulated driving experiment, the network for 5 pilot subjects were constructed using mutual information. After a threshold filter, network structure and parameters were calculated. Results show that network’s topology structure represents significant contralateral differences during different steering action. Statistical analysis of the connection weight shows that there was significant difference of the connection weights in some regions between different steering process. But the values of network parameters are very close and there was no significant difference. This study provides a novel insight of spatial feature extraction and could be beneficial for improving the classification accuracy of steering intention detection.

articleTitle: Flare Soot Monitoring Based on Thermal Infrared Image Processing and Attention-based Meta-learning
abstract: Industrial enterprises, such as thermal power plants and petrochemical factories, use the flare stack to eliminate volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emerged in the production process. Through complete burning of the flare gas, the flare stack manages to prevent air pollution and protect the safety of the plants. The monitoring of the flare stack is of great importance for the reason that uncomplete combustion will endanger the environment and even people’s lives. In this study, an effective and intelligent flare soot monitoring system has been designed to deal with this situation. Unlike some existing work, the proposed monitoring system tries to identify combustion status of the flare gas through both RGB image and thermal infrared image (see Fig. 1). The new designed system can monitor the flare soot without concerning the light and weather conditions. Further more, we also constructed a deep neural model based on attention mechanisms and meta-learning to cooperate the problem of lacking sufficient black smoke samples. Experimental results showed that the devised monitoring system can recognize black smoke through videos of flare combustion timely and accurately regardless of the light and weather.

articleTitle: The Low Carbon Pickup and Delivery Problem with Time Windows and its Optimization Approach
abstract: Pickup and delivery problem is commonly exist in logistics system, and its optimization considering time windows is essential in practical application. Meanwhile, with the increasing awareness of environmental protection, carbon emissions should also be considered during the routing design. In this paper, a low-carbon model is introduced for the pickup and delivery problem with time windows; a division method is proposed for the different delivery costs of logistics customers in different regions; a capacity constraint processing approach is proposed to solve the capacity of the vehicle during driving. Since the requirements for the logistic system are described by several objective formulations, the multi-objective approach is adopted to solve the optimization problem. The experiment selects two sets of Shanghai logistics data at different scales. Feasible solutions with advantages of different expectations can be obtained from the experiment result.

articleTitle: Abnormal Data Identification and Cleaning Method of Wind Turbine Based on Multi-model Fusion
abstract: With the rapid development of the installed capacity of wind turbines in the world, the problem of collecting and processing massive data in wind farms has become increasingly prominent. There are many clusters in the wind turbine data, which changes the original characteristics of the wind farm operation data. These outliers lead to the failure to accurately model the power curve, leads to adverse effects on turbine power prediction and optimal control of the power system. This paper analyzes the characteristics of abnormal data of wind turbines. Then, a fusion rule, polynomial fitting, and DBSCAN clustering algorithm are proposed to identify outliers. First, the exception data is filtered by rules. Then the method of linear fitting and DBSCAN clustering was used to identify and screen out abnormal data. Finally, A case study of anomalous values in historical data of six wind turbines from different wind farms was conducted. The results demonstrate that the proposed method is effective in identifying anomalous data and that the performance of the method is insensitive to the wind turbine parameters, so that it can be used in different wind farms.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fuzzy Control for Active Suspension Systems with Time-Varying Displacement and Speed Constraints
abstract: In this article, an adaptive backstepping fuzzy control strategy is proposed for the active suspension systems (ASSs) with the time-varying constraints. The fuzzy-logic control is used to tackle unknown mass of the ASSs. When the constraint is violated, the stability and safety of the ASSs will be reduced. Thus, the Barrier Lyapunov functions are used to show the closed-loop system’s stability by ensuring that the time-varying restrictions are not broken. Finally, numerical simulations are presented to confirm effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Development of a triboelectric palm-like sensor aiming at underwater perceptual construction
abstract: Marine mammals relying on tactile still maintain a remarkably high prey capture rate without visual or acoustic detection. A similar ability has not been fully developed in artificial perceptual systems of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUV) to gather information about physical objects. A palm-like tactile sensor based on a triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG), aiming at constructing an underwater perceptual system, is designed in this paper. The proposed device mimics the structure of the palm of a sea otter, and its neural structure can also provide clues confirming the importance of tactile information. It is composed of a triboelectric sensor unit for sensing external stimuli, flexible support, fixed frame, upper hatch cover for sealing, and flexible cover. With palm structure and TENG assistance, the tactile sensor can detect the external load magnitude and approximate the external stimulation area without the effect of contact frequency. The experimental results demonstrated that a triboelectric tactile sensor is a promising tool for integration into AUVs’ grippers.

articleTitle: Design of Integral Sliding Mode Controller with Fuzzy Switching Gain Adjustment for Morphing Aircraft
abstract: The morphing aircraft can obtain the best aerodynamic characteristics by changing its shape in order to adapt to the current mission and environment. In this paper, a non-affine parameter-dependent linear variable parameter (LPV) system model of a morphing aircraft whose wingspan and sweep angle can be changed is used as the object. First, the linear fractional form (LFR) is used to design an integral sliding mode that converges in a finite time. Then, the fuzzy switching gain adjustment method is introduced to eliminate the interference items and uncertain items in the nonlinear system. The simulation results show that the method can ensure the stability of the variant process in the presence of large disturbances and uncertainties. This controller design method has universal adaptability to LPV system.

articleTitle: Variable speed trajectory prediction method of dynamic prosthesis based on improved SeqGAN
abstract: The speed control of dynamic prosthetic needs virtual constraint to provide control standard, which is mainly provided by fitting regression algorithm at present, but there are still three problems to be solved. The fitting regression method has poor tolerance to the effective error of human motion. At the same time, it needs to not only measure the precise speed, but also collect a large amount of data at different speeds to deal with the problem of speed change. SeqGAN is usually used to deal with discrete text data. The main body of the prediction network is LSTM network, which can deal with more complex continuous sequence prediction. In this paper, SeqGAN is improved to the Feature Generative Adversarial Nets(F-SeqGAN), we collecte the data of constant speed walking joints of the experimental subjects in the discrete speed dimension, to predicte the change of knee and ankle joint angles in the next time stage by the change data of thigh joint angles in the last time stage, avoiding speed judgment and realize speed smooth variable speed trajectory prediction. Compared with Gaussian Process Regression method, it has advantages.

articleTitle: A Novel Active Power Regulation Strategy Based on SMC-Consensus Algorithm for Islanded Microgrid
abstract: Nowadays, in the islanded microgrid (IMG), the active power sharing is an important issue. To realize the reasonable sharing of active power among energy resources considering the economical operation and pollutant emission, a power regulation strategy based on sliding mode controller (SMC) and consensus algorithm is proposed in this paper. The design process is as below: firstly, a novel consensus algorithm combining with SMC is proposed. Then, on the basis of the designed consensus algorithm, a novel power regulation strategy is proposed, which can share the active power economically among resources with reducing pollutant emission. Finally, the related case tests are provided to confirm the effect of the novel regulation strategy.

articleTitle: Comparison of long-term load forecasting methods for air conditioning system of a large building
abstract: In order to solve the problem of increasing energy consumption of central air conditioning system in large buildings, it has become a consensus to use group control algorithm to save energy for central air conditioning system. In order to implement the algorithm in the central air conditioning system with large delay, the prediction algorithm is usually used to get the cooling load at the next moment as the control basis. When designing a load prediction algorithm for a large building in Shanghai, we hope to get a method to continuously predict the subsequent load based on the operation data of a long history. In this paper, we choose three more suitable prediction methods, Support Vector Regression (SVR) prediction, BP neural network prediction and Exponential Weighted Moving Average(EWMA) prediction. These three methods are used to predict, and the results are compared in four aspects: operation speed, prediction accuracy, practicability and feasibility. The results show that the SVR model is better than the other two in long-term load forecasting, and is more suitable for load forecasting in this kind of scenarios.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Compensation Capacitor in Joint-less Track Circuit via Long Short-Term Memory Network
abstract: The fault detection and diagnosis of compensation capacitors in the ZPW-2000 Joint-less Track Circuit (JTC) are quite crucial and challenging for Chinese railway safety. In this work, we present a novel method based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network for the compensation capacitor disconnection fault detection. We tackle the problem based on the compensation capacitors relationship in spatial dimension and the temporal correlation between the normal and fault state of the capacitors. Specifically, to acquire more realistic sequence data, the JTC is firstly modeled and verified with measured data, and then extract the feature data from shunt current based on the JTC model. The obtained data are fed into the LSTM network to detect the compensation capacitor disconnection fault. The experiments show that the proposed method achieves competitive and robust results.

articleTitle: Bio-inspired Coral-like Sensor Aiming at Ocean Wave Monitoring
abstract: Since designing efficient ocean wave sensors for marine engineering is still a challenge, in this paper, a self-powered bionic coral wave sensor (BCWS) based on a triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) is proposed, which aims at wave detection for marine engineering construction, marine resource development, and marine disaster warning. The BCWS consists of coral tentacles, buoyancy disc, spring, counterweight mechanism, and perceiving units (60mm in length, 10mm in width, and 1.5mm in thickness) with multi-modal motions and encapsulates inside the coral tentacles through flexible rubber joints. Meanwhile, the unique structure of BCWS can not only eliminate the influence of seawater on the sensor output performance but also realize the three-dimensional perception of wave information. The analysis of experimental data reveals that BCWS perceive wave direction, wave height, wave frequency, and wave period with millimeter accuracy. Therefore, this novel BCWS can provide an intelligent solution for modern marine engineering.

articleTitle: Research and application of automated test for background program of railway CTC system
abstract: Railway CTC (Centralized Train Control) system is widely applied in dispatching centers and stations of various railway bureaus for train operation dispatching and command. In order to overcome the shortcomings of existing test strategies for background program of railway CTC system, this paper propose a new automated test strategy. In this strategy, four types of logfiles are added into the logging module of all CTC system background programs for automated test. An automated test tool "Testmidware" is newly developed. With the "Testmidware" and prerecorded test scripts, testers can conduct a complete automated regression test on all the existing functions of the background program. The automated test strategy proposed in this paper has been applied in practical work, which effectively reduces the manpower, greatly improves the test efficiency, and ensures the software release on schedule.

articleTitle: A new laser-based loop detection method for laneway environment 3D mapping
abstract: This paper presents a 3D SLAM loop detection method for the mapping of laneway environment within lidar scans. Attuned to the fact that laneway settings such as underground mines, long corridors, and long tunnels, are often low-featured narrow tunnel-like environment without GPS availability and poor light condition. The proposed method solves the difficulty of feature extraction in laneway environment by encoding keyframe scans. Furthermore, the similarity score of encoded scans for matching is calculated in an efficient way, which enables the real-time loop detection mechanism while reverse revisiting is encountered in laneway environment. The proposed method is evaluated on datasets gathered from a long corridor environment.

articleTitle: Bayesian Robust Tucker Decomposition for Multiway Data Analysis
abstract: Tensor decomposition is an effective tool for dealing with higher-order data. Recently, robust tensor decomposition has demonstrated its powerful ability to fit higher-order data and combat noise for multiway data analysis. In this paper, we propose a Bayesian Robust Tucker Decomposition (BRTD) method which can automatically determine an optimal multi-linear rank for Tucker model without tuning any parameters. Specifically, for the generative process, we specify a hierarchical sparsity-inducing prior for automatic rank determination. For Bayesian inference, we present a variational Bayesian framework for BRTD model learning. Experimental results on the simulated and real surveillance video datasets demonstrate its superiority over other state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Short-term Gas Load Forecast based on TCN-BiGRU
abstract: With the fast development of natural gas in China, short-term gas load forecasting plays a vital role in gas companies, which guides gas purchases. Gas usage is usually affected by various factors such as temperature, humidity, holidays, etc., which bring instability and randomness to gas consumption and increase the difficulty of gas load forecasting. This paper introduces a short-term gas load forecasting method based on Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) and a Bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU) neural network. This paper adopts the sliding window method. The sliding window has a fixed length. It is used to process gas data, combining Temporal Convolutional Network and Bidirectional gated recurrent unit. Finally, a fully connected layer is applied to export the load prediction results. The proposed method is employed to predict daily gas consumption based on the real data and compared with the most advanced way. The result shows that the prediction error of the developed method is the lowest, thus outperforming the other methods. The method can be also applied to learn other amount of energy such as wind and electric energy.

articleTitle: A parameter based transfer learning fault diagnosis method under different working conditions
abstract: In industrial applications, equipment is often worked under multiple working conditions, making it prone to various failures. Because of the lack of enough training data, the use of data-driven fault diagnosis methods is often restricted. In this paper, to address such a problem, a parameter based transfer learning(TL) method for few-shot fault diagnosis under different working conditions is proposed. In the methodology, Marginal Distribution Adaptation (MDA) is first used to decrease the divergence via minimizing the maximum mean distance between two marginal distributions of target and source domain. Then, the fault diagnosis model is built by training the from new target domain dataset and new source domain dataset. Finally, part of new target domain dataset are used to test the diagnosis accuracy of the model. Experimental results on bearing benchmark data sets from the University of Ottawa validate the proposed method. Compared with other effective fault diagnosis approaches reported in the literature, the proposed method can obtain higher diagnosis recognition rates and stronger robustness.

articleTitle: Adaptive coherent noise suppression for three-axis fluxgate sensor
abstract: The variation of geomagnetic field greatly increases the difficulty of magnetic anomaly detection. This paper propose an improved adaptive coherent noise suppression(ACNS) method, which provides an effective denoising method for magnetic anomaly detection. Firstly, the signal of three-axis fluxgate sensor and their total magnetic field signal are denoised by the ACNS method, secondly, the four groups of signal above are summed by the adaptive weighted summation method, and then we use OBF algorithm to get the energy of the signal, achieve the goal of magnetic anomaly detection. Finally, the experimental results show that the improved method in this paper has better denoising effect than the original method, and the magnetic anomaly can be detected better by OBF algorithm after using the improved ACNS algorithm.

articleTitle: Emergency Medical Terminal Delivery Optimization based on Improved A* Algorithm
abstract: The paper addresses a novel way to solve the emergent medical delivery problem based on UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicles) and proposes a path search strategy based on Improved A* algorithm with following features. First, the strategy uses a grid method to construct a raster model of the flight airspace to analyze the pharmaceutical logistics UAV performance constraints. Second, the strategy integrates various influencing factors and designs specific improvement plans of the A* algorithm and its implementation process. Third, the path search strategy is base on the Improved A* algorithm for pharmaceutical logistics UAV transportation. Finally, the path planning simulation is carried out to verify the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: A vehicle autonomous positioning technology based on terrain relative navigation
abstract: Considering the characteristics of satellite navigation signals that are vulnerable to occlusion, interference and deception, and the situation that satellite navigation signals can-not be received in complex environments, this paper proposes a vehicle autonomous positioning method based on terrain relative navigation. This method matches the terrain data collected by the vehicle during driving with the pre-established topographic map, so as to estimate the position of the vehicle in the topographic map and realize the positioning of the vehicle on the structured road. The positioning process does not rely on GNSS, and is less affected by other factors due to the main use of road terrain information. This paper uses the constructed topographic map and sampling data to realize the vehicle positioning on the road, and the positioning error is less than 1 meter.

articleTitle: IMU-based Locomotion Mode Recognition by Deep Convolutional Neural Networks with Wide First-layer Kernels
abstract: In this paper, the locomotion mode recognition problem with single inertial measurement unit (IMU) is investigated by developing the novel deep convolutional neural network (CNN) learning models. More precisely, the novel wide first-layer kernels and skip connections are adopted in the CNN model for better feature selection on IMU signals. Based on the measurement data of nine locomotion modes, our experiment results have shown that the employed method can achieve well classification results with high robustness and generalization ability.

articleTitle: SC-RegNet: Unsupervised Self-Calibrated 3D Biomedical Image Registration Network
abstract: Deformable image registration is critical in many biomedical image analysis tasks. Traditional registration algorithms involve a time-consuming iterative optimization process. Most deep learning-based registration networks follow the U-Net shape encoding-decoding architecture, and their downsampling layers are shallow, making it difficult to obtain sufficient semantic information with a small receptive field. In this work, we extend the self-calibrated convolution applied to tasks such as 2D target detection to the encoding stage of 3D image registration networks. The proposed SC-RegNet can get more semantic information to make up for the existing registration networks in an unsupervised training manner while not introducing additional parameters. We evaluated SC-RegNet on two public available human Brain MRI datasets: LPBA40 and IBSR18, and a private mouse brain dataset. The experimental results show the superiority of SC-RegNet over the SOTA image registration methods with no extra time-consuming.

articleTitle: Temperature Compensation for Fiber Optic Gyroscope Based on Bayesian Optimized : Support Vector Regression
abstract: In this paper, the temperature compensation method of Fiber Optic Gyroscope (FOG) based on Bayesian Optimization Support Vector Regression (BO-SVR) is proposed, which can improve the working accuracy of FOG in the temperature changing environment. According to the nonlinear characteristics of temperature drift with zero bias and hysteresis of temperature rise and fall, a piecewise Support Vector Regression (SVR) model of temperature rise and fall is constructed. In order to improve the modeling accuracy, the penalty parameter C and kernel function parameters of BO-SVR are introduced for optimization. The experiment of temperature compensation in the range of –40<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>C to 60<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>C is verified by medium precision FOG, and compared with the results of neural network compensation method, the results show that Bayesian optimization algorithm can reduce the time delay of temperature change for BO-SVR model.

articleTitle: Semi-direct Visual SLAM Algorithm Based on Improved Keyframe Selection
abstract: In order to meet the continuous improvement of real-time performance, positioning accuracy and robustness for visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM), and to address the problem that sparse maps are difficult to directly use for autonomous navigation, a semi-direct visual SLAM algorithm based on improved keyframe selection is proposed. It is based on ORB-SLAM2 framework. The front-end fuses feature-based method and direct method to get the camera initial poses. By minimizing the re-projection error to optimize the pose, it obtains a more accurate pose estimation. The proposed redundant keyframe deletion algorithm is applied in the back-end. It is based on the relative motion distance between keyframes, so as to delete the keyframes with overlapping visual fields and reduce the number of keyframes. The filtered keyframes are used for closed-loop detection and dense point cloud map construction. Then the map is filtered and converted into an octree map with higher storage efficiency. Experiments show that the algorithm can improve the real-time performance while ensuring the positioning accuracy, and has strong robustness to the sparse texture or camera’s fast-moving scene, and it can reconstruct the 3D maps of different environment.

articleTitle: Hybrid observer design for nonlinear systems with unknown inputs
abstract: In this paper we investigate the observer design for a class of nonlinear systems with unknown inputs. A novel hybrid observer integrating both the flow and jump dynamics is proposed. The proposed observer is implemented easily since the flexibility of the impulsive time sequence. The efficiency and superiority of the proposed observer herein are demonstrated via two simulation results.

articleTitle: Gaussian pseudospectral optimization method with smoothing penalty function path constraint handling for UAV obstacle avoidance planning
abstract: Trajectory planning is an important basis for autonomous flight of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). A Gaussian pseudospectral trajectory planning algorithm based on smoothing penalty function is proposed. Firstly, the boundary conditions and dynamic constraints of UAV are considered, and the path constraints are studied to establish the trajectory planning dynamic optimization model. Then, smoothing function is introduced to tackle the path constraints and this method is employed to transform the converted constraints. Combined with Gauss-Legendre collocation, the proposed method is given in detail. Finally, simulation experiment is carried out on UAV model. After the simulation experiment, the proposed method has better path constraints satisfaction and performance index than those of traditional Gaussian pseudospectral method.

articleTitle: A Detection Method for Parkinson’s Hand Tremor Based on Machine Learning
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a common neurode-generative disease, which threatens people’s health seriously. Advanced artificial intelligence methods such as machine learning provide a new way for the diagnosis of PD, so it has become a hot topic of concern. This paper proposes a method to expand the hand tremor data set by Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), extracts the characteristics of tremor data by Discrete Wavelet Transform-Singular Value Decomposition (DWT-SVD), and finally utilizes multiple classification by Support Vector Machine (SVM) to realize the detection of Parkinson’s disease.

articleTitle: Data-Driven MPC for Linear Systems using Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel scheme to solve the optimal control problem for unknown linear systems in a data driven manner. The method doesn’t require any prior knowledge of the system, and only utilizes past input-output trajectories to describe the system features implicitly and realize the prediction on the basis of behavioral systems theory. Meanwhile, we adopt reinforcement learning to update the terminal cost function online to ensure the closed-loop stability. The merit of the proposed scheme is the avoiding of the system identification process and the complex design process of terminal cost, terminal set and terminal controller in the standard MPC. We verify the performance of the algorithm by simulation.

articleTitle: Event-triggered quantized consensus of scalar linear multi-agent systems with packet losses
abstract: This paper studies the event-triggered quantized consensus problem for discrete-time scalar linear multi-agent systems. Due to the limited communication resources, the information exchanged among neighboring agents should be quantized into finite bits and transmitted over an unreliable digital network suffers from dropouts. The existence of nondeterministic packet losses exacerbates the effect of quantization error and damages the consensus performance. To handle these issues, an event-triggering strategy including a local event-triggering function for each agent and a dynamic quantizing-updating method is designed. It is theoretically proved that the estimation error is always bounded by an enlarged event-triggering function and the asymptotic consensus of concerned systems can be guaranteed at a finite bit rate. A simulation example is provided to confirm the effectiveness of our event-triggered control protocol. It shows that the communication frequency among neighbors can be reduced a lot while guaranteeing the system performance.

articleTitle: Clustering Analysis Based on Short Video Content Producers
abstract: With the popularity of smart phones and the acceleration of people’s lives, short video apps like Douyin, Kuaishou, and Bilibili have become substitutes for current content and social media. This article conducts research from the perspective of short video content producers, selects the Bilibili platform, crawls the basic information of Bilibili users, and extracts the relevant characteristics of the short video content producers, including the total number of videos played, the number of videos, rank, number of fans, number of likes. k-means++ clustering analysis is performed on short video content producers. In the cluster analysis, the better number of clusters is obtained according to the intra-cluster error variance (SSE) and Silhouette Coefficient k, then The short video content producers of the Bilibili Platform are grouped into k clusters, and finally the potential correlation between the features and the clustering results is found, and feature differences between different groups of short video producers are compared.

articleTitle: PI double closed-loop single-phase inverter control technology based on rotating coordinate system
abstract: A single-phase inverter is a power supply device that converts direct current into single-phase alternating current. Since the feedback information of the inverter is AC sinusoidal signal, the PI control method under the traditional static coordinate system cannot realize the sinusoidal signal of tracking feedback without static error, so this paper adopts the synchronous rotating coordinate system to realize the PI controller's high-precision tracking of the sinusoidal signal, and improved the traditional generalized second-order integration algorithm that is commonly used to generate orthogonal virtual axes without the influence of low-frequency attenuation . Due to the existence of the virtual impedance of the inverter, the output voltage will be distorted under the impact of harmonic currents. For this reason, this article reduces the equivalent inductance of the filter system at the output by adding a current inner loop controller, which improves the system’s dynamic response to current changes and also reduces the virtual impedance of the inverter, so as to achieve the purpose of correcting the voltage waveform. Finally, through the establishment of a simulation platform and a physical platform, use linear load and non-linear load to load test the inverter output voltage. The experimental results show that the inverter using the PI double-loop control algorithm based on the rotating coordinate system has excellent load adaptability.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Sliding Mode Control for DC-DC Buck Converters Subject to Time-Varying Disturbances
abstract: A composite integral sliding mode controller (CISMC) is investigated for buck converter systems under various disturbances. The disturbances, such as unknown input voltage fluctuations and resistance uncertainties, enter converter system from both matched and mismatched channels, which severely degrade the system performance. The proposed CISMC consists of a disturbance observer with finite-time convergence performance (FTDO) and an sliding mode controller in integral form (ISMC). Constructing a new modified integral sliding mode surface that contains disturbance estimations, the effects of mismatched disturbances can be eliminated. Using this composite method, the output error of converters can accurately converge to zero in finite time. Therefore, this algorithm can adapt the converters to the applications requiring higher steady-state and dynamic performance. A rigorous stability analysis and simulation results under the condition of multiple time-varying disturbances is given to prove the effectiveness of CISMC.

articleTitle: Research on Recognition Method of Life Electroshock Based on Otsu and RBF
abstract: Three-level leakage protection is often used in low voltage distribution networks in China. In order to achieve the differential protection, the set value of the third-level leakage protection, i.e. the total protection, is set to be larger than the fatal current of the human body. Its action criterion does not consider whether the object of electroshock is a life or not, so there is a blind area of electroshock protection for the life. This paper studies the existing action criteria of leakage protectors and their defects in the third-level leakage protection, and puts forward a method to identify the types of electroshock by using Otsu and RBF (Radial Basis Function) neural network. When electroshock occurs to a life body, the leakage protector is immediately tripped without regard to the magnitude of the electroshock current. It solves the problem of the protection blind area in the third-level leakage protection. The software simulation model is built to get the shock current waveforms of life and non-life body. At the same time, a physical prototype of a leakage protector is developed. The test and validation of the proposed method show that the method has a strong anti-jamming ability. The recognition time of shock type is less than 80 ms, and the correct rate is 95%.

articleTitle: Distributed Formation Control of Multiple Mobile Robots: An Adaptive Event-triggered Approach
abstract: In our work, the distributed formation issues for mobile robots are discussed. In particular, a novel adaptive even- triggered communication strategy is investigated to improve the information exchange efficiency among neighboring robots. With the aid of Lyapunov-Krasovskii method, sufficient configuration formation criterions are established by convex optimization. Subsequently, the event-triggered parameters along with formation controller parameters can be developed, respectively. At last, the validity of our proposed formation design is validated via an illustrate example.

articleTitle: Neuroadaptive Distributed State Feedback Cooperative Control for Multiple Surface Vessels with Input Constraints
abstract: In this paper, neuroadaptive distributed state feed-back cooperative control method for multiple surface vessels(MSVs) with the condition of position and velocity are known, unknown time-varying environmental disturbances, model parameter uncertainties and input saturation is proposed. Firstly, a neuroadaptive estimator is designed to estimate the composite disturbance composed of uncertain model parameters and time-varying environmental disturbance. Secondly, an auxiliary dynamic system is introduced to deal with the control input saturation constraints of the surface vessels. Thirdly, based on the dynamic surface control(DSC) technology, the state information of the adjacent surface vessels, the graph theory and the estimate value of the composite disturbance by the neuroadaptive estimator, a distributed state feedback controller for the MSVs under the input constraints is designed. In particular, a second-order linear tracking differentiator is introduced to solve the problem of noise sensitivity of a filter in the traditional DSC technology and to smooth the virtual control signal. Finally, through Lyapunov stability theory, it’s proved that closed-loop system is stable.

articleTitle: Output Formation Control for Heterogeneous Linear Multi-Agent Systems via Node-Based Adaptive Control Method
abstract: This paper studies the output formation control problem of heterogeneous linear leader-follower multi-agent systems(MASs) via node-based adaptive control method. By combing the leader and the relative position as an exosystem, the output formation control problem is converted to a standard output regulation problem. To estimate the state of leader, an adaptive observer is proposed, and a distributed state observer for each agent is also presented for practical consideration. Then based on output regulation technique, a node-based adaptive dynamic output feedback control protocol is devised. The adaptive strategy is constructed without using global information in this paper, which achieves fully distributed mode. Finally, a simulation result gives evidence of the availability of the presented control protocol.

articleTitle: Soft-Sensing Method of Effluent Ammonia Nitrogen Based on Emotional Neural Network
abstract: In the process of wastewater treatment process (WWTP), the concentration of effluent ammonia nitrogen is one of the important indexes to test whether the water quality reaches the standard. Soft sensing technology is a method which can use some easily measurable auxiliary variables to predict key variables online. In this paper, we designed a soft sensing model of effluent NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>-N based on radial basis emotional neural network (RBENN), and then a feature selection (FS) method of sticky binary particle swarm optimization (SBPSO) algorithm based on mutual information (MI) and symmetric uncertainty (SU) is proposed to obtain the appropriate feature variables while balancing correlation and redundancy, and then the network parameters are optimized by comprehensive learning particle swarm optimization (CLPSO) algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed method effectively improves the prediction performance of the model.

articleTitle: Impedance control based on the human gait data for lower limb rehabilitation robot
abstract: The lower limb rehabilitation robots (LLRR) have brought significant support to patients with movement disorders, and the research of LLRR has also become one hot topic in robotic fields. However, how to reduce the contact force between the rehabilitation robot and the human is becoming a challenge. Therefore, in order to make robots and humans form a most concerted whole, this paper designs a novel controller based on real human gait data. In detail, the Nokov motion capture system (NMCS) is used to collect human gait data, and then the collected data is fed to the designed control system as reference control signals. That is, the controller can simulate the interaction between the lower limbs of the human body and the environment to provide human-like abilities for the LLRR. To confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method, the simulation results based experimental date is given. The results show a satisfactory trajectory tracking effect, and the stability can be guaranteed.

articleTitle: An 8-bit Fixed Point Quantization Method for Sparse MobileNetV2
abstract: Sparse MobileNetV2 has potential for embedded image processing applications due to its low computation complexity. However, it uses 32-bit float point number system for computing and storage. As a result, its computing efficiency can be further improved. In this paper, an 8-bit fixed point quantization method for Sparse MobileNetV2 is proposed for model size reduction and computing operation simplification, which improves throughput and shrinks memory consumption. Firstly, quantization objects are confirmed by analyzing the computation pattern of Sparse MobileNetV2. Then, after the statistical analysis of the distribution characteristic of parameters, the 8-bit fixed point quantization method is applied. Experimental results of image classification on remote sensing image dataset show that the memory consumption is reduced to 18.7% and the throughput increases by l.6x, while there is only a slight accuracy loss.

articleTitle: Adversarial Attacks on Faster R-CNN: Design and Ablation Study
abstract: Most adversarial attack methods focus on image classifiers rather than the other more common models deployed in security-critical applications. This work focuses on the design of the attack on the object detection model, Faster Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Faster R-CNN). To this end, we first formulate adversarial attacks against Faster R-CNN as a multi-objective optimisation problem. Second, we apply Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) to solve the defined optimisation problem. In addition, we conduct an ablation study on the loss terms of the adversarial attacks’ objective function. Finally, the proposed attack is evaluated on the object detection task MSCOCO2017. Our experimental results show that attacking the Fast R-CNN submodule or attacking both Fast R-CNN and backbone network submodules leads to the best attack results at our widely selected evaluation metrics, and our best attack can reduce the detection accuracy mAP@[.5, .95] by 17.4%.

articleTitle: MonkeyPosekit: Automated Markerless 2D Pose Estimation of Monkey
abstract: Video-based bone recognition is becoming a crucial tool for both clinical and neuroscientific research of fine and complicated movements. But it is very time- consuming and there is lack of accuracy to extract specific aspects of behaviors, such as hand shaking and other fine motor skills, especially for automated analysis in non-human primate studies. The OpenMonkeyStudio as a 3D toolbox is available to estimate the pose of an unmarked monkey. However, there is still a lack of the 2D method, since most of laboratories are using a single front camera to obtain 2D videos due to financial constraints. Here, we build a bone- recognition auxiliary tool called MonkeyPosekit, which is based on deep learning for automatically capturing the stream information from 2D videos without the need for external hardware assistance. The MonkeyPosekit is able to identify the monkey’s activity space to track 13 bone joint points for the behavioral testing. Futhermore, we propose a novel approach of data augmentation called CageAUG to overcome the occlusion issues in this study. Equipped with the CageAUG augmentation, the accuracy has reached 98.8% in Open Monkey dataset by using the High-Resolution network.

articleTitle: Modeling, Simulation and Control of Close Formation Flight
abstract: In this paper, we focus on the aerodynamic characteristics of aircraft flying in tight formation. The formation model of a small unmanned aircraft is studied, and the disturbance of the wake induced velocity produced by the forward aircrafts on the tail aircraft is analyzed. It is found that the lead aircraft has a significant effect on uplift and drag on the trailing airplane. This has also demonstrated that the tail planes’ aerodynamic characteristics can be enhanced when the following plane is in the proper position of the leader in the tight formation flight. Precise position control of the tail plane in general flight operations is achieved under the influence of the tail vortex. First, the mathematical model of the leader's wake vortex was developed, and then two unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) were simulated using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) software to verify accuracy of this mathematical model. A control algorithm was designed to realize the stability of formation flight. Mathematical simulation and validation were performed. The designed control law is able to keep the tail plane in the appropriate position in the formation flight so that the tail plane is subjected to the maximum lift.

articleTitle: Optimal Trajectory Planning and Tracking for Autonomous Vehicles Considering Chassis Nonlinearities
abstract: This paper proposes a new type of local trajectory planning method for autonomous vehicles. In this frame, a lane-change or lane-keeping operation passed by the upper module is performed. Then, the trajectory planning algorithm can directly optimize the control sequences and obtain a feasible trajectory considering chassis nonlinearities and obstacles avoidance. A more accurate nonlinear model that considers the chassis’ nonlinearity based on the traditional linear bicycle model is realized using a cubic polynomial of slip angle to fit the magic formula. Constraint conditions are designed based on the traffic environment to avoid obstacles. With a more precise model, the control sequences can be used as feedforward control and accompany with fine feedback control to receive a good motion control performance even in a high-speed situation. Furthermore, different time-steps of the control variables are used to reduce the number of solving variables to decrease calculation time. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method and the accuracy of the proposed nonlinear vehicle model.

articleTitle: Region-adaptive Transfer Entropy for Multi-mode Fault Root Tracing of Industrial Processes
abstract: Transfer entropy (TE) is a powerful tool in calculating non-linear causal relationships. The estimations of TE are of high burden, which can be optimized by data compression. However, for multi-mode industrial processes, the compression may cause losses of details and faulty judgements because the threshold varies with modes. Therefore, we proposed an improved TE algorithm to preserve the details of data in various threshold ranges. Firstly, when a new mode is detected, the position of the breakpoints are adjusted accordingly. Then the region is divided by the breakpoints based on Gaussian distribution. The data are segmented by mean values and then converted into symbols. Finally, the TE result is estimated with symbolized sequence pair. Based on the data collected from the coal gasification process, a causal map was constructed with our method for fault root tracing. The tracing result was accord with the fact, which proves the reliability of TE in industrial process. The effectiveness of TE was further verified by comparisons with several other methods.

articleTitle: Attitude Control Of Spinning Projectile With Single Moving Mass
abstract: A single moving mass is used to realize the attitude control of the spinning projectile due to its advantages in maintaining a good aerodynamic configuration for the projectile, avoiding ablation of the rudder surfaces, and simplifying the control system structure, and so on. In this paper, a moving mass control system is designed with the pitch PID controller, yaw PID controller, and sinusoidal modulator, which generates the corresponding movement command of the moving mass with outputs of the pitch and yaw controllers based on a sinusoidal modulation mode. The moving mass follows the commands and moves along the radial direction on a straight rail fixed to the projectile. The desired periodic average maneuvering moment can be produced. Numerical simulation results demonstrate that it is feasible and effective to utilize a single moving mass for attitude control of spinning projectiles.

articleTitle: Improved high-order sliding mode control of feedback linearized PMSM for tram
abstract: The trolley driven by permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) is a typical multi-input-how much output complex drive system with strong coupling and nonlinear characteristics. Therefore, the PMSM nonlinear model is linearized by accurate feedback to optimize the motor control performance. Because the trolley track route is relatively fixed, the driving environment is mainly affected by load disturbance. Therefore, the stability of the system is guaranteed by the good anti-interference advantage of sliding mode variable structure control. Aiming at the high frequency chattering caused by the traditional sliding mode, an improved high order sliding mode control with compensation is designed, which can reduce the chattering effectively and accelerate the dynamic adaptive response process. The results of MATLAB simulation experiments show that the high-order sliding mode control system combined with different feedback linearization processing current and speed loop can track and stabilize the speed quickly, and effectively reduce the torque fluctuation, that is, meet the requirements of the actual engineering trolley operating system.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic despin mechanism design with halbach configuration and magnetic field analysis
abstract: In view of the fact that the failed spacecraft occupy the orbit resources gradually and rotate at high speed, the despin is the first step of deorbit operation. In this paper, microsatellite as the carrier, design a electromagnetic despin mechanism, which consists of permanent magnets and coils; Electromagnetic despin technology has the advantages of non-contacting control capability, no plume contamination and no consumption of fuel. The halbach configuration of permanent magnets are used to strengthen the magnetic field of the despin mechanism facing the side of failed spacecraft. The stable magnetic field is generated within a distance of 100mm-200mm, and can change the coil current to control the magnetic field. After that, establish the magnetic field model of despin mechanism, by comparing with the simulation results of ANSYS, the average error of the model is 5.25%, which shows a certain accuracy.

articleTitle: Civil Aircraft Auto Brake System Development Using Model-Based Systems Engineering
abstract: Civil aircraft auto brake system development based on Model-Based Systems Engineering(MBSE) technology is proposed in this paper. After requirements analysis, functional analysis and architecture synthesis three phases, use case model, function analysis model, tradeoff model and logical architecture of system are established in Rhapsody using Systems Modeling Language(SysML). Then a collaborative simulation mechanism combining Rhapsody/Simulink model is proposed to solve the defect that SysML can’t describe the continuous behavior of system. Collaborative simulation enables system designers to carry out comprehensive and timely verification of dynamic behavior and correctness of modeling by simulating the overall composition which greatly improves the efficiency and accuracy of development.

articleTitle: Memoryless Feedback Control of Stochastic Nonlinear Systems with Long Delays in the State and Input
abstract: This paper considers the problem of memoryless feedback control for a class of stochastic nonlinear systems with long delays in the state and input. It is shown that under the linear growth condition, the feedback domination approach together with Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional method, a linear and delay-free feedback controller is constructed to drive the stochastic time-delay system globally exponentially stable (GES) in mean square.

Author Keywords: long delays in the state and input
globally exponentially stable in mean square

articleTitle: Identify the Main Retinal Vessels using Vessel Structure Similarity Assessment
abstract: An algorithm based on vessels similarity is proposed to identify the eight main retinal vessels in retinal images. A similarity cost is proposed in this paper to measure the similarity between vessel structures based on tree edit distance and prior knowledge is add in the similarity assessment. The similarity cost is calculated between each vessel and the vessels in a reference image and each blood vessel in the test image is matched with the labeled vessel whose similarity cost is lowest. Experiment results show that the proposed method is effective for public database DRIVE as well as clinical data. This method is currently the first to identify the eight main vessels in retinal images automatically using the similarity matching of vessel structure.

Author Keywords: Eight types of blood vessel identification

articleTitle: Recursive-Gradient-Based Data-Driven Consensus Control for Multiagent Systems
abstract: The paper presents an improved recursive-gradient-based model-free adaptive control (IRGBMFAC) method which can increase the convergence rates of the loss function and improve the convergence performance of the system compared with the basic MFAC. Then IRGBMFAC is introduced into the consensus control of multi-agent systems. Due to the external environment, communication failure, data packet loss and other problems occur randomly, the communication topology of multiagent system may change inevitable. Here, the fixed topology and the switched topology are both considered. Finally, the effectiveness and feasibility of the IRGBMFAC have been demonstrated by the simulation examples.

articleTitle: Chebyshev neural network-based prescribed performance adaptive attitude tracking control for flexible spacecraft
abstract: A Chebyshev neural network-based prescribed performance adaptive attitude tracking control scheme is discussed for flexible spacecraft attitude tracking problems with external disturbances and unmodeled dynamics. The prescribed performance control method uses performance function and error transformation for limiting the tracking error to the prescribed constraint range to ensure the desired overshoot, convergence rate, and steady-state response. Chebyshev neural network is used to deal with the unknown disturbances caused by the external environment and flexible oscillations. When considering the unknown approximation error of the neural network, the upper bound of the approximation error is further estimated by an adaptive law. The numerical simulation results on flexible spacecraft show the effectiveness of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: FESO-Based Line-of-Sight Guidance Law for Path Following of Unmanned Surface Vehicles with Environmental Disturbances
abstract: This paper proposes a filter extended state observer (FESO) based integral line-of-sight (LOS) control law for unmanned surface vehicle path following control system. The filtered extended state observer is developed to observe the time-varying sideslip angle, which is caused by disturbances caused by the external environment. This ensures that the sideslip angle can be estimated in time and accurately so that the desired path can be accurately tracked without being disturbed by the external sea wind, waves, and current environment. In addition, the look-ahead distance is also different from the previous work, which is a time-varying distance determined by the cross-track error and the speed of the unmanned surface vehicle. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed theory is effective.

articleTitle: State estimation for a class of switched systems with impulsive effects and disturbances
abstract: The paper considers state estimation for switched systems, in which both nonlinear disturbances and impulsive effects are contained. By exploiting Bihari’s inequality technique, some stability criteria are established by designing average dwell time (ADT) switching law, which include some existing results as special cases. A representative example is also specified to testify the superiority of the approach.

articleTitle: Design of Environment Monitoring System Based on Loongson Processor
abstract: Combined with the demand of environmental monitoring work and the trend of autonomous and controllable equipment, a Loongson processor-based environment monitoring system is studied. Our system uses the domestic Loongson 1B processor as the main controller and RT-Thread as the operating system to collect temperature, humidity, rainfall, river water level, and other parameters in the environment through a variety of environmental sensors. The cloud server is used to store and monitor the environmental parameters sent by the terminal through the 4G LTE network. Remote clients access the cloud server in real-time and obtain environmental parameters through applications based on the Qt framework. Long-term test results show that the system runs stably, can monitor and store environmental parameters in real-time, and meets the requirements of autonomous and controllable environmental monitoring equipment.

articleTitle: Adversarial Learning-Based Automatic Evaluator for Image Captioning
abstract: Image captioning imitates the process of humans describing the visual world using natural language. Evaluating image captioning remains a challenging task. Current methods mainly focus on the similarity between the generated description and reference texts, despite the direct relevance of the caption and the corresponding image. In this paper, we propose an adversarial learning-based evaluator. The evaluator is designed on Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks and trained with Proximal Policy Optimization. Since it directly works on the relationship between images and descriptions, our model takes advantage of references of other similar images in the dataset. It gives more reliable judgment than state-of-the-art methods, taking variability of natural language into consideration for better evaluation.

articleTitle: Adaptive PI Control of Strict Feedback Systems with Full-State Constrains and Asymmetric Input Saturation
abstract: In this work, we propose a proportional-integral (PI) control strategy for strict-feedback systems subject to full-state constraints as well as input saturations, where input saturation is dealt with by a smooth approximatelion function, while the asymmetric full-state constraints are addressed through a nonlinear state-dependent transformation. It is shown that the proposed control strategy circumvents the feasibility conditions and bears the simple structure of PI control, which makes resultant control strategy robust, adaptive and fault- tolerant. Simulation validates the feasibility and performance of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Load Frequency Control for Multi-area Power Systems under Multi-rate Sampling Mechanism and Cyber-Attacks
abstract: The adaptive event-driven output feedback load frequency control with multi-area interconnected power system (MAIPS) output feedback under cyber attacks is studied in this paper. By introducing a multi-rate sampling mechanism (MRS mechanism), a novel adaptive event-driven transmission (EDT) scheme is proposed to effectively alleviate unnecessary signal transmission. Compared to some previous EDT schemes, the adaptive EDT presented in this paper can update the threshold in a timely way according to the system performance requirements. Combining the MRS mechanism and the EDT scheme, a trade-off between improving system performance and reducing network load can be found. Based on the above communication strategy, the influence of additive deception attacks at the network layer on system performance is also considered. Using the loop-function method, sufficient conditions for the output feedback LFC controller to guarantee the stability of the LFC system under the given H∞ performance index are obtained. Finally, the simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed LFC strategy.

articleTitle: Broad learning system based on Elastic Net feature sparsity and dense
abstract: Broad learning has attracted wide attention since it was proposed, because of its characteristics of short training time and online updating. However, there are many problems in the original broad learning, such as low prediction accuracy, large computational consumption of resources, and many redundant data in the calculation process. Therefore, this paper proposes a broad improvement method based on dense connection of feature layers and using Elastic Net to sparse feature layers. The different Windows of the feature layer of the original broad learning system were put into the form of dense connection, and then Elastic Net was introduced to sparse the feature nodes, and then the sparse feature nodes were combined with the input data as the input of the enhancement layer nodes, making the model more compact. The proposed method was applied to a public dataset to verily the results. The experimental results show that the proposed method has short training time and higher accuracy than other methods.

articleTitle: TDNCIB: Target-Driven Navigation with Convolutional Information Branch Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Target-driven navigation has been a significant application field of reinforcement learning. However, sparse reward and lack of useful environment information are still existing problems. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a novel design to the target-driven visual navigation based on deep reinforcement learning: Target-Driven Navigation with Convolutional Information Branch (TDNCIB), which enriches the high-dimensional information learned by the network from the environment. It is an improvement of A2C algorithm. CIB can help make full use of environmental information and serve as a complement to the baseline. Besides, a novel reward design using similarity is introduced to relieve sparse reward. The ablation study is implemented in 4 different scenes of AI2-THOR framework comparing the baseline and our TDNCIB. According to our evaluation, TDNCIB converges faster than the baseline and achieves better performance in 5 common metrics with shorter trajectory length, less collision and higher success rate.

articleTitle: An Integrated Method for Optimizing Train Speed Profile in Case of Entering Station Conflict
abstract: Punctuality is always one of the goals of high speed railway. At the same time, train delay caused by a variety of reasons is also unavoidable. It is necessary to study a method to alleviate train delay. This paper proposes a two-step train operation adjustment method based on integrating the opening management of home signal to alleviate the typical train delay caused by entering station conflict. Find the adjustment point by minimizing the running time for entering station in the first step, and optimize the speed profile to the adjustment point by an improved Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) in the second step. Through analysis and simulation, the effectiveness and availability of the proposed method is verified. In the simulation scenario, the delay time is reduced by more than 30s.

articleTitle: Memory PDSF controller design for discrete-time uncertain switched singular time-delay systems
abstract: This work is concerned with the design problem of memory proportional-derivative state feedback (PDSF) controllers for uncertain discrete-time switched singular time-delay systems based on fully considering the effects of uncertainties, time-delay and state jumps. The design method of controller gains is given by introducing appropriate free-weighting matrices to deal with the coupling relationship of variables. Sufficient conditions are derived to ensure the closed-loop systems normal and stable (NS) by adopting memory PDSF controllers and state-dependet switching laws. On the basis of the above results, based on memoryless PDSF controllers, a sufficient condition is given to ensure the closed-loop systems NS. Finally, we give an example to show the advantages of the proposed results.

articleTitle: Bifurcations control of IS-LM macroeconomic system via PD controller
abstract: In this paper, the problem of bifurcation control for an Investment-Saving Liquidity Preference-Money Supply (IS-LM) macroeconomic system with time delays is studied. In order to avoid macro-control instability caused by Hopf bifurcation, a proportional differential (PD) feedback scheme is proposed to improve the stability of the system and prevent Hopf bifurcation. Time delay is an important parameter for Hopf bifurcation. By selecting different time delays, the stability of the controlled economic system and the conditions for Hopf bifurcation are obtained. It is found that bifurcation dynamics of the IS-LM macroeconomic system can be optimized by reasonably adjusting the parameters of PD controller. Finally, the effectiveness of the PD controller is verified by numerical simulation, and the relationship between the Hopf bifurcation point and the controller parameters is obtained.

articleTitle: Synchronization of Multi-Weighted and Directed Complex Networks With Intermittent Control
abstract: We mainly investigate the control of multi-weighted and directed complex dynamical networks (MWCDNs) with periodically intermittent pinning control (PIC). If the Chebyshev distance between selected normalized vectors (SNVecs) of the coupling matrices, which can be used to prove matrices are Lyapunov stable, is less than the allowable deviation control bound (ADCB), then we can combine these SNVecs together to design suitable Lyapunov functions and prove the global synchronization. We also consider adaptive rules to synchronize MWCDNs. In the end, simulations are given.

articleTitle: Persistent Execution of Continuous Time Multi-Robot Pathfinding
abstract: Many one-shot Multi-Robot Path Finding (MRPF) algorithms have been able to find collision-free paths for hundreds or even thousands of robots moving to their respective goal positions in dense scenarios, and some persistent execution frameworks are able to drive MRPF persistently. However, these frameworks have great limitations in practical applications, which are based on discrete time and grids. In this paper, we present a persistent execution framework independent of MRPF solvers, which can not only operate in discrete time and grids, but also solve the MRPF problem based on roadmap in continuous time. Our presented prediction replanning method is at the core of the framework driving the operation of the MRPF algorithm in the case of persistent tasks, and it also deals with the impact of algorithm computation time and message transmission delay of the multi-robot system. We also presented a dynamic map addition method to solve the problem that replanning cannot be performed when robot is not on map vertex during the runtime. We evaluate our framework using Continuous-time conflict-based search (CCBS) as the MRPF solver and the results show that it can efficiently drive the MRPF algorithm to run under continuous-time persistent task situations.

articleTitle: A Korean sentence similarity calculation method based on sub-word level information
abstract: Sentence similarity is the key technology in text summary and machine translation.
